# Modular graph engine, Phase B3a: real ports and the script-node runtime - implementation plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or
> superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for
> tracking.

**Goal:** the DSP kernel's input and output become wires the planner can see (four host I/O nodes, four inputs on
every system node, the Game Boy's `serialOut` on a feedback wire, `rp.n8.cart-mirror`), the kernel runs unchanged
as one TS script node, `rp.dsp.kernel`, in a script host every Engine has, its structure travels as that node's
settings, and the sealed kernel (`DspRuntime`, the kernel stage's fan-out, the native kernel node and the
`dspSetSystems` / `dspLoadKernel` / `compileScript` RPCs) is deleted, bit-identical to the parity baseline, which
first gains 1-frame and FL-style ragged blocks.

**Architecture:** Per [docs/modular-graph-phase-b3a-design.md](modular-graph-phase-b3a-design.md). The ABI gains
a fourth prepare result, `RP_PREPARE_RESHAPE` (an instance kept across a layout change, its ports rebound by id,
its new settings committed at the swap), a type flag, `RP_TYPE_STATELESS_PREPARE` (`setGraph` never waits for
such a type's commits), queue capacities in port descriptors with drops counted to the host, and a type context on
the type-level calls. Natively, every system node takes `serialIn` / `midi` / `bytes` / `buttons`, the Game Boy
writes `serialOut`, and `rp.host.midi-in` / `midi-out` / `controller-in` / `controller-out` and
`rp.n8.cart-mirror` move what the hosts stage and drain. A `ScriptHost` per Engine runs TS nodes behind the C ABI:
an audio-side bare QuickJS runtime holding every instance, a control-side one answering `layout_for` and
`prepare_settings`, both loaded at construction with a bundle compiled to bytecode at build time. The kernel node
wraps the unchanged `DspKernel`; `buildGraph` wires it between the host I/O nodes and the systems, and the stores
publish its structure as its settings. A bench then times it against the old kernel stage, and the old path goes.

**Tech stack:** C++20 (CMake), Catch2, bare QuickJS (the in-tree `tjsc` for bytecode), TypeScript on txiki
(`pnpm test` mock tier, `pnpm test:native` real host), the graph layer of Phases A, B1 and B2.

**Provenance:** every code block below was built and run before this plan was written, on the scratch branch
`proto/b3a` in this worktree, on top of the design commit 625028cb: thirteen commits for ten tasks (two each for
Tasks 1, 9 and 10; Task 11 is the acceptance run and commits nothing), with GCC 13.3 on linux-x64. A code block that
creates a file is that file as the prototype commit left it; one that changes files is the prototype's diff for
them, so `git apply` it from the step's text (or apply it hunk by hunk with the Edit tool). Two files a command
writes are not shown: the parity baselines Task 1 records, and the `buildGraph` goldens Task 7 re-records. The two
one-off scripts that re-record and check those goldens were never committed; they are quoted from the prototype's
scratch directory, and running them over the pre-flip goldens reproduces the committed file byte for byte (checked
when this plan was generated). Every expected pass, test count and benchmark figure is what the prototype's runs
printed. Where a failing-test step quotes the prototype's first run, it says so (most were runs against stubs of the
missing code); otherwise the expected failure is what the missing code produces (a header or module that does not
exist, a member that does not exist). When this plan was generated it was replayed in a scratch clone of 625028cb,
every block written or applied in order: each commit's tree came out exactly as the prototype's, the graph-test
states the red and green steps of Tasks 2, 3 and 5 describe were rebuilt and run (a count quoted "when this plan was
checked" is from those runs), and the engine-graph tests of Tasks 4 and 6 compiled at their red states.

**Where this plan departs from the design.** The design as committed (625028cb) was written before the prototype,
and building it changed some of what it says; the plan follows what was built, and Task 10's docs commit lands the
amended design. The ABI's type-level calls (`descriptor`, `layout_for`, `query_memory`, `create`) had no context,
so one host could not serve several script types through one set of functions: they now take the `rp_node_type`
they are called through, which gains `flags` and a trailing `ctx` (Tasks 2 and 5; design section 2.2 did not
foresee it). `setGraph`'s wait for the last settings commit, which B1 never exercised and every B3a structure edit
would hit, now applies only to commits to a type without `RP_TYPE_STATELESS_PREPARE`, a type flag every script
type sets, so consecutive kernel commits queue on the command ring (Task 2). A reshape rebinds ports by stable port
id, not name, and the planner asks `prepare_settings` about every settings change, a layout change included (a
reshape with the layout unchanged is a swap; a swap for a changed layout is a `node-contract` error), with what an
instance holds per port in a per-layout `PortState` (Task 2). The system node inputs are applied once, at the top
of `prepare`, for every system, not in `process` (Task 4). Section 3.4 named only the Arduinoboy protocol as the
kernel's out-of-order sender; MI.MAP sends out of frame order too (a row byte at its note's frame, then 0xFF clocks
at frame 0), and like Arduinoboy it reaches only SameBoy's front-release serial queue, so Task 6's equivalence test
applies the queue's clamp to the old side and parity holds. The script kernel carries a transitional id,
`rp.dsp.kernel-script`, until the flip retires the native node and gives it `rp.dsp.kernel` (Tasks 6 and 7). The
bench (Task 8) comes before the deletion (Task 9), since it times the kernel node against the old kernel stage, and
the deletion first moves the old runtime's profiling onto the script host; `compileScript` goes with the other two
RPCs (no caller remains, while `ScriptCompiler` stays for the tests), and staging host MIDI becomes
allocation-free. Building it also found a defect: LSDj master sync in small blocks reads a stopped LSDj's idle
flood as clocks; Task 1 pins it in the new groups (B0's eighth defect), to be fixed on its own after B3a. The kernel
node's settings refuse two systems with one id, which the old kernel took silently.

**Ground rules for whoever executes this:**
- Commit after each task (the commit commands are given; Tasks 1, 9 and 10 commit twice). No `Co-Authored-By` or
  "generated with" trailer.
- Do not push, and do not open a PR.
- Never use an emdash character in code, comments, docs or commit messages; use " - ", ":" or ";". Some diffs below
  carry emdashes on lines the prototype did not write (context and removed lines of older code): leave those be.
- Run every command from the worktree root with absolute paths or a subshell (`(cd x && ...)`); never `cd` the
  session itself.
- Don't `rm -rf build` to fix CMake; investigate. Never use bare `git stash`, and never switch branches with
  uncommitted work in the tree. A new or removed CMake source needs a reconfigure first: `cmake -S . -B build`.
- `deps/sameboy` shows as modified after any configure. That is the tracked audio patch: expected, leave it.
- The derived bundle C arrays (`build/native/*bundle_data.c`, the new `script-bundle_data.c` and
  `script-test-bundle_data.c` among them) are never committed.
- The parity baseline is recorded only in Task 1: four new groups, recorded on the engine as it is before any B3a
  code, whose master-sync cases pin a defect on purpose. Do not fix it here; it is its own change after B3a. Every
  later task leaves every baseline passing unchanged, and a parity failure is a real change to the audio: stop and
  find it. A recording happens only on the baseline's target, `linux-x64-gnu13` (this devcontainer).
- The fixture groups need `RETROPLUG_RESOURCES_DIR=/workspaces/resources`; without it their cases skip. Pass it on
  the same command line: a shell `export` does not survive between commands.
- `node packages/retroplug/scripts/run-native-tests.mjs` (what `pnpm test:native` runs) takes ONE filter: an exact
  slug (`parity/blocks-tiny-lsdj`) or a prefix in the dash form (`parity-blocks-tiny` runs the four blocks-tiny
  groups; `parity/blocks-tiny` matches nothing). Run several files as separate commands, or the whole suite.
- While a Reaper check runs it uses `build/bin`: do not rebuild the plugin until it finishes. Run the Reaper checks
  one at a time, and before each make sure no Reaper or jackd of an earlier run is left (`pgrep -a reaper;
  pgrep -a jackd`).
- `pnpm check:docs` counts the tracked docs: 54 in the prototype, which had no plan file, so one more once this plan
  is committed.

### Task 1: Tiny host blocks in parity, recorded on today's engine

Before any B3a code exists, pin the block sizes parity has never run (design sections 6 and 7.1): 1-frame blocks,
and the ragged splits FL Studio hands a plugin, in three partitions: `1`, `fl` (the repeating list
`[33, 1, 222, 1, 7, 4096, 2]`) and `fl256` (a 256-frame buffer split inside at automation points,
`[256, 33, 1, 222, 255, 1, 1, 255, 7, 249]`). MIDI, automation CCs and transport points land on block edges: a
block's first frame, its last, and a 1-frame block's only frame. Four groups: `blocks-tiny-mgb` and
`blocks-tiny-nes` (mGB and BlipToaster at 44.1 and 48 kHz, fixture-free, so CI runs them), `blocks-tiny-lsdj` (LSDj
MIDI sync, Arduinoboy and MI.OUT at 48 kHz) and `blocks-tiny-risa` (risa host sync), both fixture-only. `risa()`
and `RISA_BOOT_MS` move from `risa.test.ts` into `scenes.ts` so the new group can share them.

The second commit adds LSDj master sync in the same splits at both rates, with a defect pinned as it is (B0's
eighth): the decoder calls a block holding more than 16 serial-out bytes a stopped LSDj's idle flood, which depends
on the block's length, so in small blocks a stopped LSDj decodes as clocks (10497 MIDI messages in 1-frame blocks
against 101 in 1024-frame ones). It is fixed after B3a, on its own, with a deliberate re-record.

- [ ] **Step 2: The splits and the mGB / NES cases**

Create `packages/retroplug/test-native/parity/blocks-tiny.ts`:

````ts
// Host blocks the rest of the matrix never runs: 1-frame blocks, and the ragged splits FL Studio hands a
// plugin. FL splits a host buffer at every automation and tempo point, so one buffer can arrive as blocks of
// 256, 33 or 1 frame, and an event's frame is an offset inside the block it lands in. Recorded on the engine
// before B3a moved the kernel's I/O onto wires (docs/modular-graph-phase-b3a-design.md sections 6 and 7.1),
// so B3a is held to it bit for bit. A case renders all of itself, boot included, in one TINY_SPLITS entry,
// and places its MIDI, its automation CCs and its transport points on block edges: a block's first frame,
// its last, and a 1-frame block's only frame, which is both.
//
// The mgb and nes cases are here (blocks-tiny-mgb.test.ts, blocks-tiny-nes.test.ts); the scenes whose timing
// is a sync protocol, which need the sibling fixtures, are blocks-tiny-lsdj.test.ts and blocks-tiny-risa.test.ts.
import type { ParityCase } from "./group";
import { cycle, even, type Segment } from "./rig";
import { BOOT_MS, frames, mgb, MGB_CHANNELS, NES_CHANNELS, phrase, ROMS, type Blocks } from "./scenes";

/** The design's ragged list (section 7.1). No buffer grid at all: 1-frame blocks between odd sizes, and a
 *  4096-frame block next to a 2-frame one, the largest swing in size from one block to the next, which is
 *  what a core's per-block run-ahead and MI.OUT's one-block latency move with. It sums to 4362 frames, a
 *  multiple of neither a 24-PPQN tick nor a console frame, so its edges drift against both from one cycle to
 *  the next rather than meeting them at one phase. */
export const FL_RAGGED = [33, 1, 222, 1, 7, 4096, 2];

/** FL's own shape: a fixed 256-frame buffer, split inside at automation points and never across one, as five
 *  buffers [256] [33 1 222] [255 1] [1 255] [7 249]. So the edges keep a 256-frame grid, and a buffer's last
 *  frame and the next buffer's first frame are each a 1-frame block, back to back. */
export const FL_BUFFER = [256, 33, 1, 222, 255, 1, 1, 255, 7, 249];

/** Every tiny-block partition, by name (the case-name suffix). Each segment's list starts its cycle afresh,
 *  so a segment's frame 0 is the first frame of a 33-frame block (`fl`) or of a 256-frame one (`fl256`). */
export const TINY_SPLITS: [string, Blocks][] = [
  ["1", (n) => even(n, 1)],
  ["fl", (n) => cycle(n, FL_RAGGED)],
  ["fl256", (n) => cycle(n, FL_BUFFER)],
];

/** Block kinds `Edges.next` looks for, by size. */
export const ONE = (n: number): boolean => n === 1;
export const SMALL = (n: number): boolean => n >= 2 && n <= 7;
export const BUFFER = (n: number): boolean => n >= 200 && n < 1024;
export const BIG = (n: number): boolean => n >= 1024;
export const ANY = (): boolean => true;

/** One segment's block list, and where its blocks' edges are. */
export class Edges {
  private readonly starts: number[] = [];

  constructor(readonly blocks: number[]) {
    let at = 0;
    for (const n of blocks) {
      this.starts.push(at);
      at += n;
    }
  }

  /** The index of the first block starting at or after frame `from` whose size passes `kinds[0]`; if no such
   *  block exists, the first passing `kinds[1]`, and so on. So `next(f, BIG, BUFFER, ANY)` is a 4096 block in
   *  `fl`, a buffer-sized one in `fl256` (it has no big block) and just the next block in `1`. */
  next(from: number, ...kinds: ((size: number) => boolean)[]): number {
    for (const kind of kinds) {
      const i = this.starts.findIndex((s, b) => s >= from && kind(this.blocks[b]));
      if (i >= 0) return i;
    }
    throw new Error(`no block of the kinds asked for starts at or after frame ${from}`);
  }

  /** Block `i`'s first frame, in segment frames. */
  first(i: number): number {
    if (i >= this.blocks.length) throw new Error(`block ${i} is past the segment's ${this.blocks.length} blocks`);
    return this.starts[i];
  }

  /** Block `i`'s last frame (its first, for a 1-frame block). */
  last(i: number): number {
    return this.first(i) + this.blocks[i] - 1;
  }

  /** The first frame of the first 1-frame block at or after frame `from`. */
  oneFrameAt(from: number): number {
    return this.first(this.next(from, ONE));
  }
}

export type TinySystem = "mgb" | "nes";

/** The automation CC each system's edge segment moves, on its two pulse voices (channels 0 and 1), with the
 *  three values it sets: mGB's pan (CC10: 0 left, 127 right, 64 both), BlipToaster's volume (CC7). Both
 *  also take CC1 (duty) on those voices, which the ramp moves. */
const AUTOMATION: Record<TinySystem, { cc: number; values: [number, number, number] }> = {
  mgb: { cc: 10, values: [0, 127, 64] },
  nes: { cc: 7, values: [127, 40, 80] },
};

/** CC1 values for the ramp: up through the four duties and back, so neighbours always differ. */
const DUTY_RAMP = [0, 40, 80, 120, 80, 40, 0, 120];

/** 700 ms of notes and automation CCs on block edges, each event at the next block of a kind after a point in
 *  the segment (in the 1-frame split every block is of every kind, so each lands on the next frame):
 *  - a note and an automation CC in a 1-frame block, the note first, as the plugin stages a tie (the host's
 *    events, then each moved parameter's CC at frame 0);
 *  - automation at a big block's frame 0, and a note-on on its last frame (a buffer-sized block in `fl256`;
 *    in `1` the same frame, so the CC comes first there);
 *  - an automation ramp, a CC at frame 0 of each of up to 32 consecutive blocks, which is what a host that
 *    splits at every automation point delivers (in `1`, a CC on each of 32 frames in a row);
 *  - a CC in a 1-frame block, and a note-off on the next block's first frame;
 *  - automation at a small block's first frame (2 to 7 frames), a note-off on its last;
 *  - a note-on in a 1-frame block, its note-off on the last frame of the next buffer-sized block;
 *  - a roll on the noise voice (channel 3): a note at the first frame of the next block every 1.5 ms.
 *  Each of them is heard: removing any one changes the case's digest. Moving one by a frame mostly is not:
 *  mGB takes a lone message at its own pace, and a lone note-on moved by a frame changes BlipToaster's output
 *  only once every ~67 frames at 48 kHz. In the 1-frame split a frame is what one block of latency moves an
 *  event by, so the ramp and the roll are dense on purpose, and mGB hears the segment moved: every event of it
 *  moved by one frame, either way, changes its digest. BlipToaster does not, so on its path a block of latency
 *  is pinned by the ragged splits, where most blocks are far longer than a frame. */
function edgeSegment(sr: number, split: Blocks, system: TinySystem): Segment {
  const e = new Edges(split(frames(sr, 700)));
  const ms = (t: number) => frames(sr, t);
  const { cc, values } = AUTOMATION[system];
  const midi: { at: number; bytes: number[] }[] = [];
  const at = (frame: number, ...messages: number[][]) => messages.forEach((bytes) => midi.push({ at: frame, bytes }));

  const one = e.next(ms(20), ONE);
  at(e.first(one), [0x90, 64, 100], [0xb0, cc, values[0]]);

  const big = e.next(ms(120), BIG, BUFFER, ANY);
  at(e.first(big), [0xb0, cc, values[1]]);
  at(e.last(big), [0x91, 71, 100]);

  const ramp = e.next(ms(200), ANY);
  for (let i = 0; i < 32 && e.first(ramp + i) < ms(280); i++) at(e.first(ramp + i), [0xb0, 1, DUTY_RAMP[i % DUTY_RAMP.length]]);

  const lone = e.next(ms(300), ONE);
  at(e.first(lone), [0xb1, 1, 96]);
  at(e.first(lone + 1), [0x80, 64, 0]);

  const small = e.next(ms(380), SMALL, ANY);
  at(e.first(small), [0xb1, cc, values[2]]);
  at(e.last(small), [0x81, 71, 0]);

  const last = e.next(ms(450), ONE);
  at(e.first(last), [0x90, 69, 90]);
  at(e.last(e.next(e.first(last) + 1, BUFFER, ANY)), [0x80, 69, 0]);

  let prev = -1;
  for (let t = 520, k = 0; t < 620; t += 1.5, k++) {
    const b = e.next(ms(t), ANY);
    if (b === prev) continue;
    prev = b;
    at(e.first(b), [0x93, k % 2 ? 52 : 40, 100]);
  }
  at(e.first(e.next(ms(640), ANY)), [0x83, 40, 0], [0x83, 52, 0]);

  return { blocks: e.blocks, midi };
}

function tinyCase(system: TinySystem, sr: number, split: string, blocks: Blocks): ParityCase {
  return {
    name: `${system}-${sr}-${split}`,
    sampleRate: sr,
    outputs: 2,
    audible: [0, 1],
    setup: system === "mgb" ? (rig) => void mgb(rig) : (rig) => void rig.add(ROMS.bliptoaster),
    segments: [
      { blocks: blocks(frames(sr, BOOT_MS)) },
      { blocks: blocks(frames(sr, 600)), midi: phrase(sr, system === "mgb" ? MGB_CHANNELS : NES_CHANNELS) },
      edgeSegment(sr, blocks, system),
    ],
  };
}

export function tinyCases(system: TinySystem): ParityCase[] {
  return [44100, 48000].flatMap((sr) => TINY_SPLITS.map(([split, blocks]) => tinyCase(system, sr, split, blocks)));
}
````

Create `packages/retroplug/test-native/parity/blocks-tiny-lsdj.test.ts`:

````ts
// LSDj's host-sync protocols in 1-frame blocks and FL-style ragged splits (blocks-tiny.ts has the lists, lsdj.ts
// the scenes): SYNC=MIDI following the host clock, each tick at its own frame; the Arduinoboy protocol, its
// clocks at a block's frame 0, its play / stop notes, 0xFA and 0xFC on the transport's edges; and MI.OUT,
// LSDj's serial out decoded into host MIDI out a block later, so the recorded block indices pin that one-block
// latency at every block size here. Tempo and transport points after a segment's start sit on 1-frame blocks,
// where FL puts them (it splits a buffer at each one), and the sync notes on block edges. Needs the sibling LSDj
// ROMs, so these skip in CI.
import { runGroup, type ParityCase } from "./group";
import { ANY, BUFFER, Edges, TINY_SPLITS } from "./blocks-tiny";
import { denseSongSav, lsdj, lsdjCase, midiOutSav, SR, tap } from "./lsdj";
import { frames, ROMS, type Blocks } from "./scenes";

/** lsdj-sync's midiSync-div1 (START, then the transport), with a tempo change a second in and the stop 50 ms
 *  into the last segment. */
function midiSync(split: string, blocks: Blocks): ParityCase {
  const play = new Edges(blocks(frames(SR, 2000)));
  const stop = new Edges(blocks(frames(SR, 500)));
  return lsdjCase(
    `midiSync-${split}`,
    ROMS.lsdj,
    (rig) => lsdj(rig, ROMS.lsdj, denseSongSav("Midi"), { mode: "midiSync", tempoDivisor: 1 }),
    [
      ...tap(0, SR, blocks),
      { blocks: play.blocks, transport: [{ at: 0, bpm: 120, ppq: 0, playing: true }, { at: play.oneFrameAt(frames(SR, 1000)), bpm: 140 }] },
      { blocks: stop.blocks, transport: [{ at: stop.oneFrameAt(frames(SR, 50)), playing: false }] },
    ],
    2,
    [0, 1],
    SR,
    blocks,
  );
}

/** lsdj-sync's Arduinoboy scene: the transport starts, note 24 (play) arrives in a 1-frame block, then note 25
 *  (stop) on a buffer-sized block's last frame, which ends the clocks, and 200 ms later the transport stop on
 *  a 1-frame block.
 *
 *  KNOWN DEFECT, recorded as it is (lsdj-sync.test.ts, design section 2.5 of modular-graph-phase-b0-design.md):
 *  Arduinoboy MIDI sync plays only under some partitions. In 1-frame blocks, and in `fl256` (no block over 256
 *  frames), it never starts, as at 128 to 768 frames, so those cases pin the silence and the work RAM the
 *  protocol's bytes leave. `fl` plays: at 120 bpm a tick is 1000 frames, so its 4096-frame block carries about
 *  four and its six other blocks almost none, and "every block carries a tick" is not the condition. */
function arduinoboy(split: string, blocks: Blocks): ParityCase {
  const run = new Edges(blocks(frames(SR, 2000)));
  const end = new Edges(blocks(frames(SR, 500)));
  const stopNote = end.last(end.next(frames(SR, 100), BUFFER, ANY));
  const stop = end.oneFrameAt(stopNote + frames(SR, 200));
  return lsdjCase(
    `midiSyncArduinoboy-${split}`,
    ROMS.arduinoboy,
    (rig) => lsdj(rig, ROMS.arduinoboy, denseSongSav("Lsdj"), { mode: "midiSyncArduinoboy", tempoDivisor: 1 }),
    [
      { blocks: blocks(frames(SR, 1000)), transport: [{ at: 0, bpm: 120, ppq: 0, playing: true }] },
      { blocks: run.blocks, midi: [{ at: run.oneFrameAt(0), bytes: [0x90, 24, 100] }] },
      {
        blocks: end.blocks,
        midi: [{ at: stopNote, bytes: [0x90, 25, 100] }],
        transport: [{ at: stop, playing: false }],
      },
    ],
    2,
    split === "fl" ? [0, 1] : [], // `1` and `fl256`: silent, the defect above
    SR,
    blocks,
  );
}

/** lsdj-modes' midiOut scene (play, stop, play, each by a START tap), the last run shortened to a second.
 *  KNOWN DEFECT, recorded as it is (lsdj-modes.test.ts): what MI.OUT decodes depends on the host sample rate and
 *  matches none of the song's N values, so this pins what is captured today, at 48 kHz. */
function midiOut(split: string, blocks: Blocks): ParityCase {
  return lsdjCase(
    `midiOut-${split}`,
    ROMS.arduinoboy,
    (rig) => lsdj(rig, ROMS.arduinoboy, midiOutSav(), { mode: "midiOut" }),
    [
      ...tap(0, SR, blocks),
      { blocks: blocks(frames(SR, 2000)) },
      ...tap(0, SR, blocks),
      { blocks: blocks(frames(SR, 400)) },
      ...tap(0, SR, blocks),
      { blocks: blocks(frames(SR, 1000)) },
    ],
    2,
    [0, 1],
    SR,
    blocks,
  );
}

const cases: ParityCase[] = [midiSync, arduinoboy, midiOut].flatMap((scene) => TINY_SPLITS.map(([split, blocks]) => scene(split, blocks)));

runGroup("blocks-tiny-lsdj", cases);
````

Create `packages/retroplug/test-native/parity/blocks-tiny-risa.test.ts`:

````ts
// risa host sync in 1-frame blocks and FL-style ragged splits (blocks-tiny.ts has the lists): risa.test.ts's
// transport script (start, a tempo change, stop, a loop wrap's locate) with every point after a segment's start
// on a 1-frame block, where FL puts it: it splits a buffer at each tempo point and at the loop end, so the block
// after a wrap starts with the locate. The risa-sync role clocks risa at each tick's own frame, so its clocks
// land on block edges throughout, and the arm it sends on a locate flushes the FIFO. Mesen's audio is
// partition-invariant (blocks.ts), so these lanes pin the bytes the role sent and when, not the partition.
// Needs the sibling risa fixtures, so these skip in CI.
import { runGroup, type ParityCase } from "./group";
import { Edges, TINY_SPLITS } from "./blocks-tiny";
import { frames, risa, RISA_BOOT_MS, ROMS, type Blocks } from "./scenes";

const SR = 48000;

function transport(split: string, blocks: Blocks): ParityCase {
  const play = new Edges(blocks(frames(SR, 1500)));
  const stop = new Edges(blocks(frames(SR, 500)));
  const wrap = new Edges(blocks(frames(SR, 1500)));
  return {
    name: `transport-${split}`,
    needs: [ROMS.risa, ROMS.risaSong],
    sampleRate: SR,
    outputs: 2,
    audible: [0, 1],
    setup: (rig) => void risa(rig),
    segments: [
      { blocks: blocks(frames(SR, RISA_BOOT_MS)) },
      { blocks: play.blocks, transport: [{ at: 0, bpm: 120, ppq: 0, playing: true }, { at: play.oneFrameAt(frames(SR, 900)), bpm: 140 }] },
      { blocks: stop.blocks, transport: [{ at: stop.oneFrameAt(0), playing: false }] },
      // Playing again from ppq 4, then the wrap: a locate back to the loop start on a 1-frame block.
      { blocks: wrap.blocks, transport: [{ at: 0, ppq: 4, playing: true }, { at: wrap.oneFrameAt(300), ppq: 0 }] },
    ],
  };
}

runGroup(
  "blocks-tiny-risa",
  TINY_SPLITS.map(([split, blocks]) => transport(split, blocks)),
);
````

---

### Task 2: Reshape

A node may keep its instance across a settings change that alters its layout (design section 2.4). The kernel
needs it: its ports are per system, and its state (each system's tick counter and role scratch, the project
stages') must survive a system being added, which a rebuild could not carry, since the new instance is created on
the control thread while the old one still runs on the audio thread.

`prepare_settings` gains `RP_PREPARE_RESHAPE`: keep this instance, with the layout `layout_for` gives the new
settings. The planner asks the live instance about every settings change, a layout change included (only the
instance knows whether it can keep up); a reshape that keeps the layout is a swap, and a swap for a changed layout
is a `node-contract` error. What an instance holds per port and param (its layout, param and control-output
streams, resource-output slots, and the control side's applied / wired / mask records) moves into a per-layout
`PortState`: a reshape builds a new one on the control thread while the running plan still uses the old, sharing
into it by id every stream and slot that persists (a param whose id, type, range and enum labels match; an output
whose id, kind and resource type match), and each plan holds the `PortState`s it was built with, so nothing the
audio thread reads is written or freed while the next plan is planned. The prepared settings commit at adoption
through the existing path, a `ports_changed` always follows a layout-changing reshape (after its
`commit_settings`), and a feedback wire to or from the node keeps its front.

`rp_node_type` gains `flags`, with `RP_TYPE_STATELESS_PREPARE`: `setGraph`'s adoption wait now counts only plans
that commit to a type without it (`PlanStorage::awaitsAdoption`), so a host that stops calling `process` while
the plugin stays active (DPF's CLAP `stop_processing` does nothing) no longer holds every such edit for the 2 s
timeout and then refuses it. The C++ layer takes `static constexpr bool reshapes` and `stateless_prepare`; a
`static_assert` refuses the second beside `needs_rebuild`, which reads the current settings. The toy node is
`rp.test.shape`, whose ports and params are named by its settings.

**Files:**
- Create: `packages/native/test/graph/Reshape.test.cpp`
- Modify: `packages/native/cmake/tests.cmake`, `packages/native/src/graph/GraphHost.cpp`, `packages/native/src/graph/GraphHost.hpp`, `packages/native/src/graph/PlanStorage.hpp`, `packages/native/src/graph/Planner.cpp`, `packages/native/src/graph/Planner.hpp`, `packages/native/src/graph/node.hpp`, `packages/native/src/graph/rp_node.h`, `packages/native/test/graph/NoAlloc.test.cpp`, `packages/native/test/graph/NodeLayer.test.cpp`, `packages/native/test/graph/Planner.test.cpp`, `packages/native/test/graph/Registry.test.cpp`, `packages/native/test/graph/SwapStress.test.cpp`, `packages/native/test/graph/TestNodes.hpp`

````diff
+// Ports and params named by its settings, so a settings change can alter its layout, and it keeps its
+// instance through one (it reshapes); its prepare reads nothing but the new settings (stateless). Each block
+// it pushes [0x90, the port's first letter, blocks] on every events output, records each input's message
+// count and each knob's value by the port's first letter, and on its first block sets every level to 5.
+// `blocks` is the state a rebuild would lose. Allocates nothing on the audio thread.
+struct ShapeSettings {
+    std::vector<std::string> ins;     // events inputs
+    std::vector<std::string> outs;    // events outputs
+    std::vector<std::string> levels;  // control outputs
+    std::vector<std::string> knobs;   // float params, 0 to 100
+    std::string              tag = "a";
+};
+
+struct Shape {
+    static constexpr const char* id = "rp.test.shape";
+    static constexpr bool reshapes = true;
+    static constexpr bool stateless_prepare = true;
+    using Settings = ShapeSettings;
+
+    static std::optional<std::string> validate(const Settings& s) {
+        if (s.tag.empty()) return "tag must not be empty";
+        return std::nullopt;
+    }
+    static void adjust_layout(Layout& l, const Settings& s) {
+        const auto port = [&](const std::string& id, PortDir dir, PortKind kind) {
+            PortDesc p;
+            p.id = id;
+            p.dir = dir;
+            p.kind = kind;
+            l.ports.push_back(p);
+        };
+        for (const auto& id : s.ins) port(id, PortDir::In, PortKind::Events);
+        for (const auto& id : s.outs) port(id, PortDir::Out, PortKind::Events);
+        for (const auto& id : s.levels) port(id, PortDir::Out, PortKind::Control);
+        for (const auto& id : s.knobs) l.params.push_back({id, id, ParamType::Float, 0.0, 100.0, 0.0, {}, {}});
+    }
+    static std::uint8_t letter(const std::string& id) { return static_cast<std::uint8_t>(id[0] & 0x7f); }
+
+    const Settings*                settings = nullptr;
+    std::uint32_t                  blocks = 0;
+    char                           ranWith = 0;     // the tag the last block ran with
+    std::uint32_t                  ranOutputs = 0;  // and how many outputs it was handed
+    std::array<std::uint32_t, 128> received{};      // the last block's messages per input, by first letter
+    std::array<double, 128>        knobs{};         // the last block's value per knob, by first letter
+    std::array<char, 16>           committed{};     // each settings' tag, in the order on_settings saw them
+    std::uint32_t                  commits = 0;
+    std::array<std::uint8_t, 16>   mask{};
+    std::uint32_t                  maskSize = 0;
+    std::uint32_t                  maskCalls = 0;
+    char                           maskedWith = 0;  // the tag in force when the last mask arrived
+
+    void on_settings(const Settings& s) noexcept {
+        settings = &s;
+        if (commits < committed.size()) committed[commits] = s.tag[0];
+        ++commits;
+    }
+    void ports_changed(std::span<const std::uint8_t> connected) noexcept {
+        maskSize = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(connected.size());
+        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < connected.size() && i < mask.size(); ++i) mask[i] = connected[i];
+        ++maskCalls;
+        maskedWith = settings->tag[0];
+    }
+    void process(const rp::Block& b) noexcept {
+        const Settings& s = *settings;
+        ranWith = s.tag[0];
+        ranOutputs = b.raw.output_count;
+        for (std::uint32_t i = 0; i < s.ins.size(); ++i) received[letter(s.ins[i])] = b.input(i).u.queue->count;
+        for (std::uint32_t o = 0; o < s.outs.size(); ++o) {
+            const std::uint8_t m[3] = {0x90, letter(s.outs[o]), static_cast<std::uint8_t>(blocks & 0x7f)};
+            graph::pushMessage(*b.output(o).u.queue, 0, m);
+        }
+        if (blocks == 0)
+            for (std::uint32_t c = 0; c < s.levels.size(); ++c)
+                graph::pushControl(*b.output(static_cast<std::uint32_t>(s.outs.size()) + c).u.control, 0, 5.0);
+        for (std::uint32_t k = 0; k < s.knobs.size(); ++k) knobs[letter(s.knobs[k])] = b.param(k).start;
+        ++blocks;
+    }
+};
+
````

Create `packages/native/test/graph/Reshape.test.cpp`:

````cpp
// Reshape (docs/modular-graph-phase-b3a-design.md section 2.4): a node may keep its instance through a settings
// change that alters its layout. The new plan's ports are bound to it by id, what its params and control outputs
// hold carries over by id, a feedback wire into or out of it keeps its block in flight, and its new settings commit
// at the swap, in push order with every other command. A node that answers rebuild is rebuilt as before, a
// document refused after a reshape was prepared leaves the instance as it was, and the commits of a node whose
// prepare is stateless never make setGraph wait.
#include <catch2/catch_test_macros.hpp>

#include <array>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

#include "GraphRig.hpp"

using namespace rp::graph;
using rp::graph::test::GraphRig;
using rp::graph::test::Shape;
using rp::graph::test::Sink;
using rp::graph::test::Source;

namespace {

// rp.test.shape `x` with these settings (and document param values), then the case's other nodes and wires.
std::string doc(const std::string& shape, const std::string& nodes = "", const std::string& wires = "",
                const std::string& params = "") {
    return R"({"nodes":[{"id":"x","type":"rp.test.shape","settings":)" + shape +
           (params.empty() ? "" : R"(,"params":)" + params) + "}" + (nodes.empty() ? "" : "," + nodes) +
           R"(],"wires":[)" + wires + "]}";
}

// rp.test.source whose prepare answers swap whatever changed, which for a change to its layout breaks the contract.
rp_prepare_result alwaysSwap(rp_node*, const rp_settings*, void** prepared, rp_error*) {
    *prepared = new test::SourceSettings{};
    return RP_PREPARE_SWAP;
}
const char* swapperDescriptor() { return R"({"id":"rp.test.swapper"})"; }
rp_node* swapperCreate(const rp_host* host, void* memory, const rp_settings* s, rp_error* err) {
    rp_node* n = rp::node_type<Source>()->create(host, memory, s, err);
    if (!n) return nullptr;
    static const rp_node_vtable vt = [&] {
        rp_node_vtable v = *n->vt;
        v.prepare_settings = &alwaysSwap;
        return v;
    }();
    n->vt = &vt;
    return n;
}

const rp_package* reshapePackage() {
    static const rp_node_type swapper{"rp.test.swapper", &swapperDescriptor, rp::node_type<Source>()->layout_for,
                                      rp::node_type<Source>()->query_memory, &swapperCreate,
                                      rp::node_type<Source>()->destroy, 0u};
    static const rp_node_type* const kTypes[] = {&swapper};
    static const rp_package kPackage{RP_ABI_VERSION, R"({"id":"rp.test.reshape"})", 1, kTypes};
    return &kPackage;
}

// The tag of x's settings as each host command was applied.
struct TagLog {
    rp_node*          x = nullptr;
    std::vector<char> tags;
};

void logTag(void* ctx, const HostCommand&, const void*, bool) {
    auto* log = static_cast<TagLog*>(ctx);
    log->tags.push_back(rp::peer_as<Shape>(log->x)->settings->tag[0]);
}

}  // namespace

TEST_CASE("a reshape keeps the instance and its state through a layout change", "[graph][reshape]") {
    GraphRig rig;
    const std::string sink = R"({"id":"s","type":"rp.test.sink"})";
    const std::string wire = R"({"from":"x.b","to":"s.events"})";
    REQUIRE(rig.set(doc(R"({"outs":["b"]})", sink, wire)).ok);
    rig.run(64, 3);
    rp_node* const before = rig.host->node("x");
    REQUIRE(rig.set(doc(R"({"outs":["a","b"]})", sink, wire)).ok);
    CHECK(rig.host->node("x") == before);
    rig.run();
    const Shape& x = rig.node<Shape>("x");
    CHECK(x.blocks == 4);
    CHECK(x.ranOutputs == 2);

    // A reshape that leaves the layout as it was is a swap: the instance takes the settings and nothing else.
    const std::uint32_t maskCalls = x.maskCalls;
    REQUIRE(rig.set(doc(R"({"outs":["a","b"],"tag":"c"})", sink, wire)).ok);
    rig.run();
    CHECK(rig.host->node("x") == before);
    CHECK(x.ranWith == 'c');
    CHECK(x.blocks == 5);
    CHECK(x.maskCalls == maskCalls);
}

TEST_CASE("a reshape rebinds ports, params and control outputs by id", "[graph][reshape]") {
    GraphRig rig;
    const std::string nodes = R"({"id":"src","type":"rp.test.source"},{"id":"s","type":"rp.test.sink"},)"
                              R"({"id":"ls","type":"rp.test.sink"})";
    const std::string wires = R"({"from":"x.b","to":"s.events"},{"from":"src.events","to":"x.q"},)"
                              R"({"from":"x.L","to":"ls.control"})";
    const auto shape = [&](const char* settings) { return rig.set(doc(settings, nodes, wires)); };
    // What survives every reshape below: b still reaches s, q still hears src, h keeps its value, L its 5.
    const auto survived = [&] {
        const Shape& x = rig.node<Shape>("x");
        const Sink& s = rig.node<Sink>("s");
        CHECK(s.eventCount == 1);
        CHECK(s.eventBytes[0] == 'b');
        CHECK(x.received['q'] == 1);
        CHECK(x.knobs['h'] == 42.0);
        CHECK(rig.node<Sink>("ls").controlStart == 5.0);  // set on x's first block only, then held by the stream
    };
    REQUIRE(shape(R"({"ins":["q"],"outs":["b"],"levels":["L"],"knobs":["h"]})").ok);
    REQUIRE(rig.host->setParam("x", "h", 42.0));
    rig.run(64, 2);
    survived();

    // One of each added before it...
    REQUIRE(shape(R"({"ins":["p","q"],"outs":["a","b"],"levels":["K","L"],"knobs":["g","h"]})").ok);
    rig.run();
    survived();
    CHECK(rig.node<Shape>("x").received['p'] == 0);
    CHECK(rig.node<Shape>("x").knobs['g'] == 0.0);  // a new param starts at its default

    // ...then those removed, and others added after it.
    REQUIRE(shape(R"({"ins":["q","r"],"outs":["b","c"],"levels":["L","M"],"knobs":["h","i"]})").ok);
    rig.run();
    survived();
    CHECK_FALSE(rig.host->setParam("x", "g", 1.0));  // gone with the layout that had it
    REQUIRE(rig.host->setParam("x", "i", 7.0));
    rig.run(64, 2);
    CHECK(rig.node<Shape>("x").knobs['i'] == 7.0);
    CHECK(rig.node<Shape>("x").blocks == 6);
}

TEST_CASE("a reshape sends document values to the params it adds, not again to the ones it keeps", "[graph][reshape]") {
    GraphRig rig;
    REQUIRE(rig.set(doc(R"({"knobs":["h"]})", "", "", R"({"h":30})")).ok);
    rig.run();
    const Shape& x = rig.node<Shape>("x");
    CHECK(x.knobs['h'] == 30.0);
    REQUIRE(rig.host->setParam("x", "h", 50.0));
    rig.run(64, 2);
    REQUIRE(x.knobs['h'] == 50.0);

    REQUIRE(rig.set(doc(R"({"knobs":["g","h"]})", "", "", R"({"g":7,"h":30})")).ok);
    rig.run();
    CHECK(x.knobs['g'] == 7.0);
    CHECK(x.knobs['h'] == 50.0);  // h's document value was already sent; the live value stands

    // A param dropped and then added back is a new param, so its document value is sent again.
    REQUIRE(rig.set(doc(R"({"knobs":["h"]})", "", "", R"({"h":30})")).ok);
    REQUIRE(rig.set(doc(R"({"knobs":["g","h"]})", "", "", R"({"g":7,"h":30})")).ok);
    rig.run();
    CHECK(x.knobs['g'] == 7.0);
}

TEST_CASE("a feedback wire into or out of a reshaped node keeps its block in flight", "[graph][reshape][feedback]") {
    GraphRig rig;
    const std::string nodes = R"({"id":"src","type":"rp.test.source"},{"id":"s","type":"rp.test.sink"})";
    const std::string wires = R"({"from":"x.b","to":"s.events","feedback":true},)"
                              R"({"from":"src.events","to":"x.q","feedback":true})";
    REQUIRE(rig.set(doc(R"({"ins":["q"],"outs":["b"]})", nodes, wires)).ok);
    rig.run(64, 2);
    rp_node* const before = rig.host->node("x");
    rig.host->setAudioThreadOwns(true);
    REQUIRE(rig.set(doc(R"({"ins":["p","q"],"outs":["a","b"]})", nodes, wires)).ok);
    // The old plan's last block (run with no drain) sends into both wires; the new plan's first block, which
    // adopts the reshape, reads what it sent.
    rig.host->run(64, rig.transport);
    rig.run();
    CHECK(rig.host->node("x") == before);
    CHECK(rig.node<Shape>("x").ranOutputs == 2);
    CHECK(rig.node<Shape>("x").received['q'] == 1);
    CHECK(rig.node<Sink>("s").eventCount == 1);
    CHECK(rig.node<Sink>("s").eventBytes[0] == 'b');
    rig.host->setAudioThreadOwns(false);
}

TEST_CASE("a reshape's settings commit at the swap, in push order with every other command", "[graph][reshape]") {
    GraphRig rig;
    REQUIRE(rig.set(doc(R"({"outs":["b"],"knobs":["g"]})")).ok);
    TagLog log{rig.host->node("x"), {}};
    rig.host->setHostCommandHandler(&logTag, &log);
    rig.run();
    rig.host->setAudioThreadOwns(true);
    const char c = 0;
    REQUIRE(rig.host->pushHostCommand(&c, 1));
    REQUIRE(rig.host->setParam("x", "g", 1.0));  // to a param the reshape drops: it reaches the stream it was sent to
    REQUIRE(rig.set(doc(R"({"outs":["a","b"],"tag":"b"})")).ok);
    REQUIRE(rig.host->pushHostCommand(&c, 1));
    const Shape& x = rig.node<Shape>("x");
    rig.host->run(64, rig.transport);  // the old plan's last block: nothing has been committed yet
    CHECK(x.ranWith == 'a');
    CHECK(x.ranOutputs == 1);
    CHECK(x.commits == 1);  // create's
    CHECK(log.tags.empty());
    rig.run();  // the drain (a command, the swap and its commit, a command), then the new plan's first block
    CHECK(log.tags == std::vector<char>{'a', 'b'});
    CHECK(x.commits == 2);
    CHECK(x.committed[1] == 'b');
    CHECK(x.ranWith == 'b');
    CHECK(x.ranOutputs == 2);
    rig.host->setAudioThreadOwns(false);
}

TEST_CASE("a reshaped node is told its connected outputs at the swap, by its new layout", "[graph][reshape]") {
    GraphRig rig;
    const std::string sink = R"({"id":"s","type":"rp.test.sink"})";
    const std::string wire = R"({"from":"x.b","to":"s.events"})";
    REQUIRE(rig.set(doc(R"({"outs":["a","b"]})", sink, wire)).ok);
    rig.run();
    const Shape& x = rig.node<Shape>("x");
    REQUIRE(x.maskCalls == 1);
    CHECK(x.maskSize == 2);
    CHECK((x.mask[0] == 0 && x.mask[1] == 1));

    // b moves to the front: connected as before by id, but not by position.
    REQUIRE(rig.set(doc(R"({"outs":["b","c","d"],"tag":"b"})", sink, wire)).ok);
    rig.run();
    CHECK(x.maskCalls == 2);
    CHECK(x.maskSize == 3);
    CHECK((x.mask[0] == 1 && x.mask[1] == 0 && x.mask[2] == 0));
    CHECK(x.maskedWith == 'b');  // after the commit: the mask is read against the settings it belongs to

    // Only an input added: the same mask by id and by position, and a reshape still brings one.
    REQUIRE(rig.set(doc(R"({"ins":["q"],"outs":["b","c","d"],"tag":"c"})", sink, wire)).ok);
    rig.run();
    CHECK(x.maskCalls == 3);
    CHECK(x.maskSize == 3);
    CHECK(x.maskedWith == 'c');
}

TEST_CASE("a node that answers rebuild for a layout change is still rebuilt", "[graph][reshape]") {
    GraphRig rig;
    REQUIRE(rig.set(R"({"nodes":[{"id":"src","type":"rp.test.source","settings":{"channels":2}}],"wires":[]})").ok);
    rig.run(64, 2);
    rp_node* const before = rig.host->node("src");
    REQUIRE(rig.node<Source>("src").frames == 128);
    REQUIRE(rig.set(R"({"nodes":[{"id":"src","type":"rp.test.source","settings":{"channels":1}}],"wires":[]})").ok);
    CHECK(rig.host->node("src") != before);
    CHECK(rig.node<Source>("src").frames == 0);
}

TEST_CASE("a node that answers swap for a change to its layout breaks the contract", "[graph][reshape]") {
    GraphRig rig;
    REQUIRE(rig.registry.addPackage(reshapePackage()));
    REQUIRE(rig.set(R"({"nodes":[{"id":"w","type":"rp.test.swapper","settings":{"channels":2}}],"wires":[]})").ok);
    rp_node* const before = rig.host->node("w");
    // What it prepared is released, not leaked (the ASan build checks).
    const auto r = rig.set(R"({"nodes":[{"id":"w","type":"rp.test.swapper","settings":{"channels":1}}],"wires":[]})");
    REQUIRE(GraphRig::codes(r) == "node-contract");
    CHECK(rig.host->node("w") == before);
    CHECK(rig.set(R"({"nodes":[{"id":"w","type":"rp.test.swapper","settings":{"channels":2,"value":0.5}}],)"
                  R"("wires":[]})").ok);  // a change it may swap
}

TEST_CASE("setGraph never waits on a stateless prepare's commits, and on every other as before",
          "[graph][reshape][swap]") {
    GraphRig rig({48000.0, 64, Target::Desktop, 50});  // a 50 ms adoption timeout
    const auto both = [](const char* shape, const char* value) {
        return doc(shape, std::string(R"({"id":"src","type":"rp.test.source","settings":{"value":)") + value + "}}");
    };
    REQUIRE(rig.set(both(R"({"outs":["b"]})", "1")).ok);
    rig.run();
    rig.host->setAudioThreadOwns(true);  // and no block runs until the end, so nothing is adopted
    // Two reshapes committing settings to x, the second planned while the first is unadopted.
    REQUIRE(rig.set(both(R"({"outs":["a","b"],"tag":"b"})", "1")).ok);
    REQUIRE(rig.set(both(R"({"outs":["b"],"tag":"c"})", "1")).ok);
    // A commit to src, whose prepare reads its settings: nothing in flight makes this one wait...
    REQUIRE(rig.set(both(R"({"outs":["b"],"tag":"c"})", "0.5")).ok);
    // ...and it makes the next one wait, and refuse at the timeout, exactly as before.
    CHECK(GraphRig::codes(rig.set(both(R"({"outs":["b"],"tag":"d"})", "0.5"))) == "busy");
    rig.run();  // adopts all three, in order
    const Shape& x = rig.node<Shape>("x");
    CHECK(x.commits == 3);
    CHECK(x.committed[1] == 'b');
    CHECK(x.committed[2] == 'c');
    CHECK(x.ranWith == 'c');
    CHECK(x.ranOutputs == 1);
    CHECK(rig.node<Source>("src").value == 0.5f);
    CHECK(rig.set(both(R"({"outs":["b"],"tag":"d"})", "0.5")).ok);
    rig.run();
    CHECK(x.ranWith == 'd');
    rig.host->setAudioThreadOwns(false);
}

TEST_CASE("a reshape in a document refused later leaves the instance and its layout as they were", "[graph][reshape]") {
    GraphRig rig;
    const std::string sink = R"({"id":"s","type":"rp.test.sink"})";
    const std::string wire = R"({"from":"x.b","to":"s.events"})";
    REQUIRE(rig.set(doc(R"({"outs":["b"],"knobs":["h"]})", sink, wire)).ok);
    rig.run();
    rp_node* const before = rig.host->node("x");
    const Shape& x = rig.node<Shape>("x");
    const std::uint32_t maskCalls = x.maskCalls;
    // Reconcile prepares the reshape; only the coupled-group check, after it, refuses the document.
    const auto r = rig.set(doc(R"({"outs":["a","b"],"knobs":["g"],"tag":"b"})",
                               sink + R"(,{"id":"l","type":"rp.test.linked"},{"id":"n","type":"rp.test.nostep"})",
                               wire + R"(,{"from":"l.link","to":"n.link"})"));
    REQUIRE(GraphRig::codes(r) == "link-without-step");
    CHECK(rig.host->node("x") == before);
    CHECK(rig.host->setParam("x", "h", 3.0));        // the old layout's param...
    CHECK_FALSE(rig.host->setParam("x", "g", 3.0));  // ...and not the refused one's
    rig.run();
    CHECK(x.commits == 1);
    CHECK(x.ranWith == 'a');
    CHECK(x.ranOutputs == 1);
    CHECK(x.maskCalls == maskCalls);
    CHECK(rig.node<Sink>("s").eventBytes[0] == 'b');

    // The same reshape on its own still lands.
    REQUIRE(rig.set(doc(R"({"outs":["a","b"],"knobs":["g"],"tag":"b"})", sink, wire)).ok);
    rig.run();
    CHECK(rig.host->node("x") == before);
    CHECK(x.ranWith == 'b');
    CHECK(x.ranOutputs == 2);
}
````

````diff
+    rp_node* const x = rig.host->node("x");
+    rig.host->setAudioThreadOwns(true);
+
+    std::string failures;
+    bool settled = false;
+    {
+        AudioThread audio(*rig.host);
+        // A stateless prepare's commits never make setGraph wait, so it can fill the ring faster than the audio
+        // thread drains it: retry, it is draining.
+        const auto retry = [&](auto&& attempt) {
+            const auto deadline = std::chrono::steady_clock::now() + std::chrono::seconds(5);
+            while (!attempt())
+                if (std::chrono::steady_clock::now() > deadline) return false;
+                else std::this_thread::yield();
+            return true;
+        };
+        for (int i = 1; i <= 200; ++i) {
+            if (!retry([&] { return rig.set(reshapeDoc(i)).ok; })) failures += "set " + std::to_string(i) + "; ";
+            if (!retry([&] { return rig.host->setParam("x", "h", static_cast<double>(i % 100)); }))
+                failures += "param " + std::to_string(i) + "; ";
+            rig.host->reclaim();
+        }
+        if (!retry([&] { return rig.host->setParam("x", "h", 99.0); })) failures += "param 99; ";
+        if (!retry([&] { return rig.set(reshapeDoc(201)).ok; })) failures += "set 201; ";
+        settled = audio.waitBlocks(4);
+        audio.stop();
+        CHECK(failures.empty());
+        CHECK_FALSE(audio.wrong());
+        CHECK(rig.host->node("x") == x);  // never rebuilt...
+        CHECK(rig.node<Shape>("x").blocks == static_cast<std::uint32_t>(audio.blocks()));  // ...and ran every block
+    }
+
+    CHECK(settled);
+    CHECK(rig.node<Shape>("x").ranWith == '5');           // variant 201's tag
+    CHECK(rig.node<Shape>("x").knobs['h'] == 99.0);       // h's stream survived every reshape
+    CHECK(rig.node<Sink>("ls").controlStart == 5.0);      // and so did L's
+    CHECK(rig.node<Sink>("s").eventBytes[0] == 'b');
+}
````

- [ ] **Step 8: Commit**

````bash
git add -A -- packages/native/
git commit -F - <<'EOF'
feat(graph): reshape - a node kept across a layout change, its settings committed at the swap

prepare_settings gains RP_PREPARE_RESHAPE: keep the instance with the layout layout_for gives the new
settings. The planner now asks the live instance about every settings change, layout change included; a node
that answers rebuild is rebuilt as before, a reshape with the layout unchanged is a swap, and a swap for a
changed layout is a node-contract error.

Everything an instance holds per port and param (its layout, param and control-output streams, resource
output slots, and the control side's applied / wired / mask records) moves into a PortState. A reshape builds
a new one on the control thread, sharing by id the streams and slots that persist and creating the rest; every
plan holds the PortStates it was built with, and the instance's current one changes only at publish, so
nothing the running plan reads is written or freed while the next one is planned. The prepared settings commit
at adoption through the existing path, ports_changed always follows a layout-changing reshape, and a feedback
wire to or from the node keeps its front.

rp_node_type gains flags, with RP_TYPE_STATELESS_PREPARE: setGraph's adoption wait now counts only plans that
commit to a type without it, so a host that stops calling process no longer holds every such edit for the
timeout. The C++ layer takes `reshapes` and `stateless_prepare` (the latter rules out needs_rebuild).
EOF
````

---

### Task 3: Queue capacity in port descriptors, and drops reaching the host

A plan queue holds 256 messages and 4 KB and drops what does not fit, while the kernel's staging vectors it replaces
were unbounded, so a large SysEx or a burst of tracker sync bytes would be dropped on a wire (design section 2.6).
An events or bytes port's layout may now declare `"capacity": {"messages": n, "bytes": n}`, either part or both; a
part left out keeps today's numbers, and either part past 1 Mi messages / 16 MiB is refused (by the parser for a
descriptor or a pack's layout, and as invalid settings when a C++ node's `adjust_layout` sets it). The planner sizes
each output queue from its port and each feedback wire's front from the wire's source (a front whose source's
capacity changed starts empty, as one whose channel count changed starts silent). A wire carries its source's
queue, so the source's capacity wins whatever its input declares, and only output capacities bound anything.
Unconnected outputs keep sharing one default-size scratch queue, whose drops are not counted.

The C++ layer declares a capacity on the port's type (`rp::bytes_out::sized<rp::capacity{.bytes = 65536}>`) or
from settings in `adjust_layout`; the TS layer as `events.out({ messages: 1024 })`, checked as `Descriptor.cpp`
checks it, and the kitchen-sink golden gains capacities so both languages still spell it byte for byte. What a
full queue drops stays in its `rp_queue::dropped`, which only the block thread touches: at the end of each block
the executor adds it to the producing instance's atomic counter and the host's total and zeroes it, the control
thread reads only those atomics (`GraphHost::droppedMessages()`, overall or per node id), and `reclaim()` names
each node the first time its outputs drop.

````cpp
// Queue capacity (docs/modular-graph-phase-b3a-design.md section 2.6): an events or bytes port may declare how many
// messages and payload bytes its queue carries. The planner sizes each output queue from its port and each feedback
// front from the wire's source, a port that declares nothing keeps today's 256 messages and 4096 bytes, and a
// capacity past the caps is refused. What a full queue drops is published by the thread that runs the block, for
// the host to read on the control thread.
#include <catch2/catch_test_macros.hpp>

#include <algorithm>
#include <array>
#include <atomic>
#include <chrono>
#include <iterator>
#include <span>
#include <string>
#include <thread>

#include "GraphRig.hpp"

using namespace rp::graph;
using rp::graph::test::GraphRig;

namespace {

constexpr std::uint32_t kPayloadBytes = 1u << 16;

// Each block, `count` messages of `size` bytes on its events output, whose queue capacity its settings declare (a
// part left 0 keeps the default).
struct BurstSettings {
    std::uint32_t count = 1;
    std::uint32_t size = 3;
    std::uint32_t messages = 0;
    std::uint32_t bytes = 0;
};

struct Burst {
    static constexpr const char* id = "rp.test.burst";
    using Settings = BurstSettings;
    struct { rp::events_out out; } outputs;

    static void adjust_layout(Layout& l, const Settings& s) {
        if (s.messages) l.ports[0].capacity.messages = s.messages;
        if (s.bytes) l.ports[0].capacity.bytes = s.bytes;
    }

    std::uint32_t count = 1, size = 3;
    void on_settings(const Settings& s) noexcept {
        count = s.count;
        size = std::min(s.size, kPayloadBytes);
    }
    void process(const rp::Block&) noexcept {
        static const std::array<std::uint8_t, kPayloadBytes> payload{};
        for (std::uint32_t i = 0; i < count; ++i) outputs.out.push(0, std::span(payload.data(), size));
    }
};

// What reached its events input this block: how many messages, and the largest. Its input declares the capacity
// its settings name, which bounds nothing: a wire carries its source's queue.
struct TallySettings {
    std::uint32_t messages = 0;
};

struct Tally {
    static constexpr const char* id = "rp.test.tally";
    using Settings = TallySettings;
    struct { rp::events_in in; } inputs;

    static void adjust_layout(Layout& l, const Settings& s) {
        if (s.messages) l.ports[0].capacity.messages = s.messages;
    }

    std::uint32_t messages = 0, largest = 0;
    void process(const rp::Block&) noexcept {
        messages = 0;
        largest = 0;
        for (const auto& m : inputs.in.messages()) {
            ++messages;
            largest = std::max(largest, m.size);
        }
    }
};

const rp_package* capacityPackage() {
    static const rp_node_type* const kTypes[] = {rp::node_type<Burst>(), rp::node_type<Tally>()};
    static const rp_package kPackage{RP_ABI_VERSION, R"({"id":"rp.test.capacity"})",
                                     static_cast<std::uint32_t>(std::size(kTypes)), kTypes};
    return &kPackage;
}

struct CapacityRig : GraphRig {
    CapacityRig() { registry.addPackage(capacityPackage()); }
};

// A burst `b` with these settings, wired to a tally `t` (through a feedback wire if asked).
std::string doc(const std::string& burst, const std::string& tally = "{}", bool feedback = false) {
    return R"({"nodes":[{"id":"b","type":"rp.test.burst","settings":)" + burst +
           R"(},{"id":"t","type":"rp.test.tally","settings":)" + tally + R"(}],"wires":[{"from":"b.out","to":"t.in")" +
           (feedback ? R"(,"feedback":true)" : "") + "}]}";
}

}  // namespace

TEST_CASE("a port that declares two messages drops the third, and the drop reaches the host", "[graph][capacity]") {
    CapacityRig rig;
    REQUIRE(rig.set(doc(R"({"count":3,"messages":2})")).ok);
    rig.run();
    CHECK(rig.node<Tally>("t").messages == 2);
    CHECK(rig.host->droppedMessages() == 1);
    CHECK(rig.host->droppedMessages("b") == 1);  // charged to the node whose output it is
    CHECK(rig.host->droppedMessages("t") == 0);
    CHECK(rig.host->droppedMessages("nope") == 0);
    // Each block's drops are published once: two more blocks are two more drops.
    rig.run(64, 2);
    CHECK(rig.host->droppedMessages() == 3);
    CHECK(rig.host->droppedMessages("b") == 3);
}

TEST_CASE("a port that declares 64 KiB carries a 60 KiB message the default drops", "[graph][capacity]") {
    CapacityRig rig;
    REQUIRE(rig.set(doc(R"({"size":61440,"bytes":65536})")).ok);
    rig.run();
    CHECK(rig.node<Tally>("t").largest == 61440);
    CHECK(rig.host->droppedMessages() == 0);

    REQUIRE(rig.set(doc(R"({"size":61440})")).ok);
    rig.run();
    CHECK(rig.node<Tally>("t").messages == 0);
    CHECK(rig.host->droppedMessages() == 1);
}

TEST_CASE("a port that declares nothing keeps 256 messages and 4096 bytes", "[graph][capacity]") {
    CapacityRig rig;
    const SetGraphResult r = rig.set(doc(R"({"count":257,"size":1})"));
    REQUIRE(r.ok);
    CHECK(r.layouts.at("b").find("capacity") == std::string::npos);  // nothing declared, nothing spelt
    rig.run();
    CHECK(rig.node<Tally>("t").messages == 256);
    CHECK(rig.host->droppedMessages() == 1);

    REQUIRE(rig.set(doc(R"({"size":4096})")).ok);
    rig.run();
    CHECK(rig.node<Tally>("t").largest == 4096);
    CHECK(rig.host->droppedMessages() == 1);

    REQUIRE(rig.set(doc(R"({"size":4097})")).ok);
    rig.run();
    CHECK(rig.node<Tally>("t").messages == 0);
    CHECK(rig.host->droppedMessages() == 2);
}

TEST_CASE("a capacity past the caps is refused as the node's settings", "[graph][capacity]") {
    CapacityRig rig;
    SetGraphResult r = rig.set(doc(R"({"messages":1048577})"));
    REQUIRE_FALSE(r.ok);
    CHECK(GraphRig::codes(r) == "settings-invalid");
    CHECK(r.errors[0].nodeId == "b");
    CHECK(r.errors[0].message == R"(port "out": "capacity.messages" must be a whole number from 1 to 1048576)");

    r = rig.set(doc(R"({"bytes":16777217})"));
    REQUIRE_FALSE(r.ok);
    CHECK(GraphRig::codes(r) == "settings-invalid");
    CHECK(r.errors[0].message == R"(port "out": "capacity.bytes" must be a whole number from 1 to 16777216)");

    CHECK(rig.set(doc(R"({"messages":1048576,"bytes":16777216})")).ok);  // the caps themselves
}

TEST_CASE("a wire carries its source's capacity, whatever its input declares", "[graph][capacity]") {
    CapacityRig rig;
    REQUIRE(rig.set(doc(R"({"count":8,"messages":8})", R"({"messages":1})")).ok);
    rig.run();
    CHECK(rig.node<Tally>("t").messages == 8);
    CHECK(rig.host->droppedMessages() == 0);

    REQUIRE(rig.set(doc(R"({"count":8,"messages":2})", R"({"messages":64})")).ok);
    rig.run();
    CHECK(rig.node<Tally>("t").messages == 2);
    CHECK(rig.host->droppedMessages() == 6);
}

TEST_CASE("a feedback wire's front is sized from its source, and resized with it", "[graph][capacity]") {
    CapacityRig rig;
    // The tally's input declares one message; the front takes the source's 512.
    REQUIRE(rig.set(doc(R"({"count":300,"messages":512})", R"({"messages":1})", true)).ok);
    rig.run();
    CHECK(rig.node<Tally>("t").messages == 0);  // a block behind
    rig.run();
    CHECK(rig.node<Tally>("t").messages == 300);

    // More than the old front holds. A front kept at 512 would hand the tally 512 and lose the rest unseen, since a
    // front is only ever filled from its own source's queue.
    REQUIRE(rig.set(doc(R"({"count":800,"messages":1024})", R"({"messages":1})", true)).ok);
    rig.run(64, 2);
    CHECK(rig.node<Tally>("t").messages == 800);
    CHECK(rig.host->droppedMessages() == 0);
}

TEST_CASE("an unconnected output's drops lose nothing, so they are not counted", "[graph][capacity]") {
    CapacityRig rig;
    REQUIRE(rig.set(R"({"nodes":[{"id":"b","type":"rp.test.burst","settings":{"count":300}}],"wires":[]})").ok);
    rig.run();
    CHECK(rig.host->droppedMessages() == 0);
}

TEST_CASE("the control thread reads drops while the audio thread publishes them", "[graph][capacity]") {
    CapacityRig rig;
    REQUIRE(rig.set(doc(R"({"count":3,"messages":2})")).ok);
    rig.host->setAudioThreadOwns(true);
    std::atomic<bool> stop{false};
    std::thread audio([&] {
        while (!stop.load(std::memory_order_acquire)) rig.host->processBlock(64, rig.transport);
    });
    // Read, and reclaimed (which reports the dropping node), while the audio thread writes every queue's count.
    const auto deadline = std::chrono::steady_clock::now() + std::chrono::seconds(10);
    while (rig.host->droppedMessages() < 100 && std::chrono::steady_clock::now() < deadline) {
        rig.host->reclaim();
        std::this_thread::yield();
    }
    stop.store(true, std::memory_order_release);
    audio.join();
    rig.host->setAudioThreadOwns(false);
    CHECK(rig.host->droppedMessages() >= 100);
    CHECK(rig.host->droppedMessages("b") == rig.host->droppedMessages());
}
````

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement it, natively**

````diff
diff --git a/packages/native/src/graph/Descriptor.cpp b/packages/native/src/graph/Descriptor.cpp

--- a/packages/native/src/graph/Descriptor.cpp
+++ b/packages/native/src/graph/Descriptor.cpp
@@ -53,6 +53,13 @@ rfl::Generic portGeneric(const PortDesc& p) {
         put(o, "resourceType", rfl::Generic(p.resourceType));
         if (p.write) put(o, "access", rfl::Generic(std::string("write")));
     }
+    // As declared: a part left undeclared is written as nothing, so a port that declares none writes no field.
+    if ((p.kind == PortKind::Events || p.kind == PortKind::Bytes) && (p.capacity.messages || p.capacity.bytes)) {
+        Object c;
+        if (p.capacity.messages) put(c, "messages", rfl::Generic(static_cast<std::int64_t>(*p.capacity.messages)));
+        if (p.capacity.bytes) put(c, "bytes", rfl::Generic(static_cast<std::int64_t>(*p.capacity.bytes)));
+        put(o, "capacity", rfl::Generic(std::move(c)));
+    }
     return rfl::Generic(std::move(o));
 }
 
@@ -203,6 +210,32 @@ rfl::Result<ChannelSpec> parseChannels(const rfl::Generic& g, const std::string&
     return ChannelSpec::fixed(static_cast<std::uint32_t>(count), *layoutName);
 }
 
+std::string capacityRange(const std::string& where, std::string_view part, std::uint32_t max) {
+    return where + ": \"capacity." + std::string(part) + "\" must be a whole number from 1 to " + std::to_string(max);
+}
+
+const char* const kNoQueue = ": only events and bytes ports have \"capacity\"";
+
+// A queue port's capacity: messages, bytes or both, each a whole number from 1 to its cap.
+rfl::Result<QueueCapacity> parseCapacity(const rfl::Generic& g, const std::string& where) {
+    auto o = g.to_object();
+    if (!o) return fail(where + ": \"capacity\" must be an object");
+    if (auto bad = unknownField(*o, {"messages", "bytes"}, where + " capacity")) return fail(*bad);
+    QueueCapacity c;
+    for (const bool bytes : {false, true}) {
+        const std::string_view part = bytes ? "bytes" : "messages";
````

- [ ] **Step 7: Commit**

````bash
git add -A -- docs/ packages/native/ packages/retroplug/
git commit -F - <<'EOF'
feat(graph): a port declares its queue capacity; drops reach the host

An events or bytes port's layout may declare "capacity": {"messages": n, "bytes": n}, either part or both; a
part left out keeps today's 256 messages / 4096 bytes, and either part past 1 Mi messages / 16 MiB is refused
(by the parser for a descriptor or a pack's layout, and as invalid settings when a C++ node's adjust_layout
sets it). The planner sizes each output queue from its port and each feedback wire's front from the wire's
source; a front whose source's capacity changed starts empty, as one whose channel count changed starts
silent. A wire carries its source's queue, so the source's capacity wins over whatever its input declares.
Unconnected outputs keep sharing one default-size scratch queue.

The C++ layer declares it on the port's type, rp::bytes_out::sized<rp::capacity{.bytes = 65536}>, or from
settings in adjust_layout; the TS layer as events.out({ messages: 1024 }), checked as Descriptor.cpp checks
it. The kitchen-sink golden gains capacities on inputs and outputs, and both languages still spell it byte
for byte.

What a full queue drops stays in its rp_queue::dropped, which only the thread running the block touches. At
the end of each block the executor adds it to the producing instance's atomic counter and the host's total,
then zeroes it; the control thread reads only those atomics (GraphHost::droppedMessages, overall or per
node), and reclaim() names each node the first time its outputs drop. The scratch queue's drops are not
counted: nothing reads it.
EOF
````

### Task 4: System node inputs, the Game Boy's `serialOut`, the host I/O nodes and the cart mirror, beside today's path

Everything design section 3 describes, natively, without changing what runs: no production document uses any of
it yet, the kernel stage still fans its sinks out by id, and parity does not move.

- **System node inputs** (design 3.1): every system node takes `serialIn` (bytes, one `pushSerialIn` per byte),
  `midi` (events, `onMidi`, with the kernel stage's rule that a message longer than a `MidiEvent`'s inline data goes
  down `pushCoreBytes` unframed), `bytes` (bytes, `pushCoreBytes`, the flush flag riding `RP_MESSAGE_FLUSH`) and
  `buttons` (events, `[button, down]`). They are applied once, at the top of `prepare` (which `process` starts with,
  and which a linked Game Boy's group runs before any member steps), in the fan-out's order, each in queue order.
  Only MIDI before bytes is observable, on the NES, where both land in the same FIFO. The bytes input records into
  the engine's sync trace (`rp.engine.sync-trace/1`).
- **The Game Boy's `serialOut`** (3.2, 4096 messages / bytes): what its core captured this block, each byte at frame
  0, copied from the core's log (only while the port is connected) so the engine's MI.OUT gather still reads it.
- **The host I/O nodes** (3.3, package `rp.host.io`, over `rp.engine.host-io/1`): `rp.host.midi-in` takes the
  staged host MIDI stable-sorted by frame (an insertion sort in place, no allocation; 3.4), `rp.host.midi-out`
  strips the 4-byte system prefix (4.4) into `Engine::midiOut()`, `rp.host.controller-in` writes the surface MIDI and
  a `connected` control (a change at frame 0 on the block the flag flips), `rp.host.controller-out` feeds
  `Engine::controllerOut()`. A plan holding midi-in or controller-in leaves the kernel stage no staged MIDI
  (transitional, `SystemTable`). The engine now clears `midiOut` / `controllerOut` at the top of its block, so the
  kernel and the output nodes both append, in plan order.
- **`rp.n8.cart-mirror`** (3.5, package `rp.n8`): feeds the engine's core-byte sink every MIDI message then every
  bytes message; the engine reads the system it names off the plan (`cartMirrorSystemId`) and refuses
  (`cart-mirror`) a second mirror or one naming a system outside the slots.
- **Drops through the Engine**: `Engine::droppedMessages`, and `droppedMessages` on the harness facet (22 methods
  there, 90 in the union).

The graph tests' counting allocator moves into its own file so `retroplug-engine-graph-test` can share it.
`SystemNode::finish` wrote silence into every connected output through its audio view, whatever the port's kind;
with `serialOut` connected that would overwrite its queue, so it now silences audio outputs only.

Create `packages/native/test/graph/CountingAllocator.hpp`:

````cpp
#pragma once

// What a stretch of code allocates and frees on the calling thread. CountingAllocator.cpp replaces the global
// operator new and delete for the binary it is linked into (every form, so a block any of them allocated is
// freed by any other), and counts each call made on a thread while that thread is counting. Link it into one
// binary at most once.

namespace rp::test {

struct AllocationCount {
    int allocations = 0;
    int frees = 0;
};

// Start counting on this thread, from zero. Only one thread counts at a time.
void beginCountingAllocations();
// Stop, and what this thread allocated and freed since beginCountingAllocations.
AllocationCount endCountingAllocations();

}  // namespace rp::test
````

Create `packages/native/test/graph/CountingAllocator.cpp`:

````cpp
#include "CountingAllocator.hpp"

#if defined(__GNUC__) && !defined(__clang__)
#pragma GCC diagnostic ignored "-Wmismatched-new-delete"  // these replacements pair aligned_alloc with free on purpose
#endif

#include <atomic>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <new>
#if defined(_WIN32)
#include <malloc.h>
#endif

namespace {

thread_local bool counting = false;
std::atomic<int>  allocations{0};  // while counting
std::atomic<int>  frees{0};        // while counting

// Every block is allocated over-aligned through one pair of calls, so any delete form can free any new
// form - the platform's aligned allocator does not mix with plain free on Windows.
void* rawAlloc(std::size_t n, std::size_t align) {
    if (align < alignof(std::max_align_t)) align = alignof(std::max_align_t);
    if (n > SIZE_MAX - align) return nullptr;  // rounding up would wrap
    const std::size_t size = (n ? n : 1) + align - 1;
#if defined(_WIN32)
    return _aligned_malloc(size, align);
#else
    return std::aligned_alloc(align, size / align * align);
#endif
}

void rawFree(void* p) noexcept {
    if (counting && p) frees.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
#if defined(_WIN32)
    _aligned_free(p);
#else
    std::free(p);
#endif
}

void* allocate(std::size_t n, std::size_t align) {
    if (counting) allocations.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    void* p = rawAlloc(n, align);
    if (!p) throw std::bad_alloc();
    return p;
}

void* allocateOrNull(std::size_t n, std::size_t align) noexcept {
    if (counting) allocations.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    return rawAlloc(n, align);
}

}  // namespace

namespace rp::test {

void beginCountingAllocations() {
    allocations = 0;
    frees = 0;
    counting = true;
}

AllocationCount endCountingAllocations() {
    counting = false;
    return {allocations.load(), frees.load()};
}

}  // namespace rp::test

// Every form is replaced, nothrow ones included: a form left to the runtime allocates through it (the
// planner's aligned nothrow new, under ASan), and the replaced delete then frees what it never allocated.
void* operator new(std::size_t n) { return allocate(n, alignof(std::max_align_t)); }
void* operator new[](std::size_t n) { return allocate(n, alignof(std::max_align_t)); }
void* operator new(std::size_t n, std::align_val_t a) { return allocate(n, static_cast<std::size_t>(a)); }
void* operator new[](std::size_t n, std::align_val_t a) { return allocate(n, static_cast<std::size_t>(a)); }
void* operator new(std::size_t n, const std::nothrow_t&) noexcept { return allocateOrNull(n, alignof(std::max_align_t)); }
void* operator new[](std::size_t n, const std::nothrow_t&) noexcept { return allocateOrNull(n, alignof(std::max_align_t)); }
void* operator new(std::size_t n, std::align_val_t a, const std::nothrow_t&) noexcept {
    return allocateOrNull(n, static_cast<std::size_t>(a));
}
void* operator new[](std::size_t n, std::align_val_t a, const std::nothrow_t&) noexcept {
    return allocateOrNull(n, static_cast<std::size_t>(a));
}
void operator delete(void* p) noexcept { rawFree(p); }
void operator delete[](void* p) noexcept { rawFree(p); }
void operator delete(void* p, std::size_t) noexcept { rawFree(p); }
void operator delete[](void* p, std::size_t) noexcept { rawFree(p); }
void operator delete(void* p, std::align_val_t) noexcept { rawFree(p); }
void operator delete[](void* p, std::align_val_t) noexcept { rawFree(p); }
void operator delete(void* p, std::size_t, std::align_val_t) noexcept { rawFree(p); }
````
