````cpp
#pragma once

// Two nodes for driving and reading the engine's nodes in a NodeRig: a source a test scripts block by block, with
// one output per system node input, and a probe that records what reaches its inputs.

#include <array>
#include <cstdint>
#include <iterator>
#include <span>
#include <vector>

#include "graph/node.hpp"

namespace rp::host::test {

// Large enough that nothing a test queues is dropped.
inline constexpr rp::capacity kFeedCapacity{.messages = 1024, .bytes = 65536};

struct Message {
    std::uint32_t             frame = 0;
    std::vector<std::uint8_t> data;
    std::uint32_t             flags = 0;  // RP_MESSAGE_*
};

// Pushes what the test queued in `next` for each output on its next block, in order, then forgets it. The outputs
// are named after the system node inputs they feed.
struct Feed {
    static constexpr const char* id = "rp.test.feed";
    struct {
        rp::bytes_out::sized<kFeedCapacity>  serialIn;
        rp::events_out::sized<kFeedCapacity> midi;
        rp::bytes_out::sized<kFeedCapacity>  bytes;
        rp::events_out::sized<kFeedCapacity> buttons;
    } outputs;
    enum Port : std::uint32_t { SerialIn, Midi, Bytes, Buttons };

    std::array<std::vector<Message>, 4> next;

    void process(const rp::Block& b) noexcept {
        for (std::uint32_t o = 0; o < next.size(); ++o) {
            for (const Message& m : next[o]) rp::graph::pushMessage(*b.output(o).u.queue, m.frame, m.data, m.flags);
            next[o].clear();
        }
    }
};

// What reached its inputs in the last block it ran.
struct Probe {
    static constexpr const char* id = "rp.test.probe";
    struct {
        rp::events_in  events;
        rp::bytes_in   bytes;
        rp::control_in control;
    } inputs;

    std::vector<Message> events, bytes;
    double               controlStart = 0.0;
    std::vector<double>  controlChanges;  // their values, in order
    double               controlAtZero = 0.0;  // the start, then any change at frame 0

    template <class In>
    static void record(const In& in, std::vector<Message>& out) {
        out.clear();
        for (const rp_message& m : in.messages()) {
            const auto data = in.data(m);
            out.push_back({m.frame, std::vector<std::uint8_t>(data.begin(), data.end()), m.flags});
        }
    }
    void process(const rp::Block&) noexcept {
        record(inputs.events, events);
        record(inputs.bytes, bytes);
        controlStart = controlAtZero = inputs.control.start();
        controlChanges.clear();
        for (const rp_control_change& c : inputs.control.changes()) {
            controlChanges.push_back(c.value);
            if (c.frame == 0) controlAtZero = c.value;
        }
    }
};

inline const rp_package* testPackage() {
    static const rp_node_type* const kTypes[] = {rp::node_type<Feed>(), rp::node_type<Probe>()};
    static const rp_package kPackage{RP_ABI_VERSION, R"({"id":"rp.test.engine-graph"})",
                                     static_cast<std::uint32_t>(std::size(kTypes)), kTypes};
    return &kPackage;
}

}  // namespace rp::host::test
````

Create `packages/native/test/engine-graph/HostIo.test.cpp`:

````cpp
// The engine's host I/O nodes and the cart mirror (docs/modular-graph-phase-b3a-design.md sections 3.3 to 3.5),
// beside today's kernel stage: what the hosts stage reaches a plan through rp.host.midi-in and controller-in, what
// a plan sends reaches the buffers the hosts drain through rp.host.midi-out and controller-out, both producers of
// those buffers coexist, rp.n8.cart-mirror feeds the engine's core-byte sink, the Game Boy's serialOut carries
// MI.OUT while the engine's own gather still does, and a full queue's drops reach the engine and the harness RPC.
// Driven on a quiescent Engine, and on a NodeRig where a node's calls on the engine are what is checked.
//
// Run via `pnpm test:plugin engine-graph`.

#include <algorithm>
#include <cstdint>
#include <functional>
#include <memory>
#include <string>
#include <utility>
#include <vector>

#include <catch2/catch_test_macros.hpp>

#include "../graph/CountingAllocator.hpp"
#include "GraphDocs.hpp"
#include "NodeRig.hpp"
#include "host/dsp/ScriptCompiler.hpp"
#include "host/engine/Engine.hpp"
#include "host/engine/EngineInvoker.hpp"
#include "host/graph/HostIoNodes.hpp"
#include "host/rpc/EngineRpcService.hpp"
#include "system/SystemFactory.hpp"
#include "system/mesen/MesenNesConfig.hpp"
#include "system/mesen/MesenNesSystem.hpp"
#include "system/sameboy/SameBoyConfig.hpp"
#include "system/sameboy/SameBoySystem.hpp"

using rp::host::test::DocExtras;
using rp::host::test::docNode;
using rp::host::test::docWire;
using rp::host::test::graphRequest;
using rp::host::test::readFile;
using rp::host::test::stereoDocument;

namespace {

constexpr double kRate = 48000.0;
constexpr std::uint32_t kFrames = 1024;

const char* const kGb = rp::host::test::kGbType;
const char* const kNes = rp::host::test::kNesType;

std::unique_ptr<SameBoySystem> mgb(SystemId id) {
    SameBoyConfig cfg;
    cfg.model = SameBoyModel::DmgB;
    auto s = std::make_unique<SameBoySystem>(id, cfg, readFile(RP_MGB_ROM_PATH));
    s->onActivate(kRate);
    return s;
}

std::unique_ptr<SystemBase> bliptoaster(SystemId id) {
    MesenNesConfig cfg;
    cfg.romPath = RP_BLIPTOASTER_ROM_PATH;
    auto s = std::make_unique<MesenNesSystem>(id, cfg, readFile(RP_BLIPTOASTER_ROM_PATH));
    s->onActivate(kRate);
    return s;
}

// A stand-in kernel, compiled as the control plane compiles the real one: two globals, `processBlock` its body.
void loadKernel(Engine& e, const std::string& processBlock) {
    const auto bc = dsp::compileToBytecode("function setSystems(json) {}\nfunction processBlock(input) {\n" + processBlock + "\n}\n");
    REQUIRE(bc.has_value());
    REQUIRE(e.loadKernel(*bc));
}

// One stereo block; the output, interleaved.
std::vector<float> block(Engine& e, std::uint32_t frames = kFrames) {
    std::vector<float> l(frames), r(frames), out;
    float* outs[2] = {l.data(), r.data()};
    e.processBlock(frames, outs, 2);
    for (std::uint32_t i = 0; i < frames; ++i) {
        out.push_back(l[i]);
        out.push_back(r[i]);
    }
    return out;
}

std::vector<std::uint8_t> noteOn(std::uint8_t key) { return {0x90, key, 100}; }

// A host MIDI-out message as rp.host.midi-out reads it: the emitting system's id, 4 bytes little-endian, then the MIDI.
std::vector<std::uint8_t> tagged(std::uint32_t system, std::vector<std::uint8_t> midi) {
    std::vector<std::uint8_t> out{static_cast<std::uint8_t>(system), static_cast<std::uint8_t>(system >> 8),
                                  static_cast<std::uint8_t>(system >> 16), static_cast<std::uint8_t>(system >> 24)};
    out.insert(out.end(), midi.begin(), midi.end());
    return out;
}

struct Out {
    std::uint32_t             system, frame;
    std::vector<std::uint8_t> data;
    bool operator==(const Out&) const = default;
};
std::vector<Out> midiOut(const Engine& e) {
    std::vector<Out> out;
    for (const auto& m : e.midiOut()) out.push_back({m.system, m.frame, m.data});
    return out;
}

// The host I/O nodes alone, on no systems: `nodes` and `wires`, and the host's stereo pair.
Engine::GraphRequest hostIoOnly(std::vector<std::string> nodes, std::vector<std::string> wires, bool kernel = false) {
    return graphRequest(stereoDocument({}, DocExtras{std::move(nodes), std::move(wires), kernel}), {});
}

// A lone BlipToaster NES rendered for 3.5 s in 1024-frame blocks, MIDI staged by `stage` ahead of each block (with
// the block's first frame): through rp.host.midi-in into its midi input, or through today's path, the kernel stage,
// with a stand-in kernel that forwards every staged message to the NES as core MIDI.
std::vector<float> renderNes(bool viaKernel, const std::function<void(Engine&, std::uint64_t)>& stage) {
    Engine e(kRate);
    REQUIRE(e.parkCore(bliptoaster(1)));
    DocExtras extras;
    extras.kernel = viaKernel;
    if (!viaKernel) {
        extras.nodes = {docNode("midi-in", "rp.host.midi-in")};
        extras.wires = {docWire("midi-in.midi", "sys-1.midi")};
    }
    REQUIRE(e.setGraph(graphRequest(stereoDocument({{1, kNes}}, extras), {1})).ok);
    if (viaKernel)
        loadKernel(e, "for (var i = 0; i < input.midiIn.length; i++) emitCoreMidi(1, input.midiIn[i].frame, input.midiIn[i].data);");
    std::vector<float> out;
    for (std::uint64_t at = 0; at < static_cast<std::uint64_t>(3.5 * kRate); at += kFrames) {
        stage(e, at);
        const auto b = block(e);
        out.insert(out.end(), b.begin(), b.end());
    }
    return out;
}

// The first frame two interleaved stereo renders differ at, or SIZE_MAX.
std::size_t firstDifference(const std::vector<float>& a, const std::vector<float>& b) {
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < a.size() && i < b.size(); ++i)
        if (a[i] != b[i]) return i / 2;
    return a.size() == b.size() ? SIZE_MAX : std::min(a.size(), b.size()) / 2;
}

// `messages` (frame, MIDI) staged ahead of the first block at or past `seconds`.
using Staged = std::vector<std::pair<std::uint32_t, std::vector<std::uint8_t>>>;
std::function<void(Engine&, std::uint64_t)> stageAt(std::vector<std::pair<double, Staged>> plan) {
    return [plan = std::move(plan)](Engine& e, std::uint64_t at) {
        for (const auto& [seconds, messages] : plan) {
            const auto from = static_cast<std::uint64_t>(seconds * kRate);
            if (at < from || at >= from + kFrames) continue;
            for (const auto& [frame, bytes] : messages) e.stageMidi(frame, bytes);
        }
    };
}

}  // namespace

TEST_CASE("rp.host.midi-in hands a NES exactly what today's kernel stage hands it", "[engine-graph][host-io]") {
    // The plugin stages DAW events, then each moved automation slot's CC at frame 0, so a block can be [100, 300, 0].
    // A queue keeps frame order by clamping an earlier frame up, so midi-in sorts first, stably: the NES, whose FIFO
    // stable-sorts by frame, gets the frame-0 note at frame 0, and two frame-0 notes in the order they were staged.
    // BlipToaster plays the last note it is given on a channel, so either order shows. It ignores MIDI for its first
    // second or so (parity/scenes.ts BOOT_MS).
    const Staged ragged{{100, noteOn(60)}, {300, noteOn(62)}, {0, noteOn(64)}};
    const Staged ties{{0, noteOn(67)}, {0, noteOn(69)}};
    const auto viaMidiIn = renderNes(false, stageAt({{1.5, ragged}, {2.5, ties}}));
    const auto today = renderNes(true, stageAt({{1.5, ragged}, {2.5, ties}}));
    CHECK(firstDifference(viaMidiIn, today) == SIZE_MAX);

    // And each order is audible: the frame-0 note clamped behind the others (no sort), or the ties swapped (an
    // unstable one), renders something else from that block on.
    const auto clamped = renderNes(true, stageAt({{1.5, {{100, noteOn(60)}, {300, noteOn(62)}, {300, noteOn(64)}}}, {2.5, ties}}));
    const auto swapped = renderNes(true, stageAt({{1.5, ragged}, {2.5, {{0, noteOn(69)}, {0, noteOn(67)}}}}));
    const auto from = [](double seconds) { return static_cast<std::size_t>(seconds * kRate) / kFrames * kFrames; };
    CHECK(firstDifference(viaMidiIn, clamped) >= from(1.5));
    CHECK(firstDifference(viaMidiIn, clamped) < from(2.5));
    CHECK(firstDifference(viaMidiIn, swapped) >= from(2.5));
    CHECK(firstDifference(viaMidiIn, swapped) != SIZE_MAX);
}

TEST_CASE("rp.host.midi-in sorts and pushes the staged MIDI without allocating", "[engine-graph][host-io]") {
    Engine e(kRate);
    REQUIRE(e.setGraph(hostIoOnly({docNode("midi-in", "rp.host.midi-in")}, {})).ok);
    for (const std::uint32_t frame : {100u, 300u, 0u, 100u, 0u}) e.stageMidi(frame, noteOn(60));
    float l[64], r[64];
    float* outs[2] = {l, r};
    // No warm-up: a sort that allocates on its first call is caught too.
    rp::test::beginCountingAllocations();
    e.processBlock(64, outs, 2);
    const auto counted = rp::test::endCountingAllocations();
    CHECK(counted.allocations == 0);
    // The staged messages' own bytes, freed as the staging is cleared, as the kernel stage frees them today: each
    // staged message owns its bytes (DspRuntime::MidiIn).
    CHECK(counted.frees == 5);
}

TEST_CASE("rp.host.midi-out lands each message in Engine::midiOut, tagged with the system its prefix names",
          "[engine-graph][host-io]") {
    Engine e(kRate);
    REQUIRE(e.setGraph(hostIoOnly({docNode("midi-in", "rp.host.midi-in"), docNode("midi-out", "rp.host.midi-out")},
                                  {docWire("midi-in.midi", "midi-out.midi")}))
                .ok);
    e.stageMidi(7, tagged(2, {0x90, 60, 100}));
    e.stageMidi(9, tagged(513, {0xF8}));
    e.stageMidi(11, {3, 0, 0});  // too short to name a system: dropped
    block(e);
    CHECK(midiOut(e) == std::vector<Out>{{2, 7, {0x90, 60, 100}}, {513, 9, {0xF8}}});
}

TEST_CASE("the kernel stage and the host I/O nodes share the host's buffers, in plan order", "[engine-graph][host-io]") {
    // Both produce what the hosts drain after a block, so the engine starts each block's buffers empty itself and
    // each producer appends as it runs. A plan holding rp.host.midi-in or controller-in takes what is staged, so the
    // kernel stage then gets none of it. The stand-in kernel reports how many messages it was handed.
    const std::string kernel =
        "emitMidiOut(7, 3, [input.midiIn.length]);\n"
        "emitControllerOut([0xB0, 0, input.controllerIn ? input.controllerIn.length : 0]);";
    const auto controllerOut = [](const Engine& e) { return e.controllerOut(); };
    using Bytes = std::vector<std::vector<std::uint8_t>>;

    SECTION("with the host I/O nodes") {
        Engine e(kRate);
        REQUIRE(e.setGraph(hostIoOnly({docNode("midi-in", "rp.host.midi-in"), docNode("midi-out", "rp.host.midi-out"),
                                       docNode("controller-in", "rp.host.controller-in"),
                                       docNode("controller-out", "rp.host.controller-out")},
                                      {docWire("midi-in.midi", "midi-out.midi"), docWire("controller-in.midi", "controller-out.midi")},
                                      true))
                    .ok);
        loadKernel(e, kernel);
        e.stageMidi(4, tagged(5, {0xF8}));
        e.stageControllerMidi({0x90, 11, 127});
        block(e);
        CHECK(midiOut(e) == std::vector<Out>{{7, 3, {0}}, {5, 4, {0xF8}}});
        CHECK(controllerOut(e) == Bytes{{0xB0, 0, 0}, {0x90, 11, 127}});
        // Nothing staged, and nothing drained in between: the next block starts from empty buffers all the same.
        block(e);
        CHECK(midiOut(e) == std::vector<Out>{{7, 3, {0}}});
        CHECK(controllerOut(e) == Bytes{{0xB0, 0, 0}});
    }
    SECTION("with the kernel after them in plan order") {
        Engine e(kRate);
        REQUIRE(e.setGraph(hostIoOnly({docNode("midi-in", "rp.host.midi-in"), docNode("midi-out", "rp.host.midi-out"),
                                       docNode("kernel", "rp.dsp.kernel")},
                                      {docWire("midi-in.midi", "midi-out.midi")}))
                    .ok);
        loadKernel(e, kernel);
        e.stageMidi(4, tagged(5, {0xF8}));
        block(e);
        CHECK(midiOut(e) == std::vector<Out>{{5, 4, {0xF8}}, {7, 3, {0}}});
    }
    SECTION("without them, the kernel stage gets what is staged, as today") {
        Engine e(kRate);
        REQUIRE(e.setGraph(hostIoOnly({}, {}, true)).ok);
        loadKernel(e, kernel);
        e.stageMidi(0, {0xF8});
        e.stageMidi(0, {0xFA});
        e.stageControllerMidi({0x90, 11, 127});
        block(e);
        CHECK(midiOut(e) == std::vector<Out>{{7, 3, {2}}});
        CHECK(controllerOut(e) == Bytes{{0xB0, 0, 1}});
    }
}

TEST_CASE("rp.host.controller-in's connected output follows the engine's flag from frame 0", "[engine-graph][host-io]") {
    using rp::host::test::NodeRig;
    using rp::host::test::Probe;
    NodeRig rig(kRate);
    REQUIRE(rig.set(R"({"nodes":[{"id":"surface","type":"rp.host.controller-in"},{"id":"probe","type":"rp.test.probe"}],
                        "wires":[{"from":"surface.connected","to":"probe.control"}]})")
                .ok);
    Probe& probe = rig.node<Probe>("probe");
    const rp_transport t{kRate, 120.0, 0.0, 0};
    const auto run = [&](bool connected) {
        rig.connected = connected;
        rig.host->processBlock(64, t);
    };
    run(false);
    CHECK(probe.controlAtZero == 0.0);
    CHECK(probe.controlChanges.empty());
    run(true);  // the block it is attached: a change at frame 0
    CHECK(probe.controlAtZero == 1.0);
    CHECK(probe.controlChanges == std::vector<double>{1.0});
    run(true);  // then the value holds, with no change
    CHECK(probe.controlStart == 1.0);
    CHECK(probe.controlChanges.empty());
    run(false);
    CHECK(probe.controlAtZero == 0.0);
}

TEST_CASE("rp.n8.cart-mirror hands the cart every MIDI message, then every byte message, in queue order",
          "[engine-graph][host-io][n8]") {
    using rp::host::test::Feed;
    using rp::host::test::HostCall;
    using rp::host::test::NodeRig;
    NodeRig rig(kRate);
    REQUIRE(rig.set(R"({"nodes":[{"id":"feed","type":"rp.test.feed"},{"id":"cart","type":"rp.n8.cart-mirror","settings":{"system":1}}],
                        "wires":[{"from":"feed.midi","to":"cart.midi"},{"from":"feed.bytes","to":"cart.bytes"}]})")
                .ok);
    Feed& feed = rig.node<Feed>("feed");
    feed.next[Feed::Midi] = {{3, {0x90, 1, 100}}, {8, {}}, {8, {0x80, 1, 0}}};  // the empty one is skipped, as today
    feed.next[Feed::Bytes] = {{1, {0xF2, 0, 0}, RP_MESSAGE_FLUSH}, {5, {0xF8}}};
    rig.host->processBlock(64, rp_transport{kRate, 120.0, 0.0, 0});
    REQUIRE(rig.cart.size() == 4);
    const auto is = [](const HostCall& c, std::uint32_t frame, std::vector<std::uint8_t> data, bool flush) {
        return c.frame == frame && c.data == data && c.flush == flush;
    };
    CHECK(is(rig.cart[0], 3, {0x90, 1, 100}, false));
    CHECK(is(rig.cart[1], 8, {0x80, 1, 0}, false));
    CHECK(is(rig.cart[2], 1, {0xF2, 0, 0}, true));
    CHECK(is(rig.cart[3], 5, {0xF8}, false));
}

TEST_CASE("the engine feeds the cart mirror to its core-byte sink, and reads the system it mirrors off the plan",
          "[engine-graph][host-io][n8]") {
    Engine e(kRate);
    REQUIRE(e.parkCore(bliptoaster(1)));
    const auto mirrored = [](std::string settings) {
        return DocExtras{{docNode("midi-in", "rp.host.midi-in"), docNode("cart", "rp.n8.cart-mirror", std::move(settings))},
                         {docWire("midi-in.midi", "cart.midi")}};
    };
    CHECK(e.cartMirrorSystemId() == 0);
    REQUIRE(e.setGraph(graphRequest(stereoDocument({{1, kNes}}, mirrored(R"({"system":1})")), {1})).ok);
    CHECK(e.cartMirrorSystemId() == 1);

    // With no sink (the CLI, the tests), nothing goes anywhere.
    e.stageMidi(0, noteOn(1));
    block(e);
    std::vector<std::pair<std::uint32_t, std::vector<std::uint8_t>>> cart;
    e.setCoreByteSink([&](std::uint32_t frame, const std::uint8_t* d, std::size_t n, bool) { cart.push_back({frame, {d, d + n}}); });
    e.stageMidi(5, noteOn(2));
    block(e);
    REQUIRE(cart.size() == 1);
    CHECK(cart[0].first == 5);
    CHECK(cart[0].second == noteOn(2));

    // One mirror at most, naming one of the document's systems; and none is 0.
    auto two = mirrored(R"({"system":1})");
    two.nodes.push_back(docNode("cart-2", "rp.n8.cart-mirror", R"({"system":1})"));
    auto refused = e.setGraph(graphRequest(stereoDocument({{1, kNes}}, two), {1}));
    REQUIRE_FALSE(refused.ok);
    CHECK(refused.errors.at(0).code == "cart-mirror");
    refused = e.setGraph(graphRequest(stereoDocument({{1, kNes}}, mirrored(R"({"system":9})")), {1}));
    REQUIRE_FALSE(refused.ok);
    CHECK(refused.errors.at(0).code == "cart-mirror");
    CHECK(e.cartMirrorSystemId() == 1);
    REQUIRE(e.setGraph(graphRequest(stereoDocument({{1, kNes}}), {1})).ok);
    CHECK(e.cartMirrorSystemId() == 0);
}

TEST_CASE("the Game Boy's serialOut carries what its core captured, and the engine's MI.OUT gather still does",
          "[engine-graph][host-io]") {
    // mGB, with MI.OUT capture armed, has a byte clocked out of its serial port every eight frames (it holds the
    // port in external-clock receive). The port carries this block's bytes at frame 0, here into a cart mirror whose
    // sink records them; the gather hands the same bytes to the kernel stage next block, which a stand-in kernel
    // echoes as host MIDI out.
    Engine e(kRate);
    auto core = mgb(1);
    core->setSerialOutCapture(true);
    SameBoySystem* const gb = core.get();
    REQUIRE(e.parkCore(std::move(core)));
    DocExtras extras{{docNode("cart", "rp.n8.cart-mirror", R"({"system":1})")}, {docWire("sys-1.serialOut", "cart.bytes")}};
    REQUIRE(e.setGraph(graphRequest(stereoDocument({{1, kGb}}, extras), {1})).ok);
    loadKernel(e, "for (var i = 0; i < input.serialOut.length; i++) emitMidiOut(input.serialOut[i].system, 0, [input.serialOut[i].byte]);");
    std::vector<std::uint8_t> carried;
    bool eachAtZero = true;
    e.setCoreByteSink([&](std::uint32_t frame, const std::uint8_t* d, std::size_t n, bool) {
        eachAtZero = eachAtZero && frame == 0 && n == 1;
        carried.insert(carried.end(), d, d + n);
    });
    std::vector<std::uint8_t> last;  // what the core captured last block
    std::size_t captured = 0;
    for (int b = 0; b < 100; ++b) {
        carried.clear();
        block(e);
        std::vector<std::uint8_t> log, gathered;
        for (const auto& entry : gb->serialOutLog_) log.push_back(entry.second);
        for (const auto& m : e.midiOut()) {
            CHECK(m.system == 1);
            gathered.insert(gathered.end(), m.data.begin(), m.data.end());
        }
        INFO("block " << b);
        CHECK(carried == log);
        CHECK(gathered == last);
        last = log;
        captured += log.size();
    }
    CHECK(eachAtZero);
    CHECK(captured > 0);
}

TEST_CASE("a full output queue's drops reach the engine and the harness facet", "[engine-graph][host-io]") {
    Engine           e(kRate);
    SystemFactory    factory;
    QueuedInvoker    invoker(e);
    EngineRpcService rpc(e, factory, invoker);
    REQUIRE(e.setGraph(hostIoOnly({docNode("midi-in", "rp.host.midi-in"), docNode("midi-out", "rp.host.midi-out")},
                                  {docWire("midi-in.midi", "midi-out.midi")}))
                .ok);
    for (int i = 0; i < 3; ++i) e.stageMidi(0, tagged(1, {0xF8}));
    block(e);
    CHECK(e.droppedMessages() == 0);
    CHECK(rpc.droppedMessages() == 0);
    // One block's worth more than midi-in's port holds.
    for (std::uint32_t i = 0; i < rp::host::kHostMidiInMessages + 3; ++i) e.stageMidi(0, tagged(1, {0xF8}));
    block(e);
    CHECK(e.midiOut().size() == rp::host::kHostMidiInMessages);
    CHECK(e.droppedMessages() == 3);
    CHECK(rpc.droppedMessages() == 3);
}
````

````diff
+        send();
+        sent = true;

+            direct->pushCoreBytes(0, kNoteOn60.data(), kNoteOn60.size(), false);
+            direct->pushCoreBytes(10, kNoteOff72.data(), kNoteOff72.size(), true);
+        });
+        auto second = once(2.5, [&] {
+            feed.next[Feed::Bytes].push_back({0, kNoteOn64});
+            direct->pushCoreBytes(0, kNoteOn64.data(), kNoteOn64.size(), false);
+        });
+        CHECK(compare(rig, d, 3.5, [&](std::uint64_t at) { first(at); second(at); }, &c, &heard) == "");
+        CHECK(heard >= static_cast<std::uint64_t>(2.5 * kRate));
+        CHECK(heard != kNever);
+    }
+    SECTION("buttons: [button, down] through pressButton") {
+        NodeRig rig(kRate);
+        auto direct = sms(1), control = sms(1);
+        auto viaGraph = sms(1);
+        SystemBase* graphCore = viaGraph.get();
+        REQUIRE(rig.set(fedDocument("rp.mesen.sms", rig.park(std::move(viaGraph)), {"buttons"})).ok);
+        Feed& feed = rig.node<Feed>("feed");
+        Direct d({direct.get()}, 2, {{0, 1}}), c({control.get()}, 2, {{0, 1}});
+        // smsStart's song in every core, its PAUSE held (through the input, for the graph core) only where it plays.
+        const auto pause = static_cast<std::uint8_t>(SmsButton::Start);
+        auto start = once(3.0, [&] {
+            for (SystemBase* s : {static_cast<SystemBase*>(direct.get()), graphCore, static_cast<SystemBase*>(control.get())})
+                pokeMetronome(*s);
+            feed.next[Feed::Buttons].push_back({0, {pause, 1}});
+            direct->pressButton(pause, true);
+        });
+        auto release = once(3.6, [&] {
+            feed.next[Feed::Buttons].push_back({0, {pause, 0}});
+            direct->pressButton(pause, false);
+        });
+        CHECK(compare(rig, d, 5.0, [&](std::uint64_t at) { start(at); release(at); }, &c, &heard) == "");
+        CHECK(heard != kNever);
+    }
+    SECTION("in fan-out order: midi before bytes, so a flushed message drops the MIDI queued ahead of it") {
+        // The one order a core can show: on the NES both land in the N8 FIFO. serialIn goes first and buttons last,
+        // as the kernel stage fans them out, but no core takes two of those in one queue.
+        NodeRig rig(kRate);
+        auto direct = nes(1, 0), control = nes(1, 0);
+        REQUIRE(rig.set(fedDocument("rp.mesen.nes", rig.park(nes(1, 0)), {"midi", "bytes"})).ok);
+        Feed& feed = rig.node<Feed>("feed");
+        Direct d({direct.get()}, 2, {{0, 1}}), c({control.get()}, 2, {{0, 1}});
+        auto first = once(1.5, [&] {
+            feed.next[Feed::Midi].push_back({0, kNoteOn60});
+            feed.next[Feed::Bytes].push_back({0, kNoteOff72, RP_MESSAGE_FLUSH});
+            const ::MidiEvent ev = midiEvent(0, kNoteOn60);
+            direct->onMidi(&ev, 1);
+            direct->pushCoreBytes(0, kNoteOff72.data(), kNoteOff72.size(), true);
+        });
+        auto second = once(2.5, [&] {
+            feed.next[Feed::Midi].push_back({0, kNoteOn64});
+            const ::MidiEvent ev = midiEvent(0, kNoteOn64);
+            direct->onMidi(&ev, 1);
+        });
+        CHECK(compare(rig, d, 3.5, [&](std::uint64_t at) { first(at); second(at); }, &c, &heard) == "");
+        CHECK(heard >= static_cast<std::uint64_t>(2.5 * kRate));
+        CHECK(heard != kNever);
+    }
+}
+
+TEST_CASE("a linked Game Boy takes its inputs in prepare, before its group steps", "[engine-graph][system-node][inputs]") {
+    // A coupled member is never processed, only prepared, stepped and finished, so its inputs are applied at the top
+    // of prepare. Seen in the core's queues right after the block: a linked core's serial port belongs to the cable,
+    // so the byte is still queued; the press was taken while the group stepped, so it was queued before the first step.
+    NodeRig rig(kRate);
+    auto d1 = mgb(1), d2 = mgb(2);
+    d1->linkPeers_ = {d2.get()};
+    d2->linkPeers_ = {d1.get()};
+    auto g1 = mgb(1);
+    SameBoySystem* const graph1 = g1.get();
+    const auto t1 = rig.park(std::move(g1)), t2 = rig.park(mgb(2));
+    REQUIRE(rig.set(R"({"nodes":[{"id":"feed","type":"rp.test.feed"},{"id":"a","type":"rp.sameboy.gb","settings":{"core":)" +
+                    std::to_string(t1) + R"(}},{"id":"b","type":"rp.sameboy.gb","settings":{"core":)" + std::to_string(t2) +
+                    R"(}},{"id":"out","type":"rp.host.audio-out","settings":{"buses":[2,2]}}],"wires":[
+                        {"from":"a.link","to":"b.link"},{"from":"a.mix","to":"out.out.1-2"},{"from":"b.mix","to":"out.out.3-4"},
+                        {"from":"feed.serialIn","to":"a.serialIn"},{"from":"feed.buttons","to":"a.buttons"}]})")
+                .ok);
+    Feed& feed = rig.node<Feed>("feed");
+    Direct d({d1.get(), d2.get()}, 4, {{0, 1}, {2, 3}});
+    Lanes graph(4);
+    const rp_transport t{kRate, 120.0, 0.0, 0};
+    const auto start = static_cast<std::uint8_t>(GameboyButton::Start);
+    for (int b = 0; b < 48; ++b) {
+        const bool send = b == 40;
+        if (send) {
+            feed.next[Feed::SerialIn].push_back({0, {0x90}});
+            feed.next[Feed::Buttons].push_back({0, {start, 1}});
+            d1->pushSerialIn(0, 0x90);
+            d1->pressButton(start, true);
+        }
+        rig.host->processBlock(1024, t, graph.ptrs.data(), 4);
+        d.block(1024);
+        for (std::size_t c = 0; c < 4; ++c) REQUIRE(std::memcmp(graph.data[c].data(), d.out.data[c].data(), 1024 * sizeof(float)) == 0);
+        if (!send) continue;
+        REQUIRE(graph1->serialIn_.size() == 1);
+        REQUIRE(d1->serialIn_.size() == 1);
+        CHECK(graph1->serialIn_.front().byte == 0x90);
+        CHECK(graph1->serialIn_.front().offset == d1->serialIn_.front().offset);
+        CHECK(graph1->pendingButtons_.empty());
+        CHECK(d1->pendingButtons_.empty());
+    }
+}
+
+TEST_CASE("the Game Boy's serialOut carries what its core captured this block, at frame 0, and leaves the log",
+          "[engine-graph][system-node][inputs]") {
+    // mGB holds its serial port in external-clock receive, so once MI.OUT capture is armed the engine clocks a byte
+    // out of it every eight frames. The node copies the core's log rather than draining it: the engine's MI.OUT
+    // gather reads the same log after the plan, and the core clears it at its next prepareForBlock.
+    NodeRig rig(kRate);
+    auto core = mgb(1);
+    core->setSerialOutCapture(true);
+    SameBoySystem* const gb = core.get();
+    REQUIRE(rig.set(R"({"nodes":[{"id":"gb","type":"rp.sameboy.gb","settings":{"core":)" + std::to_string(rig.park(std::move(core))) +
+                    R"(}},{"id":"probe","type":"rp.test.probe"},{"id":"out","type":"rp.host.audio-out","settings":{"buses":[2]}}],
+                        "wires":[{"from":"gb.mix","to":"out.out.1-2"},{"from":"gb.serialOut","to":"probe.bytes"}]})")
+                .ok);
+    Probe& probe = rig.node<Probe>("probe");
+    Lanes graph(2);
+    const rp_transport t{kRate, 120.0, 0.0, 0};
+    std::size_t captured = 0;
+    for (std::size_t b = 0; b < 160; ++b) {
+        const std::uint32_t frames = kBlocks[b % kBlocks.size()];
+        rig.host->processBlock(frames, t, graph.ptrs.data(), 2);
+        std::vector<std::uint8_t> log, carried;
+        for (const auto& entry : gb->serialOutLog_) log.push_back(entry.second);
+        bool eachAtZero = true;
+        for (const auto& m : probe.bytes) {
+            eachAtZero = eachAtZero && m.frame == 0 && m.data.size() == 1;
+            if (!m.data.empty()) carried.push_back(m.data[0]);
+        }
+        INFO("block " << b);
+        CHECK(eachAtZero);
+        CHECK(carried == log);
+        captured += log.size();
+    }
+    CHECK(captured > 0);
+}
+
+TEST_CASE("a system node records what its bytes input feeds the core in the engine's sync trace", "[engine-graph][system-node][inputs]") {
+    // As the kernel stage records its core-bytes sink: the bytes input only, an empty message skipped, and a long
+    // MIDI message (which also goes down the core's byte path) not at all.
+    NodeRig rig(kRate);
+    REQUIRE(rig.set(fedDocument("rp.mesen.nes", rig.park(nes(1, 0)), {"midi", "bytes"})).ok);
+    Feed& feed = rig.node<Feed>("feed");
+    feed.next[Feed::Bytes] = {{5, {1, 2, 3}}, {7, {}}};
+    feed.next[Feed::Midi] = {{0, {0x90, 60, 100, 0x90, 64, 100}}};
+    Lanes graph(2);
+    const rp_transport t{kRate, 120.0, 0.0, 0};
+    rig.host->processBlock(64, t, graph.ptrs.data(), 2);
+    REQUIRE(rig.traced.size() == 1);
+    CHECK(rig.traced[0].frame == 5);
+    CHECK(rig.traced[0].data == std::vector<std::uint8_t>{1, 2, 3});
+}
````

````cpp
#pragma once

#include <cstdint>

#include "graph/rp_node.h"

namespace rp::host {

// The engine's host I/O nodes (docs/modular-graph-phase-b3a-design.md section 3.3), each over the engine's
// rp.engine.host-io/1 service, without which it will not activate:
//
//   rp.host.midi-in         out midi: the host MIDI the engine staged, stable-sorted by frame
//   rp.host.midi-out        in midi: each message's payload is a 4-byte little-endian system id, then the MIDI,
//                           which lands in Engine::midiOut tagged with that system (section 4.4)
//   rp.host.controller-in   out midi: the staged control-surface MIDI, at frame 0; out connected: 1 while a
//                           control surface is attached, from frame 0 of the block
//   rp.host.controller-out  in midi: appended to Engine::controllerOut
//
// The host keeps staging and draining as it does; each input node takes what is staged at the top of its block.
const rp_package* hostIoPackage();

// rp.n8.cart-mirror (section 3.5), {"system": <id>}: everything on its midi input, then everything on its bytes
// input (each with its flush flag), handed to the physical N8 the engine feeds, in queue order. The system it names
// is the one the cart mirrors, which the engine reads off the plan.
const rp_package* n8Package();

// rp.host.midi-in's output: room for a dense block of DAW MIDI, the frame-0 CCs of moved automation and a SysEx
// (a wave upload), with margin. A message past it is dropped and counted (GraphHost::droppedMessages).
inline constexpr std::uint32_t kHostMidiInMessages = 2048;
inline constexpr std::uint32_t kHostMidiInBytes = 32768;
// rp.host.controller-in's: a Launchpad's pad traffic and its replies.
inline constexpr std::uint32_t kControllerInMessages = 1024;
inline constexpr std::uint32_t kControllerInBytes = 16384;

}  // namespace rp::host
````

Create `packages/native/src/host/graph/HostIoNodes.cpp`:

````cpp
#include "host/graph/HostIoNodes.hpp"

#include <cstdint>
#include <iterator>
#include <optional>
#include <string>

#include "graph/node.hpp"
#include "host/graph/HostServices.hpp"

namespace rp::host {

// Named, so its JSON Schema $defs key is the same under every compiler.
struct CartMirrorSettings {
    // The system the cart mirrors (a system id, as a system node's {"core": <id>}).
    std::uint64_t system = 0;
};

namespace {

// Every node here needs the engine's host I/O, so none activates without it.
struct HostIoNode {
    const EngineHostIo* io = nullptr;
    void bind_host(const rp_host* h) noexcept {
        io = static_cast<const EngineHostIo*>(h->get_interface(h, RP_ENGINE_HOST_IO_INTERFACE));
    }
    bool activate(double, std::uint32_t) { return io != nullptr; }
};

struct MidiIn : HostIoNode {
    static constexpr const char* id = "rp.host.midi-in";
    static constexpr const char* name = "MIDI In";
    static constexpr const char* category = "host";
    struct {
        rp::events_out::sized<rp::capacity{.messages = kHostMidiInMessages, .bytes = kHostMidiInBytes}> midi;
    } outputs;
    void process(const rp::Block&) noexcept { io->takeMidi(io->ctx, outputs.midi.queue); }
};

// The emitting system's id, little-endian, ahead of each message's MIDI (design section 4.4): private to the
// kernel's one midiOut port and this node, until each protocol node has a port of its own.
constexpr std::size_t kSystemPrefix = 4;

struct MidiOut : HostIoNode {
    static constexpr const char* id = "rp.host.midi-out";
    static constexpr const char* name = "MIDI Out";
    static constexpr const char* category = "host";
    struct { rp::events_in midi; } inputs;
    void process(const rp::Block&) noexcept {
        for (const rp_message& m : inputs.midi.messages()) {
            const auto data = inputs.midi.data(m);
            if (data.size() < kSystemPrefix) continue;  // names no system
            const std::uint32_t system = std::uint32_t{data[0]} | std::uint32_t{data[1]} << 8 |
                                         std::uint32_t{data[2]} << 16 | std::uint32_t{data[3]} << 24;
            io->midiOut(io->ctx, system, m.frame, data.data() + kSystemPrefix, data.size() - kSystemPrefix);
        }
    }
};

struct ControllerIn : HostIoNode {
    static constexpr const char* id = "rp.host.controller-in";
    static constexpr const char* name = "Control Surface In";
    static constexpr const char* category = "host";
    struct {
        rp::events_out::sized<rp::capacity{.messages = kControllerInMessages, .bytes = kControllerInBytes}> midi;
        rp::control_out connected;
    } outputs;
    // `connected` holds 1 or 0 from frame 0: a change at frame 0 on the block the flag flips, since a stream's start
    // value is the last block's end.
    void process(const rp::Block&) noexcept {
        io->takeControllerMidi(io->ctx, outputs.midi.queue);
        const double connected = io->controllerConnected(io->ctx) ? 1.0 : 0.0;
        if (connected != outputs.connected.queue->start) outputs.connected.push(0, connected);
    }
};

struct ControllerOut : HostIoNode {
    static constexpr const char* id = "rp.host.controller-out";
    static constexpr const char* name = "Control Surface Out";
    static constexpr const char* category = "host";
    struct { rp::events_in midi; } inputs;
    void process(const rp::Block&) noexcept {
        for (const rp_message& m : inputs.midi.messages()) {
            const auto data = inputs.midi.data(m);
            io->controllerOut(io->ctx, data.data(), data.size());
        }
    }
};

// What the cart mirror's system's FIFO is fed, in the order the kernel stage feeds it today: its MIDI, then its
// bytes, each in queue order. An empty message is skipped, as the kernel stage skips it.
struct CartMirror : HostIoNode {
    static constexpr const char* id = "rp.n8.cart-mirror";
    static constexpr const char* name = "N8 Cart Mirror";
    static constexpr const char* category = "host";
    using Settings = CartMirrorSettings;
    // Its settings change nothing it does (the engine reads them off the document), so a change is a swap, and its
    // prepare reads nothing a commit writes.
    static constexpr bool stateless_prepare = true;
    struct {
        rp::events_in midi;
        rp::bytes_in  bytes;
    } inputs;

    static std::optional<std::string> validate(const Settings& s) {
        if (s.system == 0 || s.system > UINT32_MAX) return "system names the system the cart mirrors: 1 to 4294967295";
        return std::nullopt;
    }

    void process(const rp::Block&) noexcept {
        for (const rp_message& m : inputs.midi.messages()) {
            const auto data = inputs.midi.data(m);
            if (!data.empty()) io->cartBytes(io->ctx, m.frame, data.data(), data.size(), false);
        }
        for (const rp_message& m : inputs.bytes.messages()) {
            const auto data = inputs.bytes.data(m);
            if (!data.empty()) io->cartBytes(io->ctx, m.frame, data.data(), data.size(), (m.flags & RP_MESSAGE_FLUSH) != 0);
        }
    }
};

}  // namespace

const rp_package* hostIoPackage() {
    static const rp_node_type* const kTypes[] = {rp::node_type<MidiIn>(), rp::node_type<MidiOut>(), rp::node_type<ControllerIn>(),
                                                 rp::node_type<ControllerOut>()};
    static const rp_package kPackage{RP_ABI_VERSION, R"({"id":"rp.host.io","version":"1.0.0"})",
                                     static_cast<std::uint32_t>(std::size(kTypes)), kTypes};
    return &kPackage;
}

const rp_package* n8Package() {
    static const rp_node_type* const kTypes[] = {rp::node_type<CartMirror>()};
    static const rp_package kPackage{RP_ABI_VERSION, R"({"id":"rp.n8","version":"1.0.0"})",
                                     static_cast<std::uint32_t>(std::size(kTypes)), kTypes};
    return &kPackage;
}

}  // namespace rp::host
````

---

### Task 5: The script-node runtime

The runtime that runs TS nodes behind the same C ABI as native ones (design section 2), beside today's path: the
kernel still runs in `DspRuntime` through the native `rp.dsp.kernel`, the production bundle registers no node yet,
and parity does not move. It is built in three parts, each red then green.

**The ABI's type context.** The type-level calls had no hint of the type they were called through, so one set of
functions could not serve several types, which the script host's one type per definition needs. `descriptor`,
`layout_for`, `query_memory` and `create` now take the `const rp_node_type*` first, and `rp_node_type` gains a
trailing `ctx`, null for a C++ node and never read by the host.

**The TS side.** A bundle registers its `defineNode` results by appending them to the global `__rp_scriptNodes`
(`src/script/register.ts`). `defineNode` gains `reshapes` and `faultOnThrow` (true or absent), `NodeInstance.onSettings`,
and a refused setting names its first issue on one line (an `rp_error` holds 256 bytes), not zod's JSON.

**The script host** (`src/host/script`, one per Engine): an audio-side bare QuickJS runtime holding every instance,
entered only by the thread that runs blocks, and a control-side one answering `layout_for` and `prepare_settings`
with the definition's `parseSettings` and `layout`; both load the same bundle, and each definition becomes an
`rp_node_type` in one package, `rp.script`, declaring `RP_TYPE_STATELESS_PREPARE`. The shim's `create` and `activate`
only allocate it; the JS instance is made on the block thread at the first call the shim gets there (the
`ports_changed` every fresh instance gets when its plan is adopted), and `destroy` hands the record to the script
host, which releases it at once while quiescent and otherwise on an SPSC ring drained by the next block's
`beginBlock`, the record going back to the control thread on a second ring to be deleted. A reshaping type answers
`RP_PREPARE_RESHAPE` for every change its definition accepts; any other `RP_PREPARE_SWAP` while its layout is the
one it was created with and `RP_PREPARE_REBUILD` once it moves. The `Block`: `messages()` a reused `Message[]`
(payloads copied into one JS-owned buffer per port, each view remade only when its message's place moves),
`control()` a reused `{ start, changes }`, `audio()` `Float32Array` views over the plan's buffers with no copy,
`send()` and `emit()` straight into the plan's queues (`graph::reserveMessage` for an array of numbers); ports are
found by id through atoms bound at creation or reshape, so a warm block allocates nothing native, and a node written
with indexed loops nothing in JS. A throw is caught and counted (`Engine::scriptThrows`), the first kept and logged
at `reclaim`, and the node runs on; `faultOnThrow`, or returning `"fault"`, faults it. The bundle,
`src/script/bundle.ts`, is compiled to global-code bytecode by `retroplug-script-bundle` (esbuild IIFE, `tjsc`
without `-m`, as the render worker is) and embedded in `retroplug-backend`; every Engine loads it at construction,
and `Engine(sampleRate, chunks)` loads another instead. Its test-only twin, `test/script/scriptTestBundle.ts`, is
embedded in `retroplug-engine-graph-test` alone: the authoring layer for toy nodes the tests write as JS source.

````diff
+// Two node types served by ONE set of functions, as the script host serves every type a bundle defines: each

+struct SharedType {

+    float       value;

+const SharedType kSharedB{R"({"id":"rp.test.shared-b"})", 3.0f};
+const SharedType& sharedOf(const rp_node_type* type) { return *static_cast<const SharedType*>(type->ctx); }
+const char* sharedDescriptor(const rp_node_type* type) { return sharedOf(type).descriptor; }
+std::size_t sharedLayout(const rp_node_type* type, const rp_settings* s, char* out, std::size_t capacity, rp_error* err) {
+    return rp::node_type<test::Source>()->layout_for(type, s, out, capacity, err);

+bool sharedMemory(const rp_node_type* type, const rp_settings* s, rp_memory_req* out, rp_error* err) {

+rp_node* sharedCreate(const rp_node_type* type, const rp_host* host, void* memory, const rp_settings* s, rp_error* err) {
+    rp_node* n = rp::node_type<test::Source>()->create(type, host, memory, s, err);
+    if (n) rp::peer_as<test::Source>(n)->value = sharedOf(type).value;
+    return n;
+}
+
+const rp_package* sharedPackage() {

+    static const rp_node_type b{"rp.test.shared-b", &sharedDescriptor, &sharedLayout, &sharedMemory, &sharedCreate,
+                                rp::node_type<test::Source>()->destroy, 0u, const_cast<SharedType*>(&kSharedB)};
+    static const rp_node_type* const kTypes[] = {&a, &b};
+    static const rp_package kPackage{RP_ABI_VERSION, R"({"id":"rp.test.shared"})", 2, kTypes};
+    return &kPackage;
+}
````

Create `packages/retroplug/src/script/register.ts`:

````ts
// How a script-node bundle hands its node definitions to the native script host
// (docs/modular-graph-phase-b3a-design.md section 2.5): it appends them to one global, which the host reads once
// the bundle has run, in each of its two contexts. A bundle loaded in several chunks (a test's toolkit, then its
// toy nodes) appends from each.
import type { DefinedNode } from "../graph/defineNode";

/** The global packages/native/src/host/script/ScriptHost.cpp reads: every definition, in registration order. */
export const SCRIPT_NODES_GLOBAL = "__rp_scriptNodes";

export function registerScriptNodes(nodes: readonly DefinedNode<any>[]): void {
  const g = globalThis as Record<string, unknown>;
  const list = (g[SCRIPT_NODES_GLOBAL] ??= []) as DefinedNode<any>[];
  list.push(...nodes);
}
````

````ts
// Each message on `in`, `copies` times on `out`, its second byte moved by the `transpose` param.
const echo = defineNode({
  id: "rp.test.script-echo",
  settings: z.object({ copies: z.number().int().min(1).max(4).default(1) }),
  ports: { in: events.in(), out: events.out() },
````

Create `packages/native/test/engine-graph/ScriptRig.hpp`:

````cpp
#pragma once

// A GraphHost carrying the core and host packages, both test packages (the graph tests' sources and sinks, and the
// engine tests' feed and probe) and a ScriptHost's script types. The script host is loaded with the test bundle
// (packages/retroplug/test/script/scriptTestBundle.ts: the authoring layer as a global `rp`, and a node of its own)
// and then with toy nodes the test writes as JS source, compiled by the control plane's compiler, so no toy ships.
//
// Two probes are bound into both of the script host's contexts, so a toy can say what ran where: `__probe(tag)`
// records the tag and the calling thread, and `__token(tag)` returns an object that records "released <tag>" and the
// thread that frees it, which is the thread that released the instance holding it.

#include <chrono>
#include <cstdint>
#include <memory>
#include <mutex>
#include <span>
#include <stdexcept>
#include <string>
#include <thread>
#include <utility>
#include <vector>

extern "C" {
#include "quickjs.h"
}

#include "../graph/TestNodes.hpp"
#include "TestNodes.hpp"
#include "graph/GraphHost.hpp"
#include "graph/HostNodes.hpp"
#include "graph/nodes/CoreNodes.hpp"
#include "host/dsp/ScriptCompiler.hpp"
#include "host/script/ScriptHost.hpp"

extern "C" {
extern const std::uint8_t  rp_script_test_bundle[];
extern const std::uint32_t rp_script_test_bundle_size;
}

namespace rp::host::test {

inline ScriptHost::Chunk scriptTestBundle() { return {rp_script_test_bundle, rp_script_test_bundle_size}; }

// A toy bundle's source as bytecode, as the control plane compiles a script.
inline std::vector<std::uint8_t> compileToys(const std::string& source) {
    auto bytecode = dsp::compileToBytecode(source);
    if (!bytecode) throw std::runtime_error("the toy source does not compile");
    return *bytecode;
}

// What the probes recorded, in order.
struct ProbeLog {
    std::mutex                                           mutex;
    std::vector<std::pair<std::string, std::thread::id>> calls;
    JSClassID                                            tokenClass[2] = {0, 0};  // control side, audio side

    void add(std::string tag) {
        const std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(mutex);
        calls.emplace_back(std::move(tag), std::this_thread::get_id());
    }
    std::vector<std::thread::id> threadsOf(const std::string& tag) {
        const std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(mutex);
        std::vector<std::thread::id> out;
        for (const auto& [t, id] : calls)
            if (t == tag) out.push_back(id);
        return out;
    }
    int count(const std::string& tag) { return static_cast<int>(threadsOf(tag).size()); }
    // Until `tag` has been recorded `n` times, for at most a few seconds (the block thread is someone else).
    bool waitFor(const std::string& tag, int n = 1) {
        const auto deadline = std::chrono::steady_clock::now() + std::chrono::seconds(5);
        while (count(tag) < n)
            if (std::chrono::steady_clock::now() > deadline) return false;
            else std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::microseconds(200));
        return true;
    }
};

struct Token {
    ProbeLog*   log;
    std::string tag;
};

inline ProbeLog* logOf(JSContext* ctx, JSValueConst data) {
    std::int64_t p = 0;
    JS_ToInt64(ctx, &p, data);
    return reinterpret_cast<ProbeLog*>(static_cast<std::intptr_t>(p));
}

inline std::string tagOf(JSContext* ctx, int argc, JSValueConst* argv) {
    const char* s = argc > 0 ? JS_ToCString(ctx, argv[0]) : nullptr;
    std::string tag = s ? s : "";
    if (s) JS_FreeCString(ctx, s);
    return tag;
}

inline JSValue probeFn(JSContext* ctx, JSValueConst, int argc, JSValueConst* argv, int, JSValueConst* data) {
    logOf(ctx, data[0])->add(tagOf(ctx, argc, argv));
    return JS_UNDEFINED;
}

inline JSValue tokenFn(JSContext* ctx, JSValueConst, int argc, JSValueConst* argv, int audioSide, JSValueConst* data) {
    ProbeLog* log = logOf(ctx, data[0]);
    JSValue token = JS_NewObjectClass(ctx, log->tokenClass[audioSide]);
    JS_SetOpaque(token, new Token{log, tagOf(ctx, argc, argv)});
    return token;
}

inline void tokenFinalizer(JSRuntime*, JSValueConst value) {
    JSClassID id = 0;
    auto* t = static_cast<Token*>(JS_GetAnyOpaque(value, &id));
    if (!t) return;
    t->log->add("released " + t->tag);
    delete t;
}

// ScriptHost::Binder.
inline void bindProbes(void* user, JSContext* ctx, bool audioSide) {
    auto* log = static_cast<ProbeLog*>(user);
    JSClassID& id = log->tokenClass[audioSide ? 1 : 0];
    JS_NewClassID(JS_GetRuntime(ctx), &id);
    JSClassDef def{};
    def.class_name = "Token";
    def.finalizer = &tokenFinalizer;
    JS_NewClass(JS_GetRuntime(ctx), id, &def);
    JSValue data = JS_NewInt64(ctx, static_cast<std::int64_t>(reinterpret_cast<std::intptr_t>(log)));
    JSValue global = JS_GetGlobalObject(ctx);
    JS_SetPropertyStr(ctx, global, "__probe", JS_NewCFunctionData(ctx, &probeFn, 1, 0, 1, &data));
    JS_SetPropertyStr(ctx, global, "__token", JS_NewCFunctionData(ctx, &tokenFn, 1, audioSide ? 1 : 0, 1, &data));
    JS_FreeValue(ctx, global);
    JS_FreeValue(ctx, data);
}

struct ScriptRig {
    ProbeLog                              log;
    // Before the graph, so it is destroyed after it: the graph's shims hand their instances back to it.
    ScriptHost                            scripts{&bindProbes, &log};
    graph::NodeRegistry                   registry;
    graph::ResourceTable                  resources;
    std::unique_ptr<graph::GraphHost>     host;
    std::vector<std::vector<float>>       outs;
    std::vector<float*>                   outPointers;
    rp_transport                          transport{48000.0, 120.0, 0.0, 0};

    // The test bundle, then `toys` (JS source; empty for none).
    explicit ScriptRig(const std::string& toys = "", std::uint32_t maxFrames = 256) {
        std::vector<std::uint8_t> toyBytecode;
        std::vector<ScriptHost::Chunk> chunks{scriptTestBundle()};
        if (!toys.empty()) {
            toyBytecode = compileToys(toys);
            chunks.emplace_back(toyBytecode);
        }
        std::string error;
        if (!scripts.load(chunks, &error)) throw std::runtime_error("the toy bundle does not load: " + error);
        for (const rp_package* p : {graph::corePackage(), graph::hostPackage(), graph::test::testPackage(),
                                    test::testPackage(), scripts.package()})
            if (!registry.addPackage(p, &error)) throw std::runtime_error("a package is refused: " + error);
        host = std::make_unique<graph::GraphHost>(registry, resources, graph::HostConfig{48000.0, maxFrames});
        outs.assign(8, std::vector<float>(maxFrames, 0.0f));
        for (auto& o : outs) outPointers.push_back(o.data());
    }

    ~ScriptRig() {
        setAudioThreadOwns(false);
        host.reset();
    }

    graph::SetGraphResult set(const std::string& json) { return host->setGraph(json); }

    // One block, as an Engine runs it: the script host's releases, then the graph's drain and block.
    void block(std::uint32_t frames = 64) {
        scripts.beginBlock();
        host->processBlock(frames, transport, outPointers.data(), static_cast<std::uint32_t>(outPointers.size()));
    }
    void run(std::uint32_t frames = 64, int blocks = 1) {
        for (int i = 0; i < blocks; ++i) block(frames);
    }

    // True before an audio thread starts running blocks, false after it has stopped, as the Engine does.
    void setAudioThreadOwns(bool owns) {
        if (owns) scripts.setAudioThreadOwns(true);
        if (host) host->setAudioThreadOwns(owns);
        if (!owns) scripts.setAudioThreadOwns(false);
    }

    // The control thread's housekeeping: plans the block thread handed back, then the instance records.
    void reclaim() {
        host->reclaim();
        scripts.reclaim();
    }

    template <class T>
    T& node(const std::string& id) {
        T* t = rp::peer_as<T>(host->node(id));
        if (!t) throw std::runtime_error("no node " + id + " of that type");
        return *t;
    }

    static std::string codes(const graph::SetGraphResult& r) {
        std::string s;
        for (const auto& e : r.errors) s += (s.empty() ? "" : ",") + e.code;
        return s;
    }
};

}  // namespace rp::host::test
````

Create `packages/native/test/engine-graph/ScriptNodes.test.cpp`:

````cpp
// The script-node runtime (docs/modular-graph-phase-b3a-design.md section 2): TS nodes behind the same C ABI as
// native ones, one runtime per engine. Toy nodes, written here as JS source on the authoring layer the test bundle
// exposes (ScriptRig.hpp), are planned and run beside the graph tests' C++ sources and sinks: what reaches them
// through Block, what they send, the control-side context laying their ports out from settings, a node kept across
// a reshape or swapped or rebuilt, where their instances are made and released, a throw, the block path's
// allocations, and a running audio thread under all of it. The embedded production bundle and an Engine built
// around a toy bundle close it.
//
// Run via `pnpm test:plugin engine-graph`.

#include <atomic>
#include <cstdint>
#include <cstdio>
#include <string>
#include <thread>
#include <vector>

#include <catch2/catch_test_macros.hpp>

#include "../graph/CountingAllocator.hpp"
#include "ScriptRig.hpp"
#include "host/engine/Engine.hpp"

using rp::host::ScriptHost;
using rp::host::test::Feed;
using rp::host::test::Probe;
using rp::host::test::ScriptRig;
namespace gt = rp::graph::test;

namespace {

std::string doc(const std::string& nodes, const std::string& wires) {
    return R"({"nodes":[)" + nodes + R"(],"wires":[)" + wires + "]}";
}
std::string node(const std::string& id, const std::string& type, const std::string& settings = "", const std::string& params = "") {
    return R"({"id":")" + id + R"(","type":")" + type + "\"" + (settings.empty() ? "" : R"(,"settings":)" + settings) +
           (params.empty() ? "" : R"(,"params":)" + params) + "}";
}
std::string wire(const std::string& from, const std::string& to) {
    return R"({"from":")" + from + R"(","to":")" + to + "\"}";
}

std::vector<std::uint8_t> bytes(std::initializer_list<int> b) {
    std::vector<std::uint8_t> v;
    for (int x : b) v.push_back(static_cast<std::uint8_t>(x));
    return v;
}

// Events and bytes straight through, counting the sends its 4-message output refuses.
const char* const kPass = R"JS(
rp.register([rp.defineNode({
  id: "rp.toy.pass",
  ports: { in: rp.events.in(), bin: rp.bytes.in(), out: rp.events.out({ messages: 4 }), bout: rp.bytes.out(),
           refused: rp.control.out() },
  create: () => {
    let refused = 0;
    return {
      process(b) {
        const ms = b.messages("in");
        for (let i = 0; i < ms.length; ++i) if (!b.send("out", ms[i].frame, ms[i].data, ms[i].flags)) ++refused;
        const bs = b.messages("bin");
        for (let i = 0; i < bs.length; ++i) b.send("bout", bs[i].frame, bs[i].data, bs[i].flags);
        b.emit("refused", 0, refused);
      },
    };
  },
})]);
)JS";

// Audio scaled in place, over views of the plan's buffers, by a param and a control input, whose changes it emits.
const char* const kGain = R"JS(
rp.register([rp.defineNode({
  id: "rp.toy.gain",
  ports: { in: rp.audio.in(), out: rp.audio.out(rp.channels.match("in")), level: rp.control.in(), changes: rp.control.out() },
  params: { gain: rp.param.float({ name: "Gain", min: 0, max: 4, default: 1 }) },
  create: () => ({
    process(b) {
      const level = b.control("level");
      const g = b.control("gain").start * level.start;
      const ins = b.audio("in"), outs = b.audio("out");
      if (ins.length !== 2 || outs.length !== 2 || ins[0].length !== b.frames) throw new Error("views are the block's");
      for (let c = 0; c < outs.length; ++c) {
        const i = ins[c], o = outs[c];
        for (let f = 0; f < b.frames; ++f) o[f] = i[f] * g * (c + 1);
      }
      for (let k = 0; k < level.changes.length; ++k) b.emit("changes", level.changes[k].frame, level.changes[k].value);
    },
  }),
})]);
)JS";

// One output per `outs` its settings name; refuses more than 4 with zod's reason.
const char* const kFan = R"JS(
rp.register([rp.defineNode({
  id: "rp.toy.fan",
  settings: rp.z.object({ outs: rp.z.number().int().min(1).max(4).default(2) }),
  ports: (s) => { const p = { in: rp.events.in() }; for (let k = 1; k <= s.outs; ++k) p["out" + k] = rp.events.out(); return p; },
  create: ({ settings }) => ({
    process(b) {
      const ms = b.messages("in");
      for (let k = 1; k <= settings.outs; ++k) for (let i = 0; i < ms.length; ++i) b.send("out" + k, ms[i].frame, ms[i].data);
    },
  }),
})]);
)JS";

// A count of its blocks on every output, [count, k] on out<k>, its outputs listed last first, so a port's position
// moves when their number does. `counter` reshapes; `plain` does not, and also sends its settings' tag.
const char* const kCounters = R"JS(
const outsFor = (s) => { const p = {}; for (let k = s.outs; k >= 1; --k) p["out" + k] = rp.events.out(); return p; };
const counted = (reshapes) => rp.defineNode({
  id: reshapes ? "rp.toy.counter" : "rp.toy.plain",
  ...(reshapes ? { reshapes: true } : {}),
  settings: rp.z.object({ outs: rp.z.number().int().min(1).max(4).default(2), tag: rp.z.number().default(0) }),
  ports: outsFor,
  create: ({ settings }) => {
    let outs = settings.outs, tag = settings.tag, count = 0;
    const name = (reshapes ? "counter " : "plain ") + tag;
    const token = __token(name);
    __probe("create " + name);
    return {
      process: (b) => {
        ++count;
        for (let k = 1; k <= outs; ++k) b.send("out" + k, 0, [count & 0x7f, k, tag & 0x7f]);
        void token;
      },
      onSettings: (s) => {
        outs = s.outs;
        tag = s.tag;
        __probe("onSettings " + (reshapes ? "counter " : "plain ") + s.outs + "/" + s.tag);
      },
    };
  },
});
rp.register([counted(true), counted(false)]);
)JS";

// A throw on every second block; one that latches on its first; one that answers "fault".
const char* const kThrowers = R"JS(
const thrower = (id, extra, at) => rp.defineNode({
  id, ...extra,
  ports: { out: rp.events.out() },
  create: () => {
    let n = 0;
    return {
      process: (b) => {
        ++n;
        b.send("out", 0, [n]);
        if (at === "fault") return n === 2 ? "fault" : undefined;
        if (n % at === 0) throw new Error("boom " + n);
      },
    };
  },
});
rp.register([thrower("rp.toy.thrower", {}, 2), thrower("rp.toy.latch", { faultOnThrow: true }, 2),
             thrower("rp.toy.quitter", {}, "fault")]);
)JS";

// The steady block path: indexed loops, every port read and written, nothing a block makes.
const char* const kSteady = R"JS(
rp.register([rp.defineNode({
  id: "rp.toy.steady",
  ports: { in: rp.events.in(), audioIn: rp.audio.in(), level: rp.control.in(),
           out: rp.events.out(), audioOut: rp.audio.out(rp.channels.match("audioIn")), peak: rp.control.out() },
  params: { gain: rp.param.float({ name: "Gain", min: 0, max: 4, default: 1 }) },
  create: () => ({
    process(b) {
      const ms = b.messages("in");
      for (let i = 0; i < ms.length; ++i) b.send("out", ms[i].frame, ms[i].data, ms[i].flags);
      const g = b.control("gain").start * b.control("level").start;
      const ins = b.audio("audioIn"), outs = b.audio("audioOut");
      for (let c = 0; c < outs.length; ++c) { const i = ins[c], o = outs[c]; for (let f = 0; f < b.frames; ++f) o[f] = i[f] * g; }
      b.emit("peak", 0, g);
      b.transport.ppq;
    },
  }),
}), rp.defineNode({
  id: "rp.toy.idiomatic",
  ports: { in: rp.events.in(), out: rp.events.out() },
  create: () => ({
    process(b) {
      for (const m of b.messages("in")) b.send("out", m.frame, [m.data[0], m.data[1], m.data[2]]);
    },
  }),
})]);
)JS";

}  // namespace

TEST_CASE("a script node's messages arrive in order with their flags, and a send past capacity is refused and counted",
          "[script]") {
    ScriptRig rig(kPass);
    const auto r = rig.set(doc(node("feed", "rp.test.feed") + "," + node("pass", "rp.toy.pass") + "," + node("probe", "rp.test.probe"),
                               wire("feed.midi", "pass.in") + "," + wire("feed.bytes", "pass.bin") + "," +
                                   wire("pass.out", "probe.events") + "," + wire("pass.bout", "probe.bytes") + "," +
                                   wire("pass.refused", "probe.control")));
    INFO(ScriptRig::codes(r));
    REQUIRE(r.ok);
    auto& feed = rig.node<Feed>("feed");
    const std::vector<rp::host::test::Message> midi{{0, bytes({0x90, 60, 100})}, {5, bytes({0x80, 60, 0})},
                                                    {5, bytes({0x90, 62, 1})},   {9, bytes({0xb0, 1, 2})},
                                                    {12, bytes({0x90, 64, 3})},  {20, bytes({0xf8})}};
    feed.next[Feed::Midi] = midi;
    feed.next[Feed::Bytes] = {{3, bytes({1, 2, 3}), 0}, {7, bytes({4}), RP_MESSAGE_FLUSH}, {7, {}, 0}};
    rig.run();
    const auto& probe = rig.node<Probe>("probe");
    REQUIRE(probe.events.size() == 4);  // the first four, in order: the output holds four
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < 4; ++i) {
        CHECK(probe.events[i].frame == midi[i].frame);
        CHECK(probe.events[i].data == midi[i].data);
    }
    REQUIRE(probe.bytes.size() == 3);
    CHECK(probe.bytes[0].data == bytes({1, 2, 3}));
    CHECK(probe.bytes[1].flags == RP_MESSAGE_FLUSH);
    CHECK(probe.bytes[1].frame == 7);
    CHECK(probe.bytes[2].data.empty());
    CHECK(probe.controlAtZero == 2.0);                // the two sends `out` refused
    CHECK(rig.host->droppedMessages("pass") == 2);   // and the queue counted them
    // A shorter block reuses the arrays: one message, the rest gone.
    feed.next[Feed::Midi] = {{30, bytes({0x90, 70, 7})}};
    rig.run();
    REQUIRE(probe.events.size() == 1);
    CHECK(probe.events[0].frame == 30);
    CHECK(probe.events[0].data == bytes({0x90, 70, 7}));
    CHECK(probe.bytes.empty());
    CHECK(rig.scripts.throwCount() == 0);
}

TEST_CASE("a script node reads a param and a control stream, emits control, and writes audio through views of the plan's "
          "buffers",
          "[script]") {
    ScriptRig rig(kGain);
    REQUIRE(rig.set(doc(node("src", "rp.test.source") + "," + node("k", "rp.core.constant", "", R"({"value":0.5})") + "," +
                            node("g", "rp.toy.gain", "", R"({"gain":3})") + "," + node("sink", "rp.test.sink"),
                        wire("src.out", "g.in") + "," + wire("k.out", "g.level") + "," + wire("g.out", "sink.in") + "," +
                            wire("g.changes", "sink.control")))
                .ok);
    rig.run();
    const auto& sink = rig.node<gt::Sink>("sink");
    // The constant's first value is a change at frame 0 (a node cannot set a control output's start), so the level
    // starts at 0 and the change is passed on.
    CHECK(sink.first[0] == 0.0f);
    CHECK(sink.controlChanges == 1);
    CHECK(sink.controlEnd == 0.5);
    rig.run();
    CHECK(sink.first[0] == 1.5f);  // the source's 1.0, times the gain param's 3, times the level's 0.5
    CHECK(sink.last[0] == 1.5f);
    CHECK(sink.first[1] == 3.0f);  // channel 2 doubled
    CHECK(sink.controlChanges == 0);
    REQUIRE(rig.host->setParam("k", "value", 0.25, 10));
    REQUIRE(rig.host->setParam("g", "gain", 2));
    rig.run();
    CHECK(sink.first[0] == 1.5f);     // both values are changes this block (the gain's at frame 0), so the starts hold
    CHECK(sink.controlChanges == 1);  // the level's change at frame 10, passed on
    CHECK(sink.controlEnd == 0.25);
    rig.run(32);  // a shorter block: new views, as long as it
    CHECK(sink.first[0] == 0.5f);     // the gain's 2, the level's 0.25
    CHECK(sink.last[0] == 0.5f);
    CHECK(sink.controlChanges == 0);
    CHECK(rig.scripts.throwCount() == 0);
}

TEST_CASE("the control side lays a script node's ports out from its settings, and refuses what its definition refuses",
          "[script]") {
    ScriptRig rig(kFan);
    const auto fan = [](const std::string& settings, const std::string& wires) {
        return doc(node("feed", "rp.test.feed") + "," + node("fan", "rp.toy.fan", settings) + "," + node("probe", "rp.test.probe"),
                   wire("feed.midi", "fan.in") + (wires.empty() ? "" : "," + wires));
    };
    const auto three = rig.set(fan(R"({"outs":3})", wire("fan.out3", "probe.events")));
    INFO(ScriptRig::codes(three));
    REQUIRE(three.ok);
    CHECK(three.layouts.at("fan").find(R"("id":"out3")") != std::string::npos);
    rig.node<Feed>("feed").next[Feed::Midi] = {{4, bytes({0x90, 1, 2})}};
    rig.run();
    REQUIRE(rig.node<Probe>("probe").events.size() == 1);
    CHECK(rig.node<Probe>("probe").events[0].frame == 4);

    CHECK(ScriptRig::codes(rig.set(fan(R"({"outs":3})", wire("fan.out4", "probe.events")))) == "unknown-port");
    const auto refused = rig.set(fan(R"({"outs":9})", ""));
    REQUIRE(ScriptRig::codes(refused) == "settings-invalid");
    CHECK(refused.errors[0].message == R"(node type "rp.toy.fan": settings: outs: Too big: expected number to be <=4)");
    CHECK(ScriptRig::codes(rig.set(fan(R"({"outs":"two"})", ""))) == "settings-invalid");
}

TEST_CASE("the test bundle's own node, defined as a production node is, plans and runs", "[script]") {
    ScriptRig rig;
    REQUIRE(rig.registry.find("rp.test.script-echo"));
    REQUIRE(rig.set(doc(node("feed", "rp.test.feed") + "," + node("echo", "rp.test.script-echo", R"({"copies":2})", R"({"transpose":2})") +
                            "," + node("probe", "rp.test.probe"),
                        wire("feed.midi", "echo.in") + "," + wire("echo.out", "probe.events")))
                .ok);
    rig.node<Feed>("feed").next[Feed::Midi] = {{8, bytes({0x90, 60, 100})}};
    rig.run();
    const auto& probe = rig.node<Probe>("probe");
````
