````bash
git commit -F - <<'EOF'
feat(engine): the script-node runtime - TS nodes behind the C ABI, one runtime per engine

Beside today's path (docs/modular-graph-phase-b3a-design.md section 2): the DSP kernel still runs in DspRuntime
through rp.dsp.kernel, the production bundle registers no node yet, and parity does not move.

- ScriptHost (src/host/script), one per Engine: an audio-side bare QuickJS runtime holding every instance, entered
  only by the thread that runs blocks, and a control-side one that answers layout_for and prepare_settings with the
  definition's own parseSettings and layout. Both load the same bundle. A bundle registers its defineNode results
  by appending them to the global __rp_scriptNodes (src/script/register.ts); each becomes an rp_node_type in one
  package, rp.script, declaring RP_TYPE_STATELESS_PREPARE.
- The shim: create and activate only allocate it. The JS instance is made on the block thread at the first call the
  shim gets there, the ports_changed every fresh instance gets when its plan is adopted; destroy queues the release
  for the next block's beginBlock (there and then while quiescent), and the record goes back to the control thread
  to be deleted. A reshaping type answers RESHAPE for every change its definition accepts, any other SWAP while its
  layout is the one it was created with and REBUILD when it moves; commit_settings calls onSettings, ports_changed
  portsChanged.
- The Block: messages() a reused Message[] (payloads copied into one JS-owned buffer per port, each view made again
  only when its message's place moves), control() a reused { start, changes }, audio() Float32Array views over the
  plan's buffers with no copy (made again when a buffer or the block length moves, detached before what they look at
  can be freed), send() and emit() straight into the plan's queues (graph::reserveMessage for an array of numbers).
  Ports are found by id through atoms bound at creation or reshape: a warm block allocates nothing native, and a
  node written with indexed loops nothing in JS.
- A throw is caught and counted (Engine::scriptThrows), the first kept and logged at reclaim, and the node runs on;
  faultOnThrow, or returning "fault", faults it.
- The ABI: every type-level call but destroy is handed its rp_node_type, which gains a ctx, so one set of functions
  serves every script type.
- defineNode: reshapes and faultOnThrow (true or absent), NodeInstance.onSettings, and a refused setting names its
  first issue on one line, which a planner error can carry, instead of zod's JSON.
- The bundle: src/script/bundle.ts, compiled to global-code bytecode by retroplug-script-bundle and embedded in
  retroplug-backend; every Engine loads it at construction, and Engine(sampleRate, chunks) loads another (a test's
  toys). Its test-only twin, test/script/scriptTestBundle.ts, is embedded in retroplug-engine-graph-test alone: the
  authoring layer for toy nodes the tests write as JS source, and one zod-settings node of its own.
EOF
````

---

### Task 6: The DSP kernel as a TS script node, proven equal to today's kernel stage

The kernel node (design section 4), beside today's path: no production document names it yet, and the engine still
runs the kernel in `DspRuntime` through the native `rp.dsp.kernel`.

`src/script/kernelNode.ts` is today's `DspKernel` behind `defineNode`, with the kernel bundle's registry (the DSP
roles alone), registered by the production script bundle. Its type id is `rp.dsp.kernel-script` while the native
node holds `rp.dsp.kernel` (a registry refuses a second type under one id); the flip (Task 7) retires the native
node and gives this one the id. Its settings are `{ project, systems: { id, pipeline, serialOut }[] }`: `{}` is an
empty kernel, ids are integers from 1 to 2^32 - 1 and distinct (the old kernel took a repeated id silently), role
configs are carried as given. Its ports are named by system id: in `midiIn`, `controllerIn`,
`controllerConnected` and each Game Boy's `sys-<id>.serialOut`; out `sys-<id>.serialIn` / `midi` / `bytes` /
`buttons`, `midiOut`, `controllerOut`, with capacities sized from the most any `test:native` block sends through
each sink (parity included), with margin. It reshapes: `onSettings` runs `setSystems`, so survivors keep their
clocks and role state and a removed id is pruned. `process` builds `DspRuntime::processBlock`'s `BlockInput`
afresh, field for field (`controllerConnected` from the control's value at frame 0, read with the new `defineNode`
helper `startValue`), and sends each sink call onto its port in emission order: a press at frame 0, host MIDI out
behind the emitting system's id (4 bytes, little-endian), a call naming no system dropped. A throw is the script
host's (counted; the node runs on). Under `RETROPLUG_PROFILE` the engine binds the per-role tracing thunks into the
script host's audio context.

The proof is `KernelNode.test.cpp`: the same blocks through today's `DspRuntime`, loaded with today's kernel bundle
(embedded in that test binary alone, `retroplug-dsp-kernel-bundle`), and through the node in a plan fed by the host
I/O nodes, every sink output compared exactly: host MIDI under every routing (the unsorted staging, fed sorted to
today's kernel), each LSDj sync mode with MI.OUT and master sync, risa and smsggdj host sync, a controller
session, structure changes, an injected throw, and the node reshaping under an audio thread. Today's output is
compared as a frame-ordered queue carries it: Arduinoboy and MI.MAP send transport bytes and clocks at frame 0 after
a row byte, which reach SameBoy's front-release serial queue at that byte's frame. `parity/kernel-node` renders mGB
and a NES through a hand-built document wiring midi-in to the kernel node to each system, bit for bit the same as
through today's kernel stage.

- Modify: `packages/native/cmake/bundles.cmake`, `packages/native/cmake/tests.cmake`, `packages/native/src/host/dsp/DspRuntime.hpp`, `packages/native/src/host/engine/Engine.cpp`, `packages/native/test/engine-graph/ScriptNodes.test.cpp`, `packages/retroplug/src/graph/defineNode.ts`, `packages/retroplug/src/script/bundle.ts`, `packages/retroplug/test/graph/define-node.test.ts`

````ts
// The DSP kernel as a script node (src/script/kernelNode.ts): its settings, the ports they give, and where each of the
// kernel's sink calls goes, over a stand-in for the script host's Block. That it does exactly what today's kernel
// does, block for block, is held natively, against DspRuntime (packages/native/test/engine-graph/KernelNode.test.cpp).
import { test, expect } from "../../testing/harness";
import type { Block, ControlStream, Message } from "../../src/graph/defineNode";
import { KERNEL_NODE_TYPE, kernelNode, type KernelSettings } from "../../src/script/kernelNode";

const portsOf = (settings: unknown) => kernelNode.layout(kernelNode.parseSettings(settings)).ports.map((p) => `${p.dir} ${p.kind} ${p.id}`);

test("{} is an empty kernel: the host's ports and no system's", () => {
  expect(portsOf({})).toEqual([
    "in events midiIn",
    "in events controllerIn",
    "in control controllerConnected",
    "out events midiOut",
    "out events controllerOut",
  ]);
  expect(kernelNode.descriptor().id).toBe(KERNEL_NODE_TYPE);
  // A structure change is a reshape, and a throw is counted rather than latched (design section 4.5).
  expect(kernelNode.reshapes).toBe(true);
  expect(kernelNode.faultOnThrow).toBe(undefined);
});

test("each system has its four outputs, and one with a serialOut its MI.OUT input, named by its id", () => {
  expect(portsOf({ systems: [{ id: 3, pipeline: [], serialOut: true }, { id: 9 }] })).toEqual([
    "in events midiIn",
    "in events controllerIn",
    "in control controllerConnected",
    "in bytes sys-3.serialOut",
    "out bytes sys-3.serialIn",
    "out events sys-3.midi",
    "out bytes sys-3.bytes",
    "out events sys-3.buttons",
    "out bytes sys-9.serialIn",
    "out events sys-9.midi",
    "out bytes sys-9.bytes",
    "out events sys-9.buttons",
    "out events midiOut",
    "out events controllerOut",
  ]);
});

test("settings fill their defaults, keep each role's config as given, and refuse a bad or repeated id", () => {
  const config = { app: "lsdj-midimap", songRowTicks: [[96, null], [96]], appConfig: { quantise: "bar" } };
  expect(kernelNode.parseSettings({ project: [{ kind: "launchpad", config }], systems: [{ id: 2, pipeline: [{ kind: "mgb" }] }] })).toEqual({
    project: [{ kind: "launchpad", config }],
    systems: [{ id: 2, pipeline: [{ kind: "mgb", config: {} }], serialOut: false }],
  });
  for (const id of [0, 1.5, -1, 2 ** 32]) expect(() => kernelNode.parseSettings({ systems: [{ id }] }), `id ${id}`).toThrow("systems.0.id");
  expect(() => kernelNode.parseSettings({ systems: [{ id: 4 }, { id: 4 }] })).toThrow("systems: two systems have the same id");
});

// A Block as the script host hands one over, recording every send.
interface Sent {
  port: string;
  frame: number;
  data: number[];
  flags: number;
}
function blockOf(
  frames: number,
  playing: boolean,
  messages: Record<string, { frame: number; data: number[] }[]>,
  controls: Record<string, ControlStream> = {},
): { block: Block; sent: Sent[] } {
  const sent: Sent[] = [];
  const block: Block = {
    frames,
    transport: { sampleRate: 44100, tempo: 120, ppq: 0, playing },
    audio: () => [],
    messages: (port) => (messages[port] ?? []).map((m): Message => ({ frame: m.frame, data: Uint8Array.from(m.data), flags: 0 })),
    send: (port, frame, data, flags = 0) => (sent.push({ port, frame, data: Array.from(data), flags }), true),
    control: (id) => controls[id] ?? { start: 0, changes: [] },
    emit: () => true,
  };
  return { block, sent };
}

const settings = (s: unknown): KernelSettings => kernelNode.parseSettings(s);
const create = (s: KernelSettings) => kernelNode.create({ settings: s, sampleRate: 44100, maxFrames: 1024 });

test("each sink call goes onto its system's port in emission order, host MIDI out behind its system's id", () => {
  const node = create(
    settings({
      project: [{ kind: "midi-routing", config: { mode: "sendToAll" } }],
      systems: [
        { id: 1, pipeline: [{ kind: "mgb", config: {} }], serialOut: true },
        { id: 2, pipeline: [{ kind: "nes-n8-midi", config: {} }] },
        { id: 0x01020304, pipeline: [{ kind: "lsdj-sync", config: { mode: "masterSync" } }], serialOut: true },
        { id: 4, pipeline: [{ kind: "risa-sync", config: {} }] },
      ],
    }),
  );
  const { block, sent } = blockOf(1024, true, {
    midiIn: [{ frame: 4, data: [0x90, 60, 100] }],
    [`sys-${0x01020304}.serialOut`]: [{ frame: 0, data: [5] }, { frame: 0, data: [5] }],
  });
  node.process(block);
  const at = (port: string) => sent.filter((s) => s.port === port).map((s) => [s.frame, ...s.data, s.flags]);
  expect(at("sys-1.serialIn")).toEqual([[4, 0x90, 0], [4, 60, 0], [4, 100, 0]]);
  expect(at("sys-2.midi")).toEqual([[4, 0x90, 60, 100, 0]]);
  const id = [4, 3, 2, 1]; // 0x01020304, little-endian
  expect(at("midiOut")).toEqual([[0, ...id, 0x90, 5, 0x7f, 0], [0, ...id, 0xfa, 0], [0, ...id, 0xf8, 0], [0, ...id, 0xf8, 0]]);
  // risa's arm flushes the FIFO; START and the first clock follow it.
  expect(at("sys-4.bytes").slice(0, 2)).toEqual([[0, 0xf9, 0x52, 0, 0, 0, 1], [0, 0xfa, 0]]);
  // Systems run in slot order, so their ports fill in that order.
  const order = sent.map((s) => s.port).filter((p, i, all) => all.indexOf(p) === i);
  expect(order).toEqual(["sys-1.serialIn", "sys-2.midi", "midiOut", "sys-4.bytes"]);
});

test("a role's press goes out at frame 0, and a surface counts as attached when it is from frame 0", () => {
  // autoStart taps START on the transport's rise.
  const press = create(settings({ systems: [{ id: 1, pipeline: [{ kind: "lsdj-sync", config: { mode: "midiSync", autoStart: true } }] }] }));
  const started = blockOf(1024, true, {});
  press.process(started.block);
  expect(started.sent.filter((s) => s.port === "sys-1.buttons")).toEqual([{ port: "sys-1.buttons", frame: 0, data: [7, 1], flags: 0 }]);
  // A controller session paints its surface on its first block either way, and takes the surface (its hello) on the
  // block it is attached; one attached later in the block is attached from the next.
  const rows = [Array.from({ length: 16 }, () => 96)];
  const sentToSurface = (connected: ControlStream): number => {
    const node = create(settings({ project: [{ kind: "launchpad", config: { app: "lsdj-midimap", songRowTicks: rows } }] }));
    const b = blockOf(1024, false, {}, { controllerConnected: connected });
    node.process(b.block);
    expect(b.sent.every((s) => s.port === "controllerOut" && s.frame === 0)).toBe(true);
    return b.sent.length;
  };
  const unattached = sentToSurface({ start: 0, changes: [] });
  expect(unattached).toBeGreaterThan(0);
  expect(sentToSurface({ start: 0, changes: [{ frame: 0, value: 1 }] })).toBeGreaterThan(unattached);
  expect(sentToSurface({ start: 1, changes: [] })).toBeGreaterThan(unattached);
  expect(sentToSurface({ start: 0, changes: [{ frame: 9, value: 1 }] })).toBe(unattached);
});

test("a structure change keeps a survivor's clock as it moves, and a removed id sends nothing", () => {
  const one = settings({ systems: [{ id: 1, pipeline: [{ kind: "lsdj-sync", config: { mode: "midiSync" } }] }] });
  const node = create(one);
  const run = () => {
    const b = blockOf(22050, true, {}); // one quarter at 120 bpm: 24 clocks
    node.process(b.block);
    return b.sent;
  };
  expect(run().filter((s) => s.port === "sys-1.serialIn").length).toBe(24);
  node.onSettings!(
    settings({
      systems: [
        { id: 2, pipeline: [{ kind: "mgb", config: {} }] },
        { id: 1, pipeline: [{ kind: "lsdj-sync", config: { mode: "midiSync" } }] },
      ],
    }),
  );
  // The clock goes on (ppq stays 0, so a fresh one would resync and send the same 24; one that kept its counter is
  // past this quarter and sends none).
  expect(run().filter((s) => s.port === "sys-1.serialIn").length).toBe(0);
  node.onSettings!(settings({ systems: [] }));
  expect(run()).toEqual([]);
});
````

Create `packages/native/test/engine-graph/KernelNode.test.cpp`:

````cpp
// The DSP kernel as a script node (docs/modular-graph-phase-b3a-design.md section 4), held to today's kernel stage.
// The same blocks are driven through today's DspRuntime, loaded with today's kernel bundle (src/dspKernelBundle.ts,
// embedded here alone), and through the kernel node of the production script bundle in a plan, fed by the host I/O
// nodes and a stand-in for the Game Boys' serialOut, its every output read back by probes. Every sink output is
// compared exactly, block by block: per system and port, the frame, bytes, flush flag and order of each message;
// the host MIDI out with its system tags in emission order; the control-surface out.
//
// Two differences are the design's, and each is applied to today's side rather than allowed for in the comparison:
//   - host MIDI reaches the node through rp.host.midi-in, which stable-sorts it by frame (section 3.4), so today's
//     kernel is fed the sorted staging;
//   - a queue is frame-ordered: a message pushed earlier than the last one on its port is carried at that one's frame
//     (graph/Queue.hpp pushMessage), so today's output is compared as a wire would carry it. Only LSDj's Arduinoboy
//     and MI.MAP modes emit out of order (a row byte at its note's frame, then transport bytes and clocks at frame 0),
//     to SameBoy's serial queue, which releases only its front byte, so a raised frame changes nothing it does. The
//     rig counts the messages raised, and each case says whether it expects any.
//
// Last, the node runs on an audio thread while the control thread reshapes it, for the thread sanitizer.
//
// Run via `pnpm test:plugin engine-graph`.

#include <algorithm>
#include <atomic>
#include <chrono>
#include <cstdint>
#include <cstdio>
#include <memory>
#include <string>
#include <thread>
#include <utility>
#include <vector>

#include <catch2/catch_test_macros.hpp>

#include "TestNodes.hpp"
#include "graph/GraphHost.hpp"
#include "graph/HostNodes.hpp"
#include "graph/Queue.hpp"
#include "graph/nodes/CoreNodes.hpp"
#include "host/dsp/DspRuntime.hpp"
#include "host/dsp/ScriptCompiler.hpp"
#include "host/graph/HostIoNodes.hpp"
#include "host/graph/HostServices.hpp"
#include "host/script/ScriptHost.hpp"

// Today's kernel bundle (cmake/bundles.cmake, retroplug-dsp-kernel-bundle).
extern "C" {
extern const std::uint8_t  rp_dsp_kernel_bundle[];
extern const std::uint32_t rp_dsp_kernel_bundle_size;
}

using rp::host::ScriptHost;
using rp::host::test::Feed;
using rp::host::test::Message;
using rp::host::test::Probe;

namespace {

using Bytes = std::vector<std::uint8_t>;

constexpr double kRate = 44100.0;
constexpr std::uint32_t kBeat = 22050;  // frames per quarter at 120 bpm
const char* const kKernel = "rp.dsp.kernel-script";  // KERNEL_NODE_TYPE (src/script/kernelNode.ts)

// ---- structures, spelled as kernelProjection spells them -----------------------------------------------------

struct Role {
    std::string kind;
    std::string config = "{}";  // JSON
};
struct System {
    std::uint32_t     id;
    std::vector<Role> pipeline;
    bool              serialOut = false;  // a Game Boy
};
struct Structure {
    std::vector<Role>   project;
    std::vector<System> systems;
};

// The system roles as the stores parse them: dead bytes to the kernel, carried as it carries them today.
const Role kSameBoy{"sameboy", R"({"model":"cgbC","highpass":"accurate","linkGroupId":0,"fastBoot":true,)"
                               R"("colorCorrection":"disabled","dmgPalette":"grey","lightTemperature":0})"};
const Role kMesen{"mesen", R"({"region":"auto","removeSpriteLimit":false,"enableFm":true,"apuLatencyMs":1.4,"s5bNoise":"n8",)"
                           R"("mmc5PhaseReset":"n8","expansionVolume":100,"channelExportMode":"mix","sdRoot":""})"};

Role routing(const std::string& mode) { return {"midi-routing", R"({"mode":")" + mode + R"("})"}; }
Role lsdj(const std::string& mode, int divisor = 1, bool autoStart = false) {
    return {"lsdj-sync", R"({"mode":")" + mode + R"(","tempoDivisor":)" + std::to_string(divisor) +
                             R"(,"autoStart":)" + (autoStart ? "true" : "false") + "}"};
}
const Role kMgb{"mgb"};
const Role kNesMidi{"nes-n8-midi"};
const Role kRisa{"risa-sync"};
Role sms(const std::string& machine) { return {"sms-sync", R"({"machine":")" + machine + R"("})"}; }

System gameBoy(std::uint32_t id, Role feature) { return {id, {kSameBoy, std::move(feature)}, true}; }
System nes(std::uint32_t id, std::vector<Role> features) {
    features.insert(features.begin(), kMesen);
    return {id, std::move(features), false};
}

std::string rolesJson(const std::vector<Role>& roles) {
    std::string s = "[";
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < roles.size(); ++i)
        s += (i ? "," : "") + std::string(R"({"kind":")") + roles[i].kind + R"(","config":)" + roles[i].config + "}";
    return s + "]";
}

// Today's KernelStructure (what syncDspFromStore pushes), or the kernel node's settings, which add serialOut.
std::string structureJson(const Structure& s, bool settings) {
    std::string out = R"({"project":)" + rolesJson(s.project) + R"(,"systems":[)";
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < s.systems.size(); ++i) {
        const System& sys = s.systems[i];
        out += (i ? "," : "") + std::string(R"({"id":)") + std::to_string(sys.id) + R"(,"pipeline":)" + rolesJson(sys.pipeline);
        if (settings) out += std::string(R"(,"serialOut":)") + (sys.serialOut ? "true" : "false");
        out += "}";
    }
    return out + "]}";
}

// ---- one block's input -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

struct BlockIn {
    std::uint32_t                                     frames = 1024;
    double                                            ppq = 0.0;
    double                                            tempo = 120.0;
    bool                                              playing = false;
    std::vector<std::pair<std::uint32_t, Bytes>>      midi;        // as a host stages it, in any frame order
    std::vector<Bytes>                                controller;  // control-surface traffic, at frame 0
    bool                                              connected = false;
    std::vector<std::pair<std::uint32_t, Bytes>>      serialOut;   // what each Game Boy captured last block
};

Bytes on(int channel, int key, int velocity = 100) {
    return {static_cast<std::uint8_t>(0x90 | channel), static_cast<std::uint8_t>(key), static_cast<std::uint8_t>(velocity)};
}
Bytes off(int channel, int key) { return {static_cast<std::uint8_t>(0x80 | channel), static_cast<std::uint8_t>(key), 0}; }
Bytes cc(int channel, int number, int value) {
    return {static_cast<std::uint8_t>(0xB0 | channel), static_cast<std::uint8_t>(number), static_cast<std::uint8_t>(value)};
}

// A message list as text, so a failed comparison shows both sides.
std::string text(const std::vector<Message>& ms) {
    std::string s;
    char b[16];
    for (const Message& m : ms) {
        s += std::to_string(m.frame) + ":";
        for (const std::uint8_t x : m.data) {
            std::snprintf(b, sizeof b, "%02x", x);
            s += b;
        }
        if (m.flags) s += "/" + std::to_string(m.flags);
        s += " ";
    }
    return s;
}

// ---- the rig ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

struct KernelRig {
    Structure  structure;
    DspRuntime today;
    // Before the graph, so it is destroyed after it: the kernel's shim hands its instance back to it.
    ScriptHost                        scripts;
    rp::graph::NodeRegistry           registry;
    rp::graph::ResourceTable          resources;
    // The engine's host I/O, standing in: what is staged for a block, and what the output nodes hand back.
    std::vector<std::pair<std::uint32_t, Bytes>> stagedMidi;
    std::vector<Bytes>                           stagedController;
    bool                                         connected = false;
    struct Out {
        std::uint32_t system;
        std::uint32_t frame;
        Bytes         data;
    };
    std::vector<Out>                  midiOut;
    std::vector<Bytes>                controllerOut;
    rp::host::EngineHostIo            hostIo{this, &takeMidi, &takeController, &isConnected, &recordMidiOut, &recordControllerOut, &noCart};
    std::unique_ptr<rp::graph::GraphHost> host;
    rp_node*                          kernel = nullptr;
    int                               blocks = 0;
    // What the comparisons covered: messages compared, by kind, and messages whose frame the queue raised.
    struct {
        int serialIn = 0, midi = 0, bytes = 0, buttons = 0, midiOut = 0, controllerOut = 0;
    } seen;
    int raised = 0;

    // `inject`: JS run after both bundles, in both runtimes.
    explicit KernelRig(Structure s, const std::string& inject = "") : structure(std::move(s)) {
        REQUIRE(today.loadKernel(Bytes(rp_dsp_kernel_bundle, rp_dsp_kernel_bundle + rp_dsp_kernel_bundle_size)));
        std::vector<ScriptHost::Chunk> chunks{ScriptHost::embeddedBundle()};
        Bytes injected;
        if (!inject.empty()) {
            const auto bc = dsp::compileToBytecode(inject);
            REQUIRE(bc.has_value());
            injected = *bc;
            REQUIRE(today.loadKernel(injected));
            chunks.emplace_back(injected);
        }
        std::string error;
        const bool loaded = scripts.load(chunks, &error);
        INFO(error);
        REQUIRE(loaded);
        for (const rp_package* p : {rp::graph::corePackage(), rp::graph::hostPackage(), rp::host::hostIoPackage(),
                                    rp::host::test::testPackage(), scripts.package()})
            REQUIRE(registry.addPackage(p, &error));
        rp::graph::HostConfig config;
        config.sampleRate = kRate;
        config.maxFrames = 8192;
        config.interfaces = [](void* ctx, const char* id) -> const void* {
            return std::string(id) == RP_ENGINE_HOST_IO_INTERFACE ? &static_cast<KernelRig*>(ctx)->hostIo : nullptr;
        };
        config.interfacesCtx = this;
        host = std::make_unique<rp::graph::GraphHost>(registry, resources, config);
        plan();
        kernel = host->node("kernel");
        REQUIRE(kernel != nullptr);
    }
    ~KernelRig() { host.reset(); }

    // A structure change, as the stores push one: to today's kernel through setSystems, to the node as its settings,
    // which reshape it (the instance kept) whenever its ports move.
    void restructure(Structure next) {
        structure = std::move(next);
        plan();
        CHECK(host->node("kernel") == kernel);
    }

    void plan() {
        const std::string json = structureJson(structure, false);
        REQUIRE(today.setSystems(Bytes(json.begin(), json.end())));
        const auto r = host->setGraph(document());
        for (const auto& e : r.errors) UNSCOPED_INFO(e.code << " at " << e.nodeId << "." << e.port << ": " << e.message);
        REQUIRE(r.ok);
    }

    // The host I/O nodes into the kernel, a feed for each Game Boy's MI.OUT, the kernel, and every output read: a
    // system's serialIn and midi on one probe, its bytes and buttons on another.
    std::string document() const {
        const auto node = [](const std::string& id, const std::string& type, const std::string& settings = "") {
            return R"({"id":")" + id + R"(","type":")" + type + "\"" + (settings.empty() ? "" : R"(,"settings":)" + settings) + "}";
        };
        const auto wire = [](const std::string& from, const std::string& to) {
            return R"({"from":")" + from + R"(","to":")" + to + "\"}";
        };
        std::vector<std::string> nodes{node("midi-in", "rp.host.midi-in"), node("controller-in", "rp.host.controller-in"),
                                       node("kernel", kKernel, structureJson(structure, true)),
                                       node("midi-out", "rp.host.midi-out"), node("controller-out", "rp.host.controller-out")};
        std::vector<std::string> wires{wire("midi-in.midi", "kernel.midiIn"), wire("controller-in.midi", "kernel.controllerIn"),
                                       wire("controller-in.connected", "kernel.controllerConnected"),
                                       wire("kernel.midiOut", "midi-out.midi"), wire("kernel.controllerOut", "controller-out.midi")};
        for (const System& s : structure.systems) {
            const std::string id = std::to_string(s.id), port = "kernel.sys-" + id;
            if (s.serialOut) {
                nodes.push_back(node("mi-out-" + id, "rp.test.feed"));
                wires.push_back(wire("mi-out-" + id + ".bytes", port + ".serialOut"));
            }
            nodes.push_back(node("in-" + id, "rp.test.probe"));
            nodes.push_back(node("io-" + id, "rp.test.probe"));
            wires.push_back(wire(port + ".serialIn", "in-" + id + ".bytes"));
            wires.push_back(wire(port + ".midi", "in-" + id + ".events"));
            wires.push_back(wire(port + ".bytes", "io-" + id + ".bytes"));
            wires.push_back(wire(port + ".buttons", "io-" + id + ".events"));
        }
        std::string doc = R"({"nodes":[)";
        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < nodes.size(); ++i) doc += (i ? "," : "") + nodes[i];
        doc += R"(],"wires":[)";
        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < wires.size(); ++i) doc += (i ? "," : "") + wires[i];
        return doc + "]}";
    }

    template <class T>
    T& node(const std::string& id) {
        T* t = rp::peer_as<T>(host->node(id));
        REQUIRE(t != nullptr);
        return *t;
    }

    // One block through both, then every output compared.
    void block(const BlockIn& in) {
        // Today: the staging sorted as rp.host.midi-in sorts it, last block's MI.OUT in slot order, no buttons or
        // keys, and the host outputs cleared first (the engine clears them, at the top of its block).
        std::vector<DspRuntime::MidiIn> midi;
        for (const auto& [frame, data] : in.midi) midi.push_back({frame, data});
        std::stable_sort(midi.begin(), midi.end(), [](const auto& a, const auto& b) { return a.frame < b.frame; });
        std::vector<DspRuntime::SerialOut> serialOut;
        for (const System& s : structure.systems)
            for (const auto& [id, captured] : in.serialOut)
                if (id == s.id)
                    for (const std::uint8_t b : captured) serialOut.push_back({id, b});
        std::vector<DspRuntime::MidiIn> controller;
        for (const Bytes& c : in.controller) controller.push_back({0, c});
        today.midiOut_.clear();
        today.controllerOut_.clear();
        today.processBlock(midi, {}, {}, serialOut, controller,
                           DspRuntime::BlockInfo{in.frames, kRate, in.tempo, in.ppq, in.playing, in.connected});

        // The node: what the host staged, each Game Boy's MI.OUT a byte a message at frame 0 as its serialOut carries
        // it, then one block as the engine runs it.
        stagedMidi = in.midi;
        stagedController = in.controller;
        connected = in.connected;
        for (const System& s : structure.systems) {
            if (!s.serialOut) continue;
            Feed& feed = node<Feed>("mi-out-" + std::to_string(s.id));
            for (const auto& [id, captured] : in.serialOut)
                if (id == s.id)
                    for (const std::uint8_t b : captured) feed.next[Feed::Bytes].push_back({0, {b}, 0});
        }
        midiOut.clear();
        controllerOut.clear();
        scripts.beginBlock();
        host->processBlock(in.frames, rp_transport{kRate, in.tempo, in.ppq, in.playing ? std::uint32_t{RP_TRANSPORT_PLAYING} : 0u});
        compare();
        ++blocks;
    }
    void run(BlockIn in, int count) {
        for (int i = 0; i < count; ++i) {
            block(in);
            in.midi.clear();
            in.controller.clear();
            in.serialOut.clear();
            if (in.playing) in.ppq += in.tempo / 60.0 * in.frames / kRate;
        }
    }

    // Today's messages for one port, as a frame-ordered queue carries them.
    std::vector<Message> carried(std::vector<Message> ms) {
        for (std::size_t i = 1; i < ms.size(); ++i)
            if (ms[i].frame < ms[i - 1].frame) {
                ms[i].frame = ms[i - 1].frame;
                ++raised;
            }
        return ms;
    }

    void compare() {
        INFO("block " << blocks);
        for (const System& s : structure.systems) {
            INFO("system " << s.id);
            std::vector<Message> serialIn, midi, bytes, buttons;
            for (const auto& e : today.serialIn_)
                if (e.system == s.id) serialIn.push_back({e.frame, {e.byte}, 0});
            for (const auto& e : today.coreMidi_)
                if (e.system == s.id) midi.push_back({e.frame, e.data, 0});
            for (const auto& e : today.coreBytes_)
                if (e.system == s.id) bytes.push_back({e.frame, e.data, e.flush ? std::uint32_t{RP_MESSAGE_FLUSH} : 0u});
            for (const auto& e : today.buttonOut_)
                if (e.system == s.id) {
                    CHECK(e.frame == 0);  // the kernel presses at frame 0, and the core takes a press with no frame
                    buttons.push_back({0, {static_cast<std::uint8_t>(e.button), static_cast<std::uint8_t>(e.down ? 1 : 0)}, 0});
                }
            const Probe& in = node<Probe>("in-" + std::to_string(s.id));
            const Probe& io = node<Probe>("io-" + std::to_string(s.id));
            CHECK(text(in.bytes) == text(carried(serialIn)));
            CHECK(text(in.events) == text(carried(midi)));
            CHECK(text(io.bytes) == text(carried(bytes)));
            CHECK(text(io.events) == text(carried(buttons)));
            seen.serialIn += static_cast<int>(serialIn.size());
            seen.midi += static_cast<int>(midi.size());
            seen.bytes += static_cast<int>(bytes.size());
            seen.buttons += static_cast<int>(buttons.size());
        }
        // Today addressed no system outside the structure, so nothing above went unread.
        const auto known = [&](std::uint32_t id) {
            return std::any_of(structure.systems.begin(), structure.systems.end(), [&](const System& s) { return s.id == id; });
        };
        for (const auto& e : today.serialIn_) CHECK(known(e.system));
        for (const auto& e : today.coreMidi_) CHECK(known(e.system));
        for (const auto& e : today.coreBytes_) CHECK(known(e.system));
        for (const auto& e : today.buttonOut_) CHECK(known(e.system));

        // One port for every system's host MIDI out, in emission order, the system its prefix's.
        std::vector<Message> expected, got;
        std::vector<std::uint32_t> expectedSystems, gotSystems;
        for (const auto& m : today.midiOut_) {
            expected.push_back({m.frame, m.data, 0});
            expectedSystems.push_back(m.system);
        }
        for (const Out& m : midiOut) {
            got.push_back({m.frame, m.data, 0});
            gotSystems.push_back(m.system);
        }
        CHECK(text(got) == text(carried(expected)));
        CHECK(gotSystems == expectedSystems);
        CHECK(controllerOut == today.controllerOut_);
        seen.midiOut += static_cast<int>(expected.size());
        seen.controllerOut += static_cast<int>(today.controllerOut_.size());
    }

    // ---- the host I/O stand-in -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    static KernelRig& of(void* ctx) { return *static_cast<KernelRig*>(ctx); }
    // As the engine's: the staging stable-sorted by frame (design section 3.4), then cleared.
    static void takeMidi(void* ctx, rp_queue* out) {
        auto& staged = of(ctx).stagedMidi;
        std::stable_sort(staged.begin(), staged.end(), [](const auto& a, const auto& b) { return a.first < b.first; });
        for (const auto& [frame, data] : staged) rp::graph::pushMessage(*out, frame, data);
        staged.clear();
    }
    static void takeController(void* ctx, rp_queue* out) {
        for (const Bytes& data : of(ctx).stagedController) rp::graph::pushMessage(*out, 0, data);
        of(ctx).stagedController.clear();
    }
    static bool isConnected(void* ctx) { return of(ctx).connected; }
    static void recordMidiOut(void* ctx, std::uint32_t system, std::uint32_t frame, const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t size) {
        of(ctx).midiOut.push_back({system, frame, Bytes(data, data + size)});
    }
    static void recordControllerOut(void* ctx, const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t size) {
        of(ctx).controllerOut.emplace_back(data, data + size);
    }
    static void noCart(void*, std::uint32_t, const std::uint8_t*, std::size_t, bool) {}

    // True before an audio thread starts running blocks, false after it has stopped, as the Engine does.
    void setAudioThreadOwns(bool owns) {
        if (owns) scripts.setAudioThreadOwns(true);
        host->setAudioThreadOwns(owns);
        if (!owns) scripts.setAudioThreadOwns(false);
    }

    // Nothing dropped, nothing faulted, and `throws` caught in all.
    void finish(std::uint32_t throws = 0) {
        CHECK(host->droppedMessages() == 0);
        CHECK_FALSE(host->isFaulted("kernel"));
        CHECK(scripts.throwCount() == throws);
    }
};

// A frame-flagged MI.OUT byte as LSDj's link carries it: a flag bit, then the protocol byte's seven bits.
std::uint8_t framed(std::uint8_t command) { return static_cast<std::uint8_t>(0x80 | (command & 0x7f)); }

// The lsdj-midimap app's song timing for a song of sixteen one-phrase rows on every channel, as the control plane
// derives it from a battery (songRowTicks).
std::string songRowTicks() {
    std::string row = "[";
    for (int r = 0; r < 16; ++r) row += (r ? "," : "") + std::string("96");
    row += "]";
    return "[" + row + "," + row + "," + row + "," + row + "]";
}
Role launchpad(const std::string& target, std::uint32_t systemId, const std::string& quantise) {
    return {"launchpad", R"({"app":"lsdj-midimap","target":")" + target + R"(","systemId":)" + std::to_string(systemId) +
                             R"(,"appConfig":{"quantise":")" + quantise + R"("},"songRowTicks":)" + songRowTicks() +
                             R"(,"anchorRows":[],"anchorSeq":0})"};
}
// A press of the pad at (x, y), (0, 0) top left, as a Launchpad in Programmer mode sends it (padIndex in
// src/launchpad/profile.ts).
Bytes pad(int x, int y, int velocity = 100) {
    return {0x90, static_cast<std::uint8_t>((7 - y) * 10 + x + 11), static_cast<std::uint8_t>(velocity)};
}

}  // namespace

TEST_CASE("the kernel node hands every system the host MIDI today's kernel hands it, under every routing",
          "[engine-graph][kernel-node]") {
    // mGB forwards each byte to its serial port, the NES each message to its FIFO, a SysEx (longer than a MidiEvent)
    // included. The plugin stages a block's DAW events, then a moved automation slot's CC at frame 0.
    KernelRig rig({{routing("sendToAll")}, {gameBoy(1, kMgb), nes(2, {kNesMidi})}});
    rig.block({.midi = {{100, on(0, 60)}, {300, on(1, 62)}, {0, cc(0, 7, 100)}}});
    rig.block({.midi = {{5, off(0, 60)}, {5, on(0, 64)}, {5, on(2, 67)}, {1023, off(1, 62)}}});
    rig.block({.midi = {{10, {0xF0, 0x7D, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 0xF7}}, {0, {0xF8}}, {10, {0xFA}}}});
    for (std::uint32_t frames : {1u, 1u, 33u, 1u, 222u, 1u, 7u, 4096u, 2u})
        rig.block({.frames = frames, .midi = {{0, on(3, 40 + static_cast<int>(frames % 50))}, {frames - 1, off(3, 40)}}});
    rig.run({.frames = 8192}, 2);  // nothing staged
    // Each routing, a structure change that keeps the node's ports (a swap).
    for (const char* mode : {"oneChannelPerInstance", "midiChannelToInstance", "fourChannelsPerInstance"}) {
        INFO(mode);
        rig.restructure({{routing(mode)}, {gameBoy(1, kMgb), nes(2, {kNesMidi})}});
        for (int ch = 0; ch < 8; ++ch) rig.block({.frames = 512, .midi = {{static_cast<std::uint32_t>(ch * 50), on(ch, 50 + ch)}}});
    }
    CHECK(rig.seen.serialIn > 100);
    CHECK(rig.seen.midi > 30);
    CHECK(rig.raised == 0);
    rig.finish();
}

TEST_CASE("the kernel node drives each LSDj sync mode as today's kernel does, MI.OUT and master sync among them",
          "[engine-graph][kernel-node]") {
    KernelRig rig({{routing("sendToAll")},
                   {gameBoy(1, lsdj("midiSync", 1, true)), gameBoy(2, lsdj("midiSync", 2)), gameBoy(3, lsdj("midiSyncArduinoboy", 1, true)),
                    gameBoy(4, lsdj("midiMap")), gameBoy(5, lsdj("keyboardMidi")), gameBoy(6, lsdj("midiPassthrough")),
                    gameBoy(7, lsdj("midiOut")), gameBoy(8, lsdj("masterSync")), gameBoy(9, lsdj("off"))}});
    // Stopped: notes only (MI.MAP rows, Arduinoboy rows and its play flag, keyboard scancodes, passthrough bytes).
    rig.block({.midi = {{0, on(0, 5)}, {40, on(0, 24)}, {41, on(0, 40)}, {90, on(0, 48)}, {91, on(1, 9)}}});
    rig.block({.midi = {{3, off(0, 5)}, {3, off(1, 9)}, {700, on(0, 72)}, {701, on(0, 27)}}});
    // The transport starts with a row note in the block: the Arduinoboy START and the clocks go out at frame 0 after
    // the row byte (raised to its frame on the wire), and MI.MAP's clocks after its row.
    rig.block({.ppq = 0.0, .playing = true, .midi = {{200, on(0, 31)}, {200, on(0, 7)}}});
    BlockIn playing{.frames = 1024, .ppq = 1024.0 / kBeat, .playing = true};
    rig.run(playing, 30);
    // MI.OUT: framed protocol bytes, a frame split over two captured bytes; master sync: a run, a quiet block, then a
    // stopped LSDj's idle flood, then a run again.
    Bytes flood;
    for (int i = 0; i < 40; ++i) flood.push_back(static_cast<std::uint8_t>(i & 0x7f));
    playing.ppq = 31 * 1024.0 / kBeat;
    for (auto captured : {std::vector<std::pair<std::uint32_t, Bytes>>{{7, {framed(0x7d), framed(0x7f), framed(0x70), framed(0x69), 0x7f}},
                                                                       {8, {5, 5, 5}}},
                          {{7, {0x80, framed(0x74), framed(64)}}, {8, {}}},
                          {{8, flood}},
                          {{8, flood}, {7, {framed(0x7e)}}},
                          {{8, {7}}}}) {
        playing.serialOut = captured;
        rig.block(playing);
        playing.ppq += 1024.0 / kBeat;
    }
    // A seek, a faster tempo across 1-frame and FL-style ragged blocks, then the transport stops.
    BlockIn fast{.ppq = 32.0, .tempo = 174.0, .playing = true};
    for (std::uint32_t frames : {33u, 1u, 222u, 1u, 7u, 4096u, 2u, 1u, 1u, 1u, 8192u}) {
        fast.frames = frames;
        rig.block(fast);
        fast.ppq += fast.tempo / 60.0 * frames / kRate;
    }
    rig.block({.ppq = fast.ppq, .tempo = 174.0, .playing = false, .midi = {{0, on(0, 25)}, {0, on(0, 26)}}});
    rig.run({.frames = 2048, .ppq = fast.ppq}, 2);
    CHECK(rig.seen.serialIn > 200);
    CHECK(rig.seen.buttons > 0);  // autoStart's START press and release
    CHECK(rig.seen.midiOut > 10);
    CHECK(rig.raised > 0);  // Arduinoboy's transport bytes and clocks, MI.MAP's clocks, behind a row byte
    rig.finish();
}

TEST_CASE("the kernel node drives risa and smsggdj host sync, and a NES's host MIDI, as today's kernel does",
          "[engine-graph][kernel-node]") {
    KernelRig rig({{routing("sendToAll")}, {nes(1, {kNesMidi, kRisa}), nes(2, {sms("sms")}), nes(3, {sms("gg")})}});
    rig.block({.midi = {{12, on(0, 60)}, {500, off(0, 60)}}});
    // A start partway into a phrase (an arm and START, flushing), clocks, a seek (a re-arm), an exact loop back to
    // the same place, a stop, and a restart at a new tempo.
    BlockIn play{.frames = 1024, .ppq = 3.25, .playing = true};
    rig.run(play, 8);
    rig.block({.ppq = 16.0, .playing = true, .midi = {{0, on(1, 50)}}});
    rig.block({.ppq = 16.0, .playing = true});
    rig.run({.frames = 777, .ppq = 16.0 + 1024.0 / kBeat, .playing = true}, 5);
    rig.block({.ppq = 20.0, .playing = false});
    BlockIn again{.ppq = 4.0, .tempo = 96.0, .playing = true};
    for (std::uint32_t frames : {1u, 1u, 33u, 222u, 7u, 4096u}) {
        again.frames = frames;
        rig.block(again);
        again.ppq += again.tempo / 60.0 * frames / kRate;
    }
    CHECK(rig.seen.bytes > 50);
    CHECK(rig.seen.midi > 0);
    CHECK(rig.raised == 0);
    rig.finish();
}

TEST_CASE("the kernel node runs a controller session as today's kernel does: its surface, its launches, its LEDs",
          "[engine-graph][kernel-node]") {
    // A Launchpad driving an emulated cart in MI.MAP (whose clock and launches go to its serial port), beside a
    // Game Boy decoding MI.OUT, so project-stage and system-stage host MIDI out interleave on one port.
    const auto structure = [](const std::string& target) {
        return Structure{{routing("sendToAll"), launchpad(target, 7, "bar")}, {gameBoy(7, lsdj("midiMap")), gameBoy(8, lsdj("midiOut"))}};
    };
    KernelRig rig(structure("system"));
    rig.block({.controller = {pad(0, 3)}});  // pressed with no surface attached
    rig.block({.connected = true});          // attached: the session takes it (Programmer mode, a full paint)
    rig.run({.connected = true}, 2);
    BlockIn play{.frames = 1024, .ppq = 0.0, .playing = true, .connected = true};
    play.controller = {pad(0, 0)};  // nothing playing yet: launched at once
    rig.block(play);
    play.ppq += 1024.0 / kBeat;
    play.controller = {pad(0, 5), pad(4, 2)};  // cued for the bar
    for (int i = 0; i < 100; ++i) {
        rig.block(play);
        play.controller.clear();
        play.ppq += 1024.0 / kBeat;
    }
    rig.block({.ppq = play.ppq, .playing = true, .connected = false});  // detached
    rig.block({.ppq = play.ppq, .playing = true, .connected = true});   // and back: repainted
    // Its launches to a real Game Boy's MIDI out instead (a new session, the predictor carried over), while the
    // other Game Boy's MI.OUT is decoded in the same blocks.
    rig.restructure(structure("midiOut"));
    play.controller = {pad(0, 6)};
    for (int i = 0; i < 40; ++i) {
        play.serialOut = {{8, {framed(0x7f), framed(0x71), framed(60)}}};
        rig.block(play);
        play.controller.clear();
        play.ppq += 1024.0 / kBeat;
    }
    CHECK(rig.seen.controllerOut > 20);
    CHECK(rig.seen.serialIn > 100);
    CHECK(rig.seen.midiOut > 40);
    rig.finish();
}

TEST_CASE("the kernel node keeps today's state across structure changes: survivors go on, a removed id is pruned",
          "[engine-graph][kernel-node]") {
    // Every change moves the node's ports, so each is a reshape: the instance is kept (the rig checks) and setSystems
    // runs at the swap. A clock that survives does not restart; an id removed and added again starts afresh.
    const Structure first{{routing("sendToAll")}, {gameBoy(1, lsdj("midiSync")), gameBoy(2, kMgb), gameBoy(3, lsdj("midiSyncArduinoboy"))}};
    KernelRig rig(first);
    BlockIn play{.frames = 1024, .ppq = 0.5, .playing = true, .midi = {{0, on(0, 24)}}};  // Arduinoboy: play
    rig.block(play);
    play.midi.clear();
    const auto step = [&](int blocks) {
        for (int i = 0; i < blocks; ++i) {
            play.ppq += 1024.0 / kBeat;
            rig.block(play);
        }
    };
    step(4);
    // A system added, which shifts no one's routing.
    rig.restructure({first.project, {first.systems[0], first.systems[1], first.systems[2], nes(4, {kNesMidi, kRisa})}});
    play.midi = {{10, on(0, 61)}};
    step(4);
    play.midi.clear();
    // A block is a little over one tick at 24 PPQN, so a playing clock sends at least one every block.
    const auto clocks = [&](std::uint32_t id) {
        const auto& sent = rig.node<Probe>("in-" + std::to_string(id)).bytes;
        return std::count_if(sent.begin(), sent.end(), [](const Message& m) { return m.data == Bytes{0xF8}; });
    };
    CHECK(clocks(3) > 0);
    // Arduinoboy's system removed, then added again: its play flag is gone, so it clocks nothing until note 24.
    rig.restructure({first.project, {first.systems[0], first.systems[1], nes(4, {kNesMidi, kRisa})}});
    step(3);
    rig.restructure({first.project, {first.systems[0], first.systems[1], nes(4, {kNesMidi, kRisa}), first.systems[2]}});
    step(3);
    CHECK(clocks(1) > 0);
    CHECK(clocks(3) == 0);
    // A feature-role edit on a survivor (its clock divided, its tick counter kept), and a new order, which moves
    // positional routing.
    rig.restructure({{routing("oneChannelPerInstance")},
                     {gameBoy(1, lsdj("midiSync", 4)), first.systems[2], nes(4, {kNesMidi, kRisa}), first.systems[1]}});
    for (int ch = 0; ch < 4; ++ch) {
        play.midi = {{static_cast<std::uint32_t>(ch), on(ch, 70)}};
        step(1);
    }
    // Everything removed, then one system back.
    rig.restructure({first.project, {}});
    step(2);
    rig.restructure({first.project, {first.systems[1]}});
    play.midi = {{0, on(0, 65)}};
    step(1);
    CHECK(rig.seen.serialIn > 50);
    CHECK(rig.seen.bytes > 10);
    rig.finish();
}

TEST_CASE("a throw in the kernel node's roles keeps what was sent before it and runs the next block, as today",
          "[engine-graph][kernel-node]") {
    // No shipped role throws on what the kernel accepts, so the throw is injected: run after both bundles, in both
    // runtimes, Math.ceil throws for one value, which walkTicks reaches when the second system's clock first syncs,
    // at ppq 10.5 (tick 252). The first system has forwarded its MIDI by then; the third never runs that block.
    const std::string inject = R"JS(
      (function () {
        var ceil = Math.ceil;
        Math.ceil = function (x) { if (x === 252) throw new Error("injected"); return ceil(x); };
      })();
    )JS";
    KernelRig rig({{routing("sendToAll")}, {gameBoy(1, kMgb), gameBoy(2, lsdj("midiSync")), gameBoy(3, kMgb)}}, inject);
    rig.block({.midi = {{0, on(0, 60)}}});
    rig.block({.ppq = 10.5, .playing = true, .midi = {{4, on(0, 62)}}});
    CHECK(rig.scripts.throwCount() == 1);
    rig.run({.ppq = 10.5 + 1024.0 / kBeat, .playing = true, .midi = {{4, on(0, 64)}}}, 3);
    CHECK(rig.seen.serialIn > 0);
    rig.finish(1);
}

TEST_CASE("the kernel node reshapes under a running audio thread, its instance kept through every structure change",
          "[engine-graph][kernel-node][stress]") {
    // Today's kernel is not run here: this is the threading of the real node, its settings committed and setSystems
    // run on the audio thread at each swap, while the control thread plans the next and reclaims the last.
    const std::vector<Structure> structures{
        {{routing("sendToAll")}, {gameBoy(1, lsdj("midiSync")), nes(2, {kNesMidi, kRisa})}},
        {{routing("sendToAll"), launchpad("system", 1, "bar")}, {gameBoy(1, lsdj("midiMap")), nes(2, {kNesMidi, kRisa}), gameBoy(3, kMgb)}},
        {{routing("oneChannelPerInstance")}, {gameBoy(3, kMgb)}},
        {{routing("sendToAll")}, {}},
    };
    KernelRig rig(structures[0]);
    rig.setAudioThreadOwns(true);
    std::atomic<bool> running{true};
    std::thread audio([&] {
        double ppq = 0.0;
        while (running.load()) {
            rig.scripts.beginBlock();
            rig.host->processBlock(512, rp_transport{kRate, 120.0, ppq, RP_TRANSPORT_PLAYING});
            ppq += 512.0 / kBeat;
            std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::microseconds(100));
        }
    });
    int refused = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < 200; ++i) {
        rig.structure = structures[static_cast<std::size_t>(i) % structures.size()];
        const auto r = rig.host->setGraph(rig.document());
        if (!r.ok) {
            REQUIRE(r.errors.at(0).code == "busy");
            ++refused;
        }
        rig.host->reclaim();
        rig.scripts.reclaim();
        std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::microseconds(150));
    }
    running = false;
    audio.join();
    rig.setAudioThreadOwns(false);
    CHECK(refused < 200);
    CHECK(rig.host->node("kernel") == rig.kernel);
    CHECK(rig.scripts.liveInstances() == 1);
    rig.finish();
}
````

Create `packages/retroplug/test-native/parity/kernel-node.test.ts`:

````ts
// The DSP kernel as a script node (docs/modular-graph-phase-b3a-design.md section 4) in a real Engine with real
// cores. mGB and a BlipToaster NES, each on its own pair of a 4-lane host, play the blocks groups' phrase, rendered
// twice from the same boot: through today's path (the stores' document, whose native rp.dsp.kernel runs the kernel
// stage on the structure they push through setSystems), and through a document built here from that one, the
// kernel node in place of the native kernel with the same structure as its settings, rp.host.midi-in into it and
// its outputs into each system's inputs, as buildGraph is to wire it. The audio is the same, sample for sample.
//
// Here among the parity files because the two renders must start from cores in the same state: the runner powers
// cores on in a fixed one for parity files only (RETROPLUG_DETERMINISTIC).
import { test, expect } from "../../testing/harness";
import { Rig, cycle, even, type Segment } from "./rig";
import { BOOT_MS, NES_CHANNELS, ROMS, frames, mgb, phrase } from "./scenes";
import { KERNEL_NODE_TYPE } from "../../src/script/kernelNode";
import type { KernelStructure } from "../../src/dspKernel";
import type { SetGraphRequest } from "../../src/backend";
import { toGraphJson, type GraphDocument } from "../../src/graph/graphDocument";

const SR = 48000;
const FOUR_LANES = { kind: "multi", channels: 4 } as const;
const rig = new Rig();

// The system inputs the kernel node feeds (design section 3.1).
const SYSTEM_INPUTS = ["serialIn", "midi", "bytes", "buttons"];

/** `request`'s document with the kernel node, set to `structure`, in place of the native kernel, and wired. */
function throughKernelNode(request: SetGraphRequest, structure: KernelStructure): SetGraphRequest {
  const doc = JSON.parse(request.document) as GraphDocument;
  const types = new Map(doc.nodes.map((n) => [n.id, n.type]));
  const settings = {
    project: structure.project ?? [],
    systems: structure.systems.map((s) => ({ ...s, serialOut: types.get(`sys-${s.id}`) === "rp.sameboy.gb" })),
  };
  const at = doc.nodes.findIndex((n) => n.type === "rp.dsp.kernel");
  expect(at, "the stores' document holds the native kernel").toBeGreaterThan(-1);
  doc.nodes.splice(at, 1, { id: "midi-in", type: "rp.host.midi-in" }, { id: "kernel", type: KERNEL_NODE_TYPE, settings });
  doc.wires.push({ from: "midi-in.midi", to: "kernel.midiIn" });
  for (const s of settings.systems) {
    for (const port of SYSTEM_INPUTS) doc.wires.push({ from: `kernel.sys-${s.id}.${port}`, to: `sys-${s.id}.${port}` });
    // MI.OUT's one block of latency, as the engine's gather gives it today.
    if (s.serialOut) doc.wires.push({ from: `sys-${s.id}.serialOut`, to: `kernel.sys-${s.id}.serialOut`, feedback: true });
  }
  return { document: toGraphJson(doc), slots: request.slots };
}

/** Boot the scene, render it, and return its lanes; through the kernel node when `viaNode`. */
function render(split: (n: number) => number[], viaNode: boolean): Float32Array[] {
  rig.reset(SR);
  const { backend, dsp } = rig.session;
  // The stores publish at the 4-lane shape the renders use, so a render sends no document of its own (which would
  // put the stores' document back in place of the one sent here).
  expect(rig.project.graph.setShape(FOUR_LANES)).toBe(true);
  const setGraph = backend.setGraph;
  const setSystems = dsp.setSystems;
  let request: SetGraphRequest | null = null;
  let structure: KernelStructure | null = null;
  backend.setGraph = (r) => ((request = r), setGraph(r));
  dsp.setSystems = (s) => ((structure = s), setSystems(s));
  try {
    mgb(rig);
    rig.add(ROMS.bliptoaster);
    rig.project.setAudioRouting("twoPerInstance");
  } finally {
    backend.setGraph = setGraph;
    dsp.setSystems = setSystems;
  }
  expect(request !== null && structure !== null, "the stores published a document and a structure").toBe(true);
  if (viaNode) {
    const r = setGraph(throughKernelNode(request!, structure!));
    expect(r.errors.map((e) => `${e.code} at ${e.nodeId}.${e.port}: ${e.message}`)).toEqual([]);
  }
  // sendToAll: both systems hear the phrase, mGB on its voices 0..3 and the NES on its channels 0..3.
  const segments: Segment[] = [
    { blocks: split(frames(SR, BOOT_MS)) },
    { blocks: split(frames(SR, 600)), midi: phrase(SR, NES_CHANNELS) },
  ];
  const parts = segments.map((seg) => {
    const r = rig.render(4, seg);
    expect(r.midiOut).toEqual([]);
    return r.lanes;
  });
  return [0, 1, 2, 3].map((l) => {
    const lane = new Float32Array(parts.reduce((n, p) => n + p[l].length, 0));
    let at = 0;
    for (const p of parts) {
      lane.set(p[l], at);
      at += p[l].length;
    }
    return lane;
  });
}

function rms(a: Float32Array, from: number): number {
  let s = 0;
  for (let i = from; i < a.length; i++) s += a[i] * a[i];
  return Math.sqrt(s / Math.max(1, a.length - from));
}

for (const [name, split] of [
  ["512-frame blocks", (n: number) => even(n, 512)],
  ["FL-style ragged blocks, 1-frame ones among them", (n: number) => cycle(n, [33, 1, 222, 1, 7, 4096, 2])],
] as const) {
  test(`mGB and a NES render the same through the kernel node as through today's kernel stage, in ${name}`, () => {
    const today = render(split, false);
    const node = render(split, true);
    for (let l = 0; l < 4; l++) {
      expect(node[l].length, `lane ${l}`).toBe(today[l].length);
      let first = -1;
      for (let i = 0; i < today[l].length && first < 0; i++) if (!Object.is(today[l][i], node[l][i])) first = i;
      expect(first, `lane ${l}: the first frame that differs`).toBe(-1);
      // Each system played the phrase: its pair sounds once the MIDI arrives, so the two did not agree on silence.
      expect(rms(today[l], frames(SR, BOOT_MS)), `lane ${l} sounds`).toBeGreaterThan(0.001);
    }
  });
}
````

````diff
+

+# DspRuntime at boot), by the same recipe, embedded only in retroplug-engine-graph-test (cmake/tests.cmake): the

+set(DSP_KERNEL_BUNDLE_JS "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/native/dsp-kernel-bundle.js")
````

Create `packages/retroplug/src/script/kernelNode.ts`:

````ts
// The DSP kernel as a script node (docs/modular-graph-phase-b3a-design.md section 4): today's DspKernel, with the
// registry the kernel bundle builds (dspKernelBundle.ts: the DSP roles, no core roles, no ROM providers), behind
// defineNode. Its settings are the kernel's structure plus one fact per system, whether it has a serialOut (a Game
// Boy); its ports follow from them and are named by system id, so a structure change is a reshape: the instance is
// kept, a surviving system's wires stay bound to its ports, and setSystems keeps today's rules (each surviving id's
// clock and role scratch, every project stage's state; a removed id pruned).
//
// Each block builds the BlockInput DspRuntime::processBlock builds today, field for field and afresh, and the
// kernel's sink calls go straight onto the output ports in emission order, where today's sink thunks append to
// vectors the engine fans out to the cores.
import { z } from "zod";
import { bytes, control, defineNode, events, startValue, type Block, type Message, type PortSpec } from "../graph/defineNode";
import type { QueueCapacity } from "../graph/descriptor";
import { DspKernel, type BlockInput, type DspTracer, type SinkTarget } from "../dspKernel";
import type { MidiEvent } from "../midiRouting";
import { RoleRegistry } from "../systemRoles";
import { registerDspRoles } from "../dspRoles";

/** The kernel node's type id. Its own is rp.dsp.kernel, which the native kernel stage holds until the engine
 *  switches over (a registry refuses a second type under one id); the switch deletes that node and this one takes
 *  the id, so a document that names rp.dsp.kernel with no settings plans as an empty kernel from then on. */
export const KERNEL_NODE_TYPE = "rp.dsp.kernel-script";

/** RP_MESSAGE_FLUSH (graph/rp_node.h): a bytes message the device takes only after dropping what it still holds. */
const FLUSH = 1;

// What each output carries in one block, at most (design section 2.6): today's sink vectors are unbounded, so these
// are sized from the most the suites send through them in one block. Measured over test:native with the fixtures
// (parity included, 2.2 million kernel blocks up to 8192 frames): per system, 18 serial-in bytes, 8 core-MIDI
// messages holding 4096 bytes (the largest message 512), 11 core-byte messages holding 11 bytes, 1 button press; 14
// host MIDI-out messages holding 70 bytes with their prefixes; 5 control-surface messages holding 206 bytes (in one).
// dsp-bench's densest profile, skipped there, sends 13 messages of 39 bytes a block. Each output has room for 16
// times the messages or more, and the bytes as well, but for core MIDI's (4 times the most measured, 32 of the largest
// message) and the MIDI out's (a decoded MI.OUT stream at its densest, a captured byte every 8 frames: 1024 in 8192).
// A queue costs 16 bytes a message plus its bytes, per plan.
export const KERNEL_SERIAL_IN: QueueCapacity = { messages: 1024, bytes: 1024 };
export const KERNEL_CORE_MIDI: QueueCapacity = { messages: 512, bytes: 16384 };
export const KERNEL_CORE_BYTES: QueueCapacity = { messages: 256, bytes: 1024 };
export const KERNEL_BUTTONS: QueueCapacity = { messages: 64, bytes: 128 };
export const KERNEL_MIDI_OUT: QueueCapacity = { messages: 1024, bytes: 8192 };
export const KERNEL_CONTROLLER_OUT: QueueCapacity = { messages: 256, bytes: 4096 };

const role = z.object({ kind: z.string(), config: z.record(z.string(), z.unknown()).default({}) });

const settings = z.object({
  /** The project-scope stages (MIDI routing, a controller session), run before every system. */
  project: z.array(role).default([]),
  /** Each system in slot order (positional routing reads it), its pipeline, and whether it has a serialOut. */
  systems: z
    .array(
      z.object({
        id: z.number().int().min(1).max(0xffffffff),
        pipeline: z.array(role).default([]),
        serialOut: z.boolean().default(false),
      }),
    )
    .refine((systems) => new Set(systems.map((s) => s.id)).size === systems.length, "two systems have the same id")
    .default([]),
});

export type KernelSettings = z.infer<typeof settings>;

/** One system's port ids, made once per settings so a sink call builds no string. */
interface SystemPorts {
  id: number;
  serialIn: string;
  midi: string;
  bytes: string;
  buttons: string;
  /** Its MI.OUT input, for a system with a serialOut. */
  serialOut: string | null;
}

const portsOf = (s: KernelSettings): SystemPorts[] =>
  s.systems.map(({ id, serialOut }) => ({
    id,
    serialIn: `sys-${id}.serialIn`,
    midi: `sys-${id}.midi`,
    bytes: `sys-${id}.bytes`,
    buttons: `sys-${id}.buttons`,
    serialOut: serialOut ? `sys-${id}.serialOut` : null,
  }));

// The per-role tracing thunks a profile build binds (spec/08-profiling.md Tier B; Engine.cpp, into the script host's
// audio context), the kernel bundle's three and traceArmed, the trace window's state, read each block in place of
// the bundle's __setTrace. `typeof` is safe on an unbound global, which is every other build.
declare function spanBegin(label: number): void;
declare function spanEnd(): void;
declare function traceName(label: number, kind: string): void;
declare function traceArmed(): boolean;
const traced = typeof spanBegin === "function" && typeof traceArmed === "function";

// The DSP roles alone, as the kernel bundle registers them: a behaviour keeps its state in the kernel's scratch
// bags, so every instance can share them.
const registry = new RoleRegistry();
registerDspRoles(registry);

// An events or bytes input as today's marshalling hands it to the kernel: fresh {frame, data} objects, `data` a plain
// array of numbers (a role may keep a reference across blocks, and may rely on what an array is).
function midiEvents(messages: readonly Message[]): MidiEvent[] {
  const out: MidiEvent[] = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < messages.length; i++) {
    const m = messages[i];
    const data: number[] = [];
    for (let j = 0; j < m.data.length; j++) data.push(m.data[j]);
    out.push({ frame: m.frame, data });
  }
  return out;
}

// The block's input, built as DspRuntime::processBlock builds it: the transport, controllerConnected only when true,
// midiIn, empty buttons and keys (no host feeds them yet), every system's MI.OUT bytes from last block in slot order,
// and controllerIn only when a surface sent something. Fresh every block, as today.
function blockInput(b: Block, systems: readonly SystemPorts[]): BlockInput {
  const t = b.transport;
  const input = {
    frames: b.frames,
    sampleRate: t.sampleRate,
    tempo: t.tempo,
    ppqStart: t.ppq,
    transport: t.playing,
  } as BlockInput;
  if (startValue(b.control("controllerConnected")) !== 0) input.controllerConnected = true;
  input.midiIn = midiEvents(b.messages("midiIn"));
  input.buttons = [];
  input.keys = [];
  const serialOut: BlockInput["serialOut"] = [];
  for (let s = 0; s < systems.length; s++) {
    const port = systems[s].serialOut;
    if (port === null) continue;
    const messages = b.messages(port);
    for (let i = 0; i < messages.length; i++) {
      const data = messages[i].data;
      for (let j = 0; j < data.length; j++) serialOut.push({ system: systems[s].id, byte: data[j] });
    }
  }
  input.serialOut = serialOut;
  const controllerIn = b.messages("controllerIn");
  if (controllerIn.length > 0) input.controllerIn = midiEvents(controllerIn);
  return input;
}

export const kernelNode = defineNode<KernelSettings>({
  id: KERNEL_NODE_TYPE,
  name: "DSP Kernel",
  category: "dsp",
  settings,
  reshapes: true,
  ports: (s) => {
    const p: Record<string, PortSpec> = {
      midiIn: events.in(),
      controllerIn: events.in(),
      controllerConnected: control.in(),
    };
    const systems = portsOf(s);
    for (const sys of systems) if (sys.serialOut) p[sys.serialOut] = bytes.in();
    for (const sys of systems) {
      p[sys.serialIn] = bytes.out(KERNEL_SERIAL_IN);
      p[sys.midi] = events.out(KERNEL_CORE_MIDI);
      p[sys.bytes] = bytes.out(KERNEL_CORE_BYTES);
      p[sys.buttons] = events.out(KERNEL_BUTTONS);
    }
    p.midiOut = events.out(KERNEL_MIDI_OUT);
    p.controllerOut = events.out(KERNEL_CONTROLLER_OUT);
    return p;
  },
  create: ({ settings: initial }) => {
    let systems = portsOf(initial);
    let byId = new Map(systems.map((s) => [s.id, s]));
    let block: Block | null = null; // the block being processed, which every sink call sends on
    const one = new Uint8Array(1);
    const press = new Uint8Array(2);
    const tagged: number[] = [];

    // Each kernel sink call onto its port, in emission order; a call naming a system with no ports is dropped, as
    // today's fan-out skips an id it cannot find. Values convert as the thunks convert them (each byte & 0xff).
    const sink: SinkTarget = {
      pushSerialIn: (system, frame, byte) => {
        const p = byId.get(system);
        if (!p) return;
        one[0] = byte;
        block!.send(p.serialIn, frame, one);
      },
      emitCoreMidi: (system, frame, data) => {
        const p = byId.get(system);
        if (p) block!.send(p.midi, frame, data);
      },
      pushCoreBytes: (system, frame, data, flush) => {
        const p = byId.get(system);
        if (p) block!.send(p.bytes, frame, data, flush ? FLUSH : 0);
      },
      // At frame 0, whatever the call says: the core takes a role's press with no frame (today's fan-out).
      pressButton: (system, _frame, button, down) => {
        const p = byId.get(system);
        if (!p) return;
        press[0] = button;
        press[1] = down ? 1 : 0;
        block!.send(p.buttons, 0, press);
      },
      // One port for every system, in emission order, each message behind its system's id, 4 bytes little-endian
      // (design section 4.4), which rp.host.midi-out strips into the message's system tag.
      emitMidiOut: (system, frame, data) => {
        tagged.length = 0;
        tagged.push(system & 0xff, (system >>> 8) & 0xff, (system >>> 16) & 0xff, (system >>> 24) & 0xff);
        for (let i = 0; i < data.length; i++) tagged.push(data[i]);
        block!.send("midiOut", frame, tagged);
      },
      emitControllerOut: (data) => {
        block!.send("controllerOut", 0, data);
      },
    };
    const tracer: DspTracer | undefined = traced
      ? { name: (label, kind) => traceName(label, kind), begin: (label) => spanBegin(label), end: () => spanEnd() }
      : undefined;
    const kernel = new DspKernel(registry, sink, tracer);
    kernel.setSystems(initial);

    return {
      // A throw goes to the script host, which counts it and runs this again next block: what the kernel sent
      // before it stands, as today.
      process(b) {
        block = b;
        if (tracer) kernel.setTracing(traceArmed());
        kernel.processBlock(blockInput(b, systems));
      },
      onSettings(next) {
        systems = portsOf(next);
        byId = new Map(systems.map((s) => [s.id, s]));
        kernel.setSystems(next);
      },
    };
  },
});
````

````diff
 namespace {

+#ifdef RETROPLUG_PROFILE
+// The per-role tracing thunks (spec/08-profiling.md Tier B) in the script host's audio context, where the kernel node
+// reads them as the native kernel reads its own: they record into the DspRuntime's trace window. traceArmed is that
+// window's state, which the node reads each block, having no __setTrace for traceReset to call.
+DspRuntime& traceOf(JSContext* ctx, JSValueConst* data) {
+    std::int64_t p = 0;
+    JS_ToInt64(ctx, &p, data[0]);
+    return *reinterpret_cast<DspRuntime*>(static_cast<std::intptr_t>(p));
+}
+JSValue spanBeginFn(JSContext* ctx, JSValueConst, int argc, JSValueConst* argv, int, JSValueConst* data) {
+    std::int32_t label = 0;
+    if (argc >= 1) JS_ToInt32(ctx, &label, argv[0]);
+    traceOf(ctx, data).spanBegin(static_cast<std::uint32_t>(label));
+    return JS_UNDEFINED;
+}
+JSValue spanEndFn(JSContext* ctx, JSValueConst, int, JSValueConst*, int, JSValueConst* data) {
+    traceOf(ctx, data).spanEnd();
+    return JS_UNDEFINED;
+}
+JSValue traceNameFn(JSContext* ctx, JSValueConst, int argc, JSValueConst* argv, int, JSValueConst* data) {
+    std::int32_t label = 0;
+    if (argc < 2) return JS_UNDEFINED;
+    JS_ToInt32(ctx, &label, argv[0]);
+    if (const char* name = JS_ToCString(ctx, argv[1])) {
+        traceOf(ctx, data).traceName(static_cast<std::uint32_t>(label), name);
+        JS_FreeCString(ctx, name);
+    }
+    return JS_UNDEFINED;
+}
+JSValue traceArmedFn(JSContext* ctx, JSValueConst, int, JSValueConst*, int, JSValueConst* data) {
+    return JS_NewBool(ctx, traceOf(ctx, data).traceArmed());
+}
+void bindTracing(void* dsp, JSContext* ctx, bool audioSide) {
+    if (!audioSide) return;
+    JSValue data = JS_NewInt64(ctx, static_cast<std::int64_t>(reinterpret_cast<std::intptr_t>(dsp)));
+    JSValue global = JS_GetGlobalObject(ctx);
+    JS_SetPropertyStr(ctx, global, "spanBegin", JS_NewCFunctionData(ctx, &spanBeginFn, 1, 0, 1, &data));
+    JS_SetPropertyStr(ctx, global, "spanEnd", JS_NewCFunctionData(ctx, &spanEndFn, 0, 0, 1, &data));
+    JS_SetPropertyStr(ctx, global, "traceName", JS_NewCFunctionData(ctx, &traceNameFn, 2, 0, 1, &data));
+    JS_SetPropertyStr(ctx, global, "traceArmed", JS_NewCFunctionData(ctx, &traceArmedFn, 0, 0, 1, &data));
+    JS_FreeValue(ctx, global);
+    JS_FreeValue(ctx, data);
+}
+constexpr rp::host::ScriptHost::Binder kScriptGlobals = &bindTracing;
+#else
+constexpr rp::host::ScriptHost::Binder kScriptGlobals = nullptr;
+#endif
+
 // The embedded script-node bundle (src/script/bundle.ts) every Engine loads unless it is built with another.
````

### Task 7: The flip - the kernel wired

Production runs the DSP kernel as the script node (design sections 3.5, 4, 5 and 7.2): every document TS builds
carries it, its structure as its settings, and nothing loads, pushes or fans out a kernel any more. One change,
accepted by strict parity: every file bit for bit, the blocks-tiny groups and the pinned master-sync cases included.
The prototype's run was bit-identical the first time. What changes, and why it keeps every output bit:

- **`buildGraph`.** The model gains each system's `pipeline` and the project's stages (`projectKernelStructure`'s,
  kept until B3b). The document gains `rp.host.midi-in` / `controller-in` into the kernel, `rp.dsp.kernel` (node id
  `kernel`) with `{ project, systems: { id, pipeline, serialOut } }` in slot order (`serialOut` for a Game Boy), each
  `kernel.sys-<id>.*` output into the system's input of that name, each Game Boy's `serialOut` back into the kernel
  as a feedback wire (MI.OUT's one block of latency), the kernel's MIDI and control-surface output into
  `rp.host.midi-out` / `controller-out`, and `rp.n8.cart-mirror` (`cart`, `{"system": <id>}`) from the first NES in
  slot order. The kernel runs before the systems because its wires say so, not because it is listed first. The 840
  goldens are re-recorded from `buildGraph` (every model gains an empty structure; the audio part of every document
  is unchanged), and the engine plans and runs each one with the embedded script kernel.
- **The engine.** The script kernel takes the id `rp.dsp.kernel`; the Engine no longer registers the native node,
  and its empty document is the stereo pair alone. The engine's MI.OUT gather goes (the Game Boy's `serialOut`
  carries it; left in place, with no native kernel to clear it, it would grow without bound once capture is
  armed), and a plan with no `rp.host.midi-in` (or `controller-in`) drops what was staged for the block instead of
  letting it grow. `rp.host.midi-in`'s output and the kernel's `sys-<id>.midi` carry 64 KiB of bytes, so a SysEx the
  host stages whole (a sample upload to a NES build) reaches the system whole.
- **The stores.** `ProjectStore.publishGraph` builds the structure (the controller projection moves in from
  `appHost`) and passes it with the systems, as one model, `EngineGraph.publish({ systems, routing, project })`. The
  systems store hands the kernel only the roles it runs (a role with a DSP behaviour), so a model, palette or asset
  edit leaves the document as it was; an edit to a role the kernel runs (an LSDj mode change), a MIDI-routing change,
  a controller edit and a polled song or start-edge change publish; a gain edit publishes nothing.
  `syncDspFromStore` and its `onSystemsChange` wiring go, the throwing load's catch included; `onSystemsChange`
  stays for the UI and the plugin's watched ROMs.
- **`DirectGraph`** gains `setPipeline(id, roles)` and `setProjectStages(stages)`, each a publish without a re-arm;
  a new or replacing system starts with no pipeline, and a refused edit puts the structure back.
- **Boot and the bundles.** `bootSession` and the plugin control plane load no kernel, and the session,
  control-plane and SDK bundles no longer bake one in (`dsp-runtime.test.ts`, which tests the old RPC seam, keeps
  its injection until Task 9). The session's `dsp` client stays until then.
- **The cart mirror.** The plugin's and the SDL host's raw-forward test and the cart mirror of a message staged at
  a system read the plan's `rp.n8.cart-mirror` (`cartMirrorSystemId`). `EngineCartMirror.test.cpp` runs on the
  kernel node and adds the case the merge review asked for: a message staged behind a reordered plan in one drain,
  judged against that plan. The comments that credited a BlipToaster host LFO with CC76-79 now name the routing and
  risa's sync.
- **Callers.** 30 store-built `test-native` files drop the kernel load and the sync hook; the direct ones move
  their `setSystems` pushes onto `setPipeline` / `setProjectStages` (three of them off a bare `SystemsStore` onto
  `DirectGraph`, the probe resetting the project stages per probe as its kernel reload did); the parity rig no
  longer reloads a kernel per case and fails a render that dropped a message; `render.ts` (the CLI `render` and the
  `RenderHost`) and the two NES export sessions lose their manual sync.
- **The deliberate change** (design 3.4, 7.2): `stageMidiIn` takes a frame (the RPC refuses one past
  `renderAudio`'s 1024-frame block), and `parity/host-midi-order` (replacing `parity/kernel-node`, whose comparison
  has no other side now) stages plugin-style notes then a frame-0 CC: a Game Boy now takes the CC before the notes,
  a NES at frame 0 as before, each rendering what the same messages staged in frame order render. `nes-core-bytes`
  sends a 60 KiB SysEx and requires it whole, with no drop (it drops at the kernel's old 16 KiB).
- Native tests that compared against the kernel stage now compare against in-order staging (HostIo), and the
  profile-only benches skip when the allocation counters, which read the native runtime, measure nothing (Task 9
  moves them).

**Files:** 108 files, by step below.
- Create: `packages/retroplug/test-native/parity/host-midi-order.test.ts`
- Delete: `packages/retroplug/test-native/parity/kernel-node.test.ts`

````diff
+TEST_CASE("a message staged at the cart is judged against the plan adopted ahead of it in the same drain",
+          "[audio][engine][n8]") {
+    // The ring carries a plan and the commands pushed after it in push order, and a command is applied against the
+    // plan current at its point of the drain. So a reorder that moves the mirror from system 1 to system 2, and a
+    // setting staged at each right behind it, send the cart system 2's and not 1's, though system 1 was the cart
+    // when they were staged.
+    Rig rig;
+    REQUIRE(rig.eng.setGraph(twoNes({1, 2}, 1)).ok);
+    rig.sink();
+    QueuedInvoker inv(rig.eng);
+    inv.setAudioThreadOwns(true);
+    REQUIRE(rig.eng.setGraph(twoNes({2, 1}, 2)).ok);  // queued: the audio thread adopts it at its next drain
+    CHECK(rig.eng.cartMirrorSystemId() == 1);           // still the running plan's
+    inv.stageSystemMidi(1, {0xF0, 0x7D, 0x01, 0xF7});
+    inv.stageSystemMidi(2, {0xF0, 0x7D, 0x02, 0xF7});
+    inv.drainInto(rig.eng);
+    CHECK(rig.eng.cartMirrorSystemId() == 2);
+    inv.setAudioThreadOwns(false);
+    REQUIRE(rig.cart.size() == 1);
+    CHECK(rig.cart[0].bytes == Bytes{0xF0, 0x7D, 0x02, 0xF7});
+}
````
