- [ ] **Step 8: Re-record the 840 `buildGraph` goldens**

The documents change on purpose. The goldens file has no update mode, so the prototype re-recorded it with a
one-off script: each case's model gains the kernel structure (no project stages, an empty pipeline per system), its
document is rebuilt, the distinct documents are re-indexed in first-appearance order, and it stops if any case's
slots or tap arm move. First keep the old file for the check that follows:

Run: `mkdir -p /tmp/b3proto/s6b && cp packages/retroplug/test/graph/golden/build-graph.json /tmp/b3proto/s6b/build-graph.before.json`
Expected: nothing printed.

Save the script as `/tmp/b3proto/s6b/regolden.ts` (from that directory its imports reach this worktree, `/workspaces/RetroPlug-main/cuttlefish`):

````ts
// Re-record test/graph/golden/build-graph.json from buildGraph: each case's model gains the kernel structure
// (no project stages, an empty pipeline per system), its document is rebuilt, and the distinct documents are
// re-indexed in first-appearance order. Slots and tap arms must not move.
import { readFileSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { buildGraph } from "../../../workspaces/RetroPlug-main/cuttlefish/packages/retroplug/src/graph/buildGraph";
import { canonicalJson } from "../../../workspaces/RetroPlug-main/cuttlefish/packages/retroplug/src/graph/canonicalJson";

const path = process.argv[2];
const golden = JSON.parse(readFileSync(path, "utf8"));
const docs: string[] = [];
const index = new Map<string, number>();
const cases = golden.cases.map((c: any) => {
  const model = { ...c.model, project: [], systems: c.model.systems.map((s: any) => ({ ...s, pipeline: [] })) };
  const built = buildGraph(model);
  if (canonicalJson(built.slots) !== canonicalJson(c.slots)) throw new Error(`${c.name}: slots moved`);
  if (canonicalJson(built.tapArm) !== canonicalJson(c.tapArm)) throw new Error(`${c.name}: tapArm moved`);
  const text = canonicalJson(built.document);
  let at = index.get(text);
  if (at === undefined) {
    at = docs.length;
    docs.push(text);
    index.set(text, at);
  }
  return canonicalJson({ ...c, model, document: at });
});
writeFileSync(path, `{"documents":[\n${docs.join(",\n")}\n],"cases":[\n${cases.join(",\n")}\n]}\n`);
console.log(`${cases.length} cases, ${docs.length} documents (was ${golden.documents.length})`);
````

Run: `node_modules/.bin/esbuild /tmp/b3proto/s6b/regolden.ts --bundle --platform=node --outfile=/tmp/b3proto/s6b/regolden.js --log-level=warning && node /tmp/b3proto/s6b/regolden.js packages/retroplug/test/graph/golden/build-graph.json`
Expected: `840 cases, 238 documents (was 238)`.

Then check that only the kernel's part of each document moved, and that the kernel lists its systems in slot order. Save as `/tmp/b3proto/s6b/check_goldens.py`:

````python
import json
old=json.load(open('/tmp/b3proto/s6b/build-graph.before.json'))
new=json.load(open('/workspaces/RetroPlug-main/cuttlefish/packages/retroplug/test/graph/golden/build-graph.json'))
AROUND={"midi-in","controller-in","kernel","cart","midi-out","controller-out"}
def audio(doc):
    nodes=[n for n in doc['nodes'] if n['id'] not in AROUND]
    def touches(e): return e.split('.',1)[0] in AROUND
    wires=[w for w in doc['wires'] if not touches(w['from']) and not touches(w['to'])]
    return json.dumps({'nodes':nodes,'wires':wires}, sort_keys=True)
bad=0
for co,cn in zip(old['cases'],new['cases']):
    assert co['name']==cn['name']
    if audio(old['documents'][co['document']])!=audio(new['documents'][cn['document']]): bad+=1; print('differs', co['name'])
    # the kernel lists the systems in slot order
    k=[n for n in new['documents'][cn['document']]['nodes'] if n['id']=='kernel'][0]
    assert [s['id'] for s in k['settings']['systems']]==cn['slots'], cn['name']
print('cases', len(new['cases']), 'audio differs in', bad)
````

Run: `python3 /tmp/b3proto/s6b/check_goldens.py`
Expected: `cases 840 audio differs in 0`.

````diff
+test("the kernel's settings are the structure, its systems in slot order with a Game Boy's serialOut", () => {

+  const kernel = g.node("kernel")!;
+  expect(kernel.type).toBe(KERNEL_NODE_TYPE);
+  expect(kernel.settings).toEqual({
+    project: [ROUTING],
+    systems: [
+      { id: 1, pipeline: [MGB], serialOut: true },
+      { id: 2, pipeline: [N8], serialOut: false },
+      { id: 3, pipeline: [], serialOut: true },

+test("the kernel takes the host's MIDI and control surface, feeds every system's inputs and gives the host its output", () => {
+  const g = built([gb(4), nes(7)]);

+  expect(wired("midi-in.midi", "kernel.midiIn")).toBe(true);
+  expect(wired("controller-in.midi", "kernel.controllerIn")).toBe(true);
+  expect(wired("controller-in.connected", "kernel.controllerConnected")).toBe(true);
+  for (const id of [4, 7])
+    for (const port of ["serialIn", "midi", "bytes", "buttons"]) expect(wired(`kernel.sys-${id}.${port}`, `sys-${id}.${port}`)).toBe(true);
+  expect(wired("kernel.midiOut", "midi-out.midi")).toBe(true);
+  expect(wired("kernel.controllerOut", "controller-out.midi")).toBe(true);
+  // MI.OUT comes back from the Game Boy a block later, and from nothing else.
+  const back = g.document.wires.filter((w) => w.to.endsWith(".serialOut"));

+  kernelSettings(back = 0): MockKernelSettings | undefined {
````

- [ ] **Step 12: The parity rig, and the new cases**

The rig fails a render that dropped a message and no longer reloads a kernel per case; `render-blocks` shares the session's graph; `nes-core-bytes` gains the 60 KiB SysEx; `plugin-controlplane` no longer expects a kernel load:

````diff

 });
+

+  // core it now rides the graph's queues: rp.host.midi-in's output, then the kernel's sys-<id>.midi for the NES
+  // (after the routing and the NES's MIDI forward), each sized to hold it (HostIoNodes.hpp kHostMidiInBytes,
+  // kernelNode.ts KERNEL_CORE_MIDI). A ROM that reads nothing keeps every byte the FIFO was handed.
+  const s = bootSession();
+  const path = "/tmp/rp-corebytes-sysex.nes";
+  expect(s.backend.writeFile(path, nromRom(parkAfter([])))).toBeTruthy();
+  const id = s.project.systems.addSystem(path);
+  if (id == null) throw new Error("addSystem failed");
+  s.audio.renderAudio(10); // let the ROM reach its parked loop
+  const before = s.audio.droppedMessages();
+
+  const sysex = new Uint8Array(60 * 1024);
+  for (let i = 1; i < sysex.length - 1; ++i) sysex[i] = i & 0x7f;
+  sysex[0] = 0xf0;
+  sysex[sysex.length - 1] = 0xf7;
+  expect(s.audio.stageMidiIn(sysex)).toBeTruthy();
+  s.audio.renderAudio(50);
+
+  const stats = s.backend.getCoreTransportStats(id);
+  s.project.systems.removeSystem(id);
+  expect(s.audio.droppedMessages() - before).toEqual(0);
+  expect(stats.rxDepth).toEqual(sysex.length);
+  expect(stats.droppedBytes).toEqual(0);
+});
````

Create `packages/retroplug/test-native/parity/host-midi-order.test.ts`:

````ts
// The one behaviour B3a changes on purpose (docs/modular-graph-phase-b3a-design.md sections 3.4 and 7.2): host MIDI
// staged out of frame order, as the plugin stages a block (the DAW's notes, then each moved automation slot's CC at
// frame 0), reaches every system in frame order, because rp.host.midi-in stable-sorts what is staged before the
// kernel reads it.
//
// - A Game Boy now takes the CC at the block's start, before the notes. Before B3a its serial queue, which releases
//   only the byte at its front, took the CC's bytes after the last note's, as if the CC were at that note's frame.
// - A NES takes the CC at frame 0, as before: its FIFO stable-sorted the same staging by frame.
//
// So for each, the plugin-style staging renders exactly what the same messages staged in frame order render, and
// something other than the CC staged at the last note's frame (the Game Boy's old behaviour), which shows the CC's
// place is audible. CC 1 on channel 1 is mGB's pulse width and BlipToaster's duty, so it changes both notes that
// follow it. Parity cannot hold this: renderBlocks refuses unsorted MIDI, so the staging goes through stageMidiIn.
//
// Among the parity files because the renders compared must start from cores in the same state: the runner powers
// cores on in a fixed one for parity files only (RETROPLUG_DETERMINISTIC).
import { test, expect } from "../../testing/harness";
import { Rig, even } from "./rig";
import { BOOT_MS, ROMS, frames, mgb } from "./scenes";

const SR = 48000;
const rig = new Rig();

type Staged = [frame: number, bytes: number[]][];
const NOTE_A: number[] = [0x90, 60, 100];
const NOTE_B: number[] = [0x90, 67, 100];
const DUTY: number[] = [0xb0, 1, 0];

/** The plugin's order: the block's notes, then the automation CC at frame 0. */
const PLUGIN_STYLE: Staged = [[100, NOTE_A], [300, NOTE_B], [0, DUTY]];
/** The same messages staged in frame order. */
const IN_ORDER: Staged = [[0, DUTY], [100, NOTE_A], [300, NOTE_B]];
/** The CC after the last note, at its frame: what a Game Boy took before. */
const CC_LAST: Staged = [[100, NOTE_A], [300, NOTE_B], [300, DUTY]];

/** Boot `place`'s system, stage `staged` for the next block through stageMidiIn, and render 400 ms from that block
 *  in 1024-frame ones; the left lane. */
function render(place: () => void, staged: Staged): Float32Array {
  rig.reset(SR);
  place();
  rig.render(2, { blocks: even(frames(SR, BOOT_MS), 1024) });
  for (const [frame, bytes] of staged) expect(rig.audio.stageMidiIn(bytes, frame), `staged at ${frame}`).toBe(true);
  return rig.render(2, { blocks: even(frames(SR, 400), 1024) }).lanes[0];
}

/** The first frame two renders differ at, or -1. */
function firstDifference(a: Float32Array, b: Float32Array): number {
  for (let i = 0; i < a.length; i++) if (!Object.is(a[i], b[i])) return i;
  return a.length === b.length ? -1 : a.length;
}

function rms(a: Float32Array): number {
  let s = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < a.length; i++) s += a[i] * a[i];
  return Math.sqrt(s / Math.max(1, a.length));
}

for (const [name, place] of [
  ["a Game Boy now takes the frame-0 CC before the notes", () => void mgb(rig)],
  ["a NES takes the frame-0 CC at frame 0, as before", () => void rig.add(ROMS.bliptoaster)],
] as const) {
  test(`plugin-style host MIDI reaches each system in frame order: ${name}`, () => {
    const plugin = render(place, PLUGIN_STYLE);
    const inOrder = render(place, IN_ORDER);
    const ccLast = render(place, CC_LAST);
    expect(rms(plugin), "the notes sound").toBeGreaterThan(0.001);
    expect(firstDifference(plugin, inOrder), "the first frame the plugin-style staging renders otherwise").toBe(-1);
    // From the first note on: before it, the CC has nothing to change.
    expect(firstDifference(plugin, ccLast)).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(100);
  });
}
````

````bash
Production runs the DSP kernel as the script node (docs/modular-graph-phase-b3a-design.md sections 3.5, 4, 5 and
7.2): every document TS builds carries it, its structure as its settings, and nothing loads, pushes or fans out a
kernel any more. Strict parity holds bit for bit, every file, the blocks-tiny groups and the pinned master-sync
cases included.

- buildGraph: the model gains each system's pipeline and the project's stages (projectKernelStructure's, kept). The
  document gains rp.host.midi-in / controller-in into the kernel, rp.dsp.kernel with { project, systems: { id,
  pipeline, serialOut } } in slot order (serialOut for a Game Boy), each kernel.sys-<id>.* output into the system's
  input of that name, each Game Boy's serialOut back as a feedback wire, the kernel's MIDI and control-surface output
  into rp.host.midi-out / controller-out, and rp.n8.cart-mirror ("cart", {"system": <id>}) from the first NES in slot
  order. The 840 goldens are re-recorded from buildGraph (every model gains an empty structure; the audio of all 840
  documents is unchanged), and the engine plans and runs each one with the embedded script kernel.
- The script kernel takes the id rp.dsp.kernel; the Engine no longer registers the native node, and its empty
  document is the stereo pair alone. The engine's MI.OUT gather is gone (the Game Boy's serialOut port carries it),
  and a plan with no rp.host.midi-in (controller-in) drops what was staged for the block instead of letting it grow.
- The stores: ProjectStore.publishGraph builds the structure (the controller projection moves in from appHost) and
  passes it with the systems. The systems store hands the kernel only the roles it runs (a role with a DSP
  behaviour), so a model, palette or asset edit leaves the document as it was; an edit to a role the kernel runs, a
  MIDI-routing change, a controller edit and a polled song or start-edge change publish; a gain edit publishes
  nothing. syncDspFromStore and its onSystemsChange wiring go, the throwing load's catch included; onSystemsChange
  stays for the UI and the plugin's watched ROMs. EngineGraph.publish takes the model as one object.
- DirectGraph: setPipeline(id, roles) and setProjectStages(stages), each a publish without a re-arm; a new or
  replacing system starts with no pipeline, and a refused edit puts the structure back.
- Callers: 30 store-built test-native files drop the kernel load and the sync hook (37 syncs); 20 direct ones move
  32 setSystems pushes onto setPipeline / setProjectStages (three of them off a bare SystemsStore onto DirectGraph,
````

### Task 8: The script-node cost bench

What B3b's node granularity depends on (design sections 6 and 7.4), measured while both kernels still exist: a
hidden `[.][bench]` case in `retroplug-engine-graph-test` at 44.1 kHz (a 1-frame block has 22.7 us), medians of 7
runs, the build type printed, asserting only that the work was done, never timing. It comes before the deletion
(design section 8 put it after) because it times the kernel node against the old kernel stage.

- Chains of 1, 4, 16 and 64 trivial TS nodes (an events pass-through written with indexed loops, `rp.bench.pass`)
  between a native source and sink, the source sending nothing or one message a block; a node's cost is the
  chain's less the source wired straight to the sink, over n.
- The kernel node in its plan against today's kernel stage (`DspRuntime::processBlock` and `runKernelStage`'s
  fan-out, driven as `KernelNode.test.cpp` drives them) over mGB, an LSDj in MIDI sync and a NES on `nes-n8-midi`,
  `sendToAll`, playing, a host message every 441 frames, each Game Boy's MI.OUT a byte every 8 frames; no core on
  either side, the two required to hand every system the same messages.
- `ScriptRig` takes a sample rate (48 kHz still its default).

Create `packages/native/test/engine-graph/ScriptBench.test.cpp`:

````cpp
// What a script node costs per block (docs/modular-graph-phase-b3a-design.md sections 6 and 7.4), at the block sizes
// a splitting host produces: 1 frame (FL Studio splits down to it), 64 and 512, at 44.1 kHz, where a 1-frame block
// has 22.7 us of real time. B3b's node granularity rests on these numbers: one protocol node per role multiplies the
// script calls a block makes by the node count.
//
// Two tables. The first is the fixed cost of a script node's process call, marshalling included: chains of 1, 4, 16
// and 64 trivial TS nodes (an events pass-through written with indexed loops) between a native source and sink, the
// source sending nothing or one message a block. A node's cost is the chain's less the source wired straight to the
// sink, over the node count. The second holds the kernel node in a plan against the kernel stage it replaced
// (DspRuntime::processBlock and Engine::runKernelStage's fan-out), both driven as KernelNode.test.cpp drives them,
// over one structure and input: mGB, an LSDj in MIDI sync and a NES on nes-n8-midi, every host message to all three,
// the transport playing, a steady MIDI stream, and each Game Boy's MI.OUT as its system node carries it. Neither
// side runs a core: today's fan-out counts each message where it would hand it to the core, and the plan's system
// stand-ins count what reaches their inputs. The plan's native nodes alone (the same document with no kernel) are
// timed too, so the kernel node's own share shows.
//
// Each figure is a median of kRuns runs; a kernel run times today's stage, then the node over the same blocks.
// Allocations are per block over every run: JS from the script host's audio runtime (today's runtime counts only in a
// RETROPLUG_PROFILE build), native on the calling thread (CountingAllocator). It asserts that the work was done (the
// messages came through, the two kernels delivered the same), never a time.
//
// Hidden from the normal run. Run it on its own: build/bin/retroplug-engine-graph-test "[bench]"

#include <algorithm>
#include <chrono>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <cstdio>
#include <iterator>
#include <memory>
#include <string>
#include <utility>
#include <vector>

#include <catch2/catch_test_macros.hpp>

#include "../graph/CountingAllocator.hpp"
#include "ScriptRig.hpp"
#include "graph/GraphHost.hpp"
#include "graph/HostNodes.hpp"
#include "graph/Queue.hpp"
#include "graph/nodes/CoreNodes.hpp"
#include "host/dsp/DspRuntime.hpp"
#include "host/graph/HostIoNodes.hpp"
#include "host/graph/HostServices.hpp"
#include "host/script/ScriptHost.hpp"

// Today's kernel bundle (cmake/bundles.cmake, retroplug-dsp-kernel-bundle).
extern "C" {
extern const std::uint8_t  rp_dsp_kernel_bundle[];
extern const std::uint32_t rp_dsp_kernel_bundle_size;
}

using rp::host::ScriptAllocations;
using rp::host::ScriptHost;
using rp::host::test::ScriptRig;
namespace gt = rp::graph::test;

namespace {

using Bytes = std::vector<std::uint8_t>;

constexpr double        kRate = 44100.0;
constexpr double        kBudgetUs = 1e6 / kRate;  // a 1-frame block's real time
constexpr double        kTempo = 120.0;
constexpr int           kRuns = 7;
constexpr int           kWarm = 64;  // blocks run before the first timed one
constexpr std::uint32_t kMaxFrames = 512;
constexpr std::uint32_t kBlockSizes[] = {1, 64, 512};

// Release and RelWithDebInfo both define NDEBUG, and nothing in the source tells them apart.
#ifdef NDEBUG
constexpr const char* kBuild = "NDEBUG (release or RelWithDebInfo)";
#else
constexpr const char* kBuild = "debug (numbers not comparable)";
#endif

using Clock = std::chrono::steady_clock;
double usSince(Clock::time_point t0) { return std::chrono::duration<double, std::micro>(Clock::now() - t0).count(); }
double median(std::vector<double> v) {
    std::sort(v.begin(), v.end());
    return v[v.size() / 2];
}
double percentOfBudget(double us) { return 100.0 * us / kBudgetUs; }

// What a stretch of blocks allocated, per block.
struct Allocations {
    bool   counted = true;  // false: the JS runtime does not count (today's, off-profile)
    double js = 0.0;        // JS allocations and reallocations
    double jsBytes = 0.0;
    double native = 0.0;    // operator new, on the calling thread
};

Allocations scriptDelta(const ScriptAllocations& a, const ScriptAllocations& b, int native, double blocks) {
    return {true, static_cast<double>(b.allocs + b.reallocs - a.allocs - a.reallocs) / blocks,
            static_cast<double>(b.bytes - a.bytes) / blocks, native / blocks};
}

void printAllocations(const Allocations& a) {
    if (a.counted) std::printf(" | %9.2f %9.1f", a.js, a.jsBytes);
    else std::printf(" | %9s %9s", "n/a", "n/a");
    std::printf(" %9.2f", a.native);
}

// ---- trivial nodes in a chain -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

constexpr int kChainBlocks = 8192;  // a run
constexpr int kChainLengths[] = {0, 1, 4, 16, 64};

// Events straight through, as cheaply as a script node can be written.
const char* const kPass = R"JS(
rp.register([rp.defineNode({
  id: "rp.bench.pass",
  ports: { in: rp.events.in(), out: rp.events.out() },
  create: () => ({
    process(b) {
      const ms = b.messages("in");
      for (let i = 0; i < ms.length; ++i) b.send("out", ms[i].frame, ms[i].data, ms[i].flags);
    },
  }),
})]);
)JS";

std::string node(const std::string& id, const std::string& type, const std::string& settings = "") {
    return R"({"id":")" + id + R"(","type":")" + type + "\"" + (settings.empty() ? "" : R"(,"settings":)" + settings) + "}";
}
std::string wire(const std::string& from, const std::string& to) { return R"({"from":")" + from + R"(","to":")" + to + "\"}"; }
std::string graphJson(const std::vector<std::string>& nodes, const std::vector<std::string>& wires) {
    std::string doc = R"({"nodes":[)";
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < nodes.size(); ++i) doc += (i ? "," : "") + nodes[i];
    doc += R"(],"wires":[)";
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < wires.size(); ++i) doc += (i ? "," : "") + wires[i];
    return doc + "]}";
}

// `n` pass nodes between a source and a sink: rp.test.source's events (a note-on a block) for `message`, else
// rp.test.feed's midi output, which sends nothing unless a test queues it.
std::string chain(bool message, int n) {
    std::vector<std::string> nodes{message ? node("src", "rp.test.source") : node("feed", "rp.test.feed"),
                                   node("sink", "rp.test.sink")};
    std::vector<std::string> wires;
    std::string from = message ? "src.events" : "feed.midi";
    for (int k = 1; k <= n; ++k) {
        const std::string id = "p" + std::to_string(k);
        nodes.push_back(node(id, "rp.bench.pass"));
        wires.push_back(wire(from, id + ".in"));
        from = id + ".out";
    }
    wires.push_back(wire(from, "sink.events"));
    return graphJson(nodes, wires);
}

struct ChainRow {
    double      us = 0.0;  // per block
    Allocations allocations;
};

ChainRow timeChain(bool message, int n, std::uint32_t frames) {
    ScriptRig rig(kPass, kMaxFrames, kRate);
    const auto r = rig.set(chain(message, n));
    INFO(ScriptRig::codes(r));
    REQUIRE(r.ok);
    rig.run(frames, kWarm);
    std::vector<double> us;
    int native = 0;
    const ScriptAllocations before = rig.scripts.audioAllocations();
    for (int run = 0; run < kRuns; ++run) {
        rp::test::beginCountingAllocations();
        const auto t0 = Clock::now();
        rig.run(frames, kChainBlocks);
        us.push_back(usSince(t0) / kChainBlocks);
        native += rp::test::endCountingAllocations().allocations;
        // Every block ran, and the last one's message came through every node.
        const auto& sink = rig.node<gt::Sink>("sink");
        REQUIRE(sink.blocks == static_cast<std::uint32_t>(kWarm + (run + 1) * kChainBlocks));
        REQUIRE(sink.eventCount == (message ? 1u : 0u));
    }
    REQUIRE(rig.scripts.liveInstances() == static_cast<std::uint32_t>(n));
    REQUIRE(rig.scripts.throwCount() == 0);
    return {median(us), scriptDelta(before, rig.scripts.audioAllocations(), native, double{kRuns} * kChainBlocks)};
}

// ---- the kernel ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

// A run, by block size: a few seconds of audio but at 1 frame, and enough blocks to time there.
int kernelBlocks(std::uint32_t frames) { return frames == 1 ? 32768 : frames == 64 ? 8192 : 2048; }

// kernelProjection's structure for the three: each pipeline holds only the roles with a DSP behaviour, the project
// MIDI routing sending every message to all of them. The node's settings add which systems have a serialOut.
struct BenchSystem {
    std::uint32_t id;
    const char*   pipeline;
    bool          gameBoy;
};
const BenchSystem kSystems[] = {
    {1, R"([{"kind":"mgb","config":{}}])", true},
    {2, R"([{"kind":"lsdj-sync","config":{"mode":"midiSync","tempoDivisor":1,"autoStart":false}}])", true},
    {3, R"([{"kind":"nes-n8-midi","config":{}}])", false},
};
constexpr std::size_t kSystemCount = std::size(kSystems);

std::string structureJson(bool settings) {
    std::string out = R"({"project":[{"kind":"midi-routing","config":{"mode":"sendToAll"}}],"systems":[)";
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < kSystemCount; ++i) {
        out += (i ? "," : "") + std::string(R"({"id":)") + std::to_string(kSystems[i].id) + R"(,"pipeline":)" +
               kSystems[i].pipeline;
        if (settings) out += std::string(R"(,"serialOut":)") + (kSystems[i].gameBoy ? "true" : "false");
        out += "}";
    }
    return out + "]}";
}

// The host MIDI: a message every kMidiEvery frames (100 a second), message m at frame m * kMidiEvery from the start, a
// note on and then its note off, on channels 0 to 3 in turn.
constexpr std::uint64_t kMidiEvery = 441;

Bytes hostMessage(std::uint64_t m) {
    const auto channel = static_cast<std::uint8_t>((m / 2) % 4), key = static_cast<std::uint8_t>(48 + (m / 2) % 24);
    if (m % 2 == 0) return {static_cast<std::uint8_t>(0x90 | channel), key, 100};
    return {static_cast<std::uint8_t>(0x80 | channel), key, 0};
}

// Block k's staged host MIDI, frame-ordered, as the engine stages it.
void stage(std::uint64_t k, std::uint32_t frames, std::vector<DspRuntime::MidiIn>& out) {
    out.clear();
    const std::uint64_t start = k * frames, end = start + frames;
    for (std::uint64_t m = (start + kMidiEvery - 1) / kMidiEvery; m * kMidiEvery < end; ++m)
        out.push_back({static_cast<std::uint32_t>(m * kMidiEvery - start), hostMessage(m)});
}

double ppqAt(std::uint64_t frame) { return kTempo / 60.0 * static_cast<double>(frame) / kRate; }

// The bytes a Game Boy's serial port clocks out over `frames` from frame `at` while its ROM holds a transfer open (mGB
// always does): one every 8 frames, the most its serialOut carries. Both Game Boys here clock at that rate, and what
// they send is the idle line, which neither role decodes.
std::uint32_t clocked(std::uint64_t at, std::uint32_t frames) { return static_cast<std::uint32_t>((at + frames) / 8 - at / 8); }
constexpr std::uint8_t kIdle[1] = {0xFF};

// What reached a system, by its input.
struct Counts {
    std::uint64_t serialIn = 0, midi = 0, bytes = 0, buttons = 0;
    bool operator==(const Counts&) const = default;
};

// Stands in for a system node: its four inputs, each message counted where the node would hand it to its core.
struct SystemInputs {
    static constexpr const char* id = "rp.bench.system";
    struct {
        rp::bytes_in  serialIn;
        rp::events_in midi;
        rp::bytes_in  bytes;
        rp::events_in buttons;
    } inputs;
    Counts counts;
    void process(const rp::Block&) noexcept {
        counts.serialIn += inputs.serialIn.messages().size();
        counts.midi += inputs.midi.messages().size();
        counts.bytes += inputs.bytes.messages().size();
        counts.buttons += inputs.buttons.messages().size();
    }
};

// Stands in for a Game Boy node's serialOut: what its core clocked out in the block, a byte a message at frame 0.
struct SerialOut {
    static constexpr const char* id = "rp.bench.serial-out";
    struct {
        rp::bytes_out serialOut;
    } outputs;
    std::uint64_t at = 0;  // frames run
    void process(const rp::Block& b) noexcept {
        for (std::uint32_t n = clocked(at, b.frames()); n > 0; --n) outputs.serialOut.push(0, kIdle);
        at += b.frames();
    }
};

const rp_package* benchPackage() {
    static const rp_node_type* const kTypes[] = {rp::node_type<SystemInputs>(), rp::node_type<SerialOut>()};
    static const rp_package kPackage{RP_ABI_VERSION, R"({"id":"rp.bench"})", static_cast<std::uint32_t>(std::size(kTypes)),
                                     kTypes};
    return &kPackage;
}

// Today's kernel and the kernel node, each fed the same blocks.
struct KernelBench {
    std::uint32_t frames;
    DspRuntime    today;
    // Before the graph, so it is destroyed after it: the kernel's shim hands its instance back to it.
    ScriptHost               scripts;
    rp::graph::NodeRegistry  registry;
    rp::graph::ResourceTable resources;
    // The engine's host I/O, standing in: what is staged for the block, and the host outputs counted.
    const std::vector<DspRuntime::MidiIn>* staged = nullptr;
    std::uint64_t                          midiOut = 0, controllerOut = 0;
    rp::host::EngineHostIo hostIo{this, &takeMidi, &takeNothing, &disconnected, &countMidiOut, &countControllerOut, &noCart};
    std::unique_ptr<rp::graph::GraphHost> host;
    // Today's side: the MI.OUT the engine gathered for the block, and what the fan-out handed each core.
    std::vector<DspRuntime::SerialOut> serialOut;
    Counts                             todayCounts[kSystemCount];

    // `kernel`: false for the plan's native nodes alone.
    KernelBench(std::uint32_t blockFrames, bool kernel) : frames(blockFrames) {
        REQUIRE(today.loadKernel(Bytes(rp_dsp_kernel_bundle, rp_dsp_kernel_bundle + rp_dsp_kernel_bundle_size)));
        const std::string structure = structureJson(false);
        REQUIRE(today.setSystems(Bytes(structure.begin(), structure.end())));
        const std::vector<ScriptHost::Chunk> chunks{ScriptHost::embeddedBundle()};
        std::string error;
        const bool loaded = scripts.load(chunks, &error);
        INFO(error);
        REQUIRE(loaded);
        for (const rp_package* p : {rp::graph::corePackage(), rp::graph::hostPackage(), rp::host::hostIoPackage(), benchPackage(),
                                    scripts.package()})
            REQUIRE(registry.addPackage(p, &error));
        rp::graph::HostConfig config;
        config.sampleRate = kRate;
        config.maxFrames = kMaxFrames;
        config.interfaces = [](void* ctx, const char* id) -> const void* {
            return std::string(id) == RP_ENGINE_HOST_IO_INTERFACE ? &static_cast<KernelBench*>(ctx)->hostIo : nullptr;
        };
        config.interfacesCtx = this;
        host = std::make_unique<rp::graph::GraphHost>(registry, resources, config);
        const auto r = host->setGraph(document(kernel));
        for (const auto& e : r.errors) UNSCOPED_INFO(e.code << " at " << e.nodeId << "." << e.port << ": " << e.message);
        REQUIRE(r.ok);
        serialOut.reserve(2 * kMaxFrames);
    }
    ~KernelBench() { host.reset(); }

    // As buildGraph wires it: the host I/O nodes into the kernel, each Game Boy's serialOut into it, its outputs to
    // each system's inputs, and on to the host outputs.
    static std::string document(bool kernel) {
        std::vector<std::string> nodes{node("midi-in", "rp.host.midi-in"), node("controller-in", "rp.host.controller-in"),
                                       node("midi-out", "rp.host.midi-out"), node("controller-out", "rp.host.controller-out")};
        std::vector<std::string> wires;
        if (kernel) {
            nodes.push_back(node("kernel", "rp.dsp.kernel", structureJson(true)));
            wires = {wire("midi-in.midi", "kernel.midiIn"), wire("controller-in.midi", "kernel.controllerIn"),
                     wire("controller-in.connected", "kernel.controllerConnected"), wire("kernel.midiOut", "midi-out.midi"),
                     wire("kernel.controllerOut", "controller-out.midi")};
        }
        for (const BenchSystem& s : kSystems) {
            const std::string id = "sys-" + std::to_string(s.id), port = "kernel." + id;
            nodes.push_back(node(id, "rp.bench.system"));
            if (s.gameBoy) nodes.push_back(node(id + "-serial", "rp.bench.serial-out"));
            if (!kernel) continue;
            if (s.gameBoy) wires.push_back(wire(id + "-serial.serialOut", port + ".serialOut"));
            for (const char* in : {"serialIn", "midi", "bytes", "buttons"}) wires.push_back(wire(port + "." + in, id + "." + in));
        }
        return graphJson(nodes, wires);
    }

    // ---- today: DspRuntime::processBlock and runKernelStage's fan-out --------------------------------------------
    void todayBlock(std::uint64_t k, const std::vector<DspRuntime::MidiIn>& midi) {
        const std::uint64_t at = k * frames;
        serialOut.clear();
        for (const BenchSystem& s : kSystems)
            if (s.gameBoy)
                for (std::uint32_t n = clocked(at, frames); n > 0; --n) serialOut.push_back({s.id, kIdle[0]});
        today.midiOut_.clear();  // the engine clears the host outputs at the top of its block
        today.controllerOut_.clear();
        today.processBlock(midi, kNoButtons, kNoKeys, serialOut, kNoMidi,
                           DspRuntime::BlockInfo{frames, kRate, kTempo, ppqAt(at), true, false});
        midiOut += today.midiOut_.size();
        controllerOut += today.controllerOut_.size();
        // The fan-out, each core call a count: serial-in, then core MIDI, then core bytes, then buttons, each in
        // emission order, the system found by id.
        for (const auto& e : today.serialIn_)
            if (Counts* c = todayFor(e.system)) ++c->serialIn;
        for (const auto& e : today.coreMidi_)
            if (Counts* c = e.data.empty() ? nullptr : todayFor(e.system)) ++c->midi;
        for (const auto& e : today.coreBytes_)
            if (Counts* c = e.data.empty() ? nullptr : todayFor(e.system)) ++c->bytes;
        for (const auto& e : today.buttonOut_)
            if (Counts* c = todayFor(e.system)) ++c->buttons;
    }
    Counts* todayFor(std::uint32_t id) {
        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < kSystemCount; ++i)
            if (kSystems[i].id == id) return &todayCounts[i];
        return nullptr;
    }

    // ---- the node, in its plan, as the engine runs a block -------------------------------------------------------
    void nodeBlock(std::uint64_t k, const std::vector<DspRuntime::MidiIn>& midi) {
        staged = &midi;
        scripts.beginBlock();
        host->processBlock(frames, rp_transport{kRate, kTempo, ppqAt(k * frames), RP_TRANSPORT_PLAYING});
    }
    Counts nodeCounts(std::size_t i) const {
        return rp::peer_as<SystemInputs>(host->node("sys-" + std::to_string(kSystems[i].id)))->counts;
    }

    static KernelBench& of(void* ctx) { return *static_cast<KernelBench*>(ctx); }
    // As the engine's: the staging, frame-ordered, onto the queue.
    static void takeMidi(void* ctx, rp_queue* out) {
        for (const auto& m : *of(ctx).staged) rp::graph::pushMessage(*out, m.frame, m.data);
    }
    static void takeNothing(void*, rp_queue*) {}
    static bool disconnected(void*) { return false; }
    static void countMidiOut(void* ctx, std::uint32_t, std::uint32_t, const std::uint8_t*, std::size_t) { ++of(ctx).midiOut; }
    static void countControllerOut(void* ctx, const std::uint8_t*, std::size_t) { ++of(ctx).controllerOut; }
    static void noCart(void*, std::uint32_t, const std::uint8_t*, std::size_t, bool) {}

    inline static const std::vector<DspRuntime::MidiIn>     kNoMidi{};
    inline static const std::vector<DspRuntime::ButtonIn>   kNoButtons{};
    inline static const std::vector<DspRuntime::KeyIn>      kNoKeys{};
};

struct KernelRow {
    double      us = 0.0;  // per block
    Allocations allocations;
};

struct KernelRows {
    KernelRow     today, node, plan;  // plan: the node's plan with no kernel in it
    Counts        delivered;          // to every system, by input, over every block run
    std::uint64_t blocks = 0;         // run, warm-up included
};

KernelRows timeKernel(std::uint32_t frames) {
    const int blocks = kernelBlocks(frames);
    KernelRows rows;
    KernelBench bench(frames, true), plan(frames, false);
    // Block k's staging, for the run's blocks, made before the run.
    std::vector<std::vector<DspRuntime::MidiIn>> staged(static_cast<std::size_t>(std::max(blocks, kWarm)));
    const auto prepare = [&](std::uint64_t first, int count) {
        for (int i = 0; i < count; ++i) stage(first + static_cast<std::uint64_t>(i), frames, staged[static_cast<std::size_t>(i)]);
    };
    // One side over `count` blocks from block `first`: its time per block, its native allocations added to `native`.
    const auto runSide = [&](auto&& block, std::uint64_t first, int count, int& native) {
        rp::test::beginCountingAllocations();
        const auto t0 = Clock::now();
        for (int i = 0; i < count; ++i) block(first + static_cast<std::uint64_t>(i), staged[static_cast<std::size_t>(i)]);
        const double us = usSince(t0) / count;
        native += rp::test::endCountingAllocations().allocations;
        return us;
    };
    const auto todayBlock = [&](std::uint64_t k, const auto& midi) { bench.todayBlock(k, midi); };
    const auto nodeBlock = [&](std::uint64_t k, const auto& midi) { bench.nodeBlock(k, midi); };
    const auto planBlock = [&](std::uint64_t k, const auto& midi) { plan.nodeBlock(k, midi); };

    int ignored = 0;
    prepare(0, kWarm);
    runSide(todayBlock, 0, kWarm, ignored);
    runSide(nodeBlock, 0, kWarm, ignored);
    runSide(planBlock, 0, kWarm, ignored);

    std::vector<double> todayUs, nodeUs, planUs;
    int nativeToday = 0, nativeNode = 0, nativePlan = 0;
    bench.today.resetAllocStats(false);  // a window for today's runtime, which counts only in a profile build
    const ScriptAllocations nodeBefore = bench.scripts.audioAllocations(), planBefore = plan.scripts.audioAllocations();
    std::uint64_t k = kWarm;
    for (int run = 0; run < kRuns; ++run, k += static_cast<std::uint64_t>(blocks)) {
        prepare(k, blocks);
        todayUs.push_back(runSide(todayBlock, k, blocks, nativeToday));
        nodeUs.push_back(runSide(nodeBlock, k, blocks, nativeNode));
        planUs.push_back(runSide(planBlock, k, blocks, nativePlan));
    }
    const double measured = double{kRuns} * blocks;
    rows.today.us = median(todayUs);
    const DspAllocStats stats = bench.today.allocStats();
    if (stats.enabled) {
        REQUIRE(stats.blockCount == static_cast<std::uint64_t>(measured));
        rows.today.allocations = {true, static_cast<double>(stats.allocCalls + stats.reallocCalls) / measured,
                                  static_cast<double>(stats.allocBytes) / measured, nativeToday / measured};
    } else {
        rows.today.allocations = {false, 0.0, 0.0, nativeToday / measured};
    }
    rows.node = {median(nodeUs), scriptDelta(nodeBefore, bench.scripts.audioAllocations(), nativeNode, measured)};
    rows.plan = {median(planUs), scriptDelta(planBefore, plan.scripts.audioAllocations(), nativePlan, measured)};

    // The two kernels handed every system the same messages, and there were some.
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < kSystemCount; ++i) {
        INFO("system " << kSystems[i].id);
        const Counts got = bench.nodeCounts(i), expected = bench.todayCounts[i];
        CHECK(got == expected);
        rows.delivered.serialIn += got.serialIn;
        rows.delivered.midi += got.midi;
        rows.delivered.bytes += got.bytes;
        rows.delivered.buttons += got.buttons;
        CHECK(plan.nodeCounts(i) == Counts{});
    }
    CHECK(bench.todayCounts[0].serialIn > 0);  // mGB: the host MIDI, a byte a message
    CHECK(bench.todayCounts[1].serialIn > 0);  // the LSDj: its clocks
    CHECK(bench.todayCounts[2].midi > 0);      // the NES: the host MIDI
    CHECK(bench.midiOut == 0);                 // nothing here sends host MIDI out
    CHECK(bench.host->droppedMessages() == 0);
    CHECK(bench.scripts.throwCount() == 0);
    CHECK(bench.scripts.liveInstances() == 1);
    rows.blocks = k;
    return rows;
}

// A time per block, with the share it takes of a 1-frame block's real time and of its own block's.
void printTime(double us, std::uint32_t frames) {
    std::printf(" | %9.3f %8.1f%% %8.2f%%", us, percentOfBudget(us), percentOfBudget(us) / frames);
}

void chainTable() {
    std::printf("\nchains of n pass-through TS nodes (rp.bench.pass) between a native source and sink, %d blocks a run\n",
                kChainBlocks);
    std::printf("input: rp.test.feed (nothing) or rp.test.source (one note-on a block); a node = (the chain - the source "
                "wired straight to the sink) / n\n");
    std::printf("%-7s %6s %5s | %9s %9s %9s | %9s %9s | %9s %9s %9s\n", "input", "frames", "nodes", "us/block", "%1-frame",
                "%own", "us/node", "%1-frame", "JS allocs", "JS bytes", "native");
    for (const bool message : {false, true}) {
        for (const std::uint32_t frames : kBlockSizes) {
            double baseline = 0.0;
            for (const int n : kChainLengths) {
                const ChainRow row = timeChain(message, n, frames);
                if (n == 0) baseline = row.us;
                std::printf("%-7s %6u %5d", message ? "1 msg" : "nothing", frames, n);
                printTime(row.us, frames);
                const double perNode = n == 0 ? 0.0 : (row.us - baseline) / n;
                if (n == 0) std::printf(" | %9s %9s", "-", "-");
                else std::printf(" | %9.3f %8.1f%%", perNode, percentOfBudget(perNode));
                printAllocations(row.allocations);
                std::printf("\n");
            }
        }
    }
}

void kernelTable() {
    std::printf("\nthe kernel node against today's kernel stage: mGB, an LSDj in MIDI sync and a NES on nes-n8-midi, routing "
                "sendToAll; playing at %.0f bpm; a host message every %llu frames; each Game Boy's MI.OUT a byte every 8 "
                "frames\n",
                kTempo, static_cast<unsigned long long>(kMidiEvery));
    std::printf("today: DspRuntime::processBlock + runKernelStage's fan-out; node: its plan (the host I/O nodes, the kernel "
                "node, each Game Boy's serialOut, a stand-in for each system's inputs); plan: that plan with no kernel\n");
    std::printf("no core runs on either side; today's runtime counts JS allocations only in a RETROPLUG_PROFILE build\n");
    std::printf("%6s  %-20s %6s | %9s %9s %9s | %9s %9s %9s\n", "frames", "path", "blocks", "us/block", "%1-frame", "%own",
                "JS allocs", "JS bytes", "native");
    for (const std::uint32_t frames : kBlockSizes) {
        const KernelRows rows = timeKernel(frames);
        const int blocks = kernelBlocks(frames);
        for (const auto& [path, row] : {std::pair{"today's kernel stage", rows.today}, std::pair{"kernel node, plan", rows.node},
                                        std::pair{"plan, no kernel", rows.plan}}) {
            std::printf("%6u  %-20s %6d", frames, path, blocks);
            printTime(row.us, frames);
            printAllocations(row.allocations);
            std::printf("\n");
        }
        const auto count = [](std::uint64_t n) { return static_cast<unsigned long long>(n); };
        std::printf("%6s  node / today %.2f; the kernel node alone (node - plan) %.3f us; delivered in %llu blocks: %llu "
                    "serial-in, %llu MIDI, %llu bytes, %llu buttons\n",
                    "", rows.node.us / rows.today.us, rows.node.us - rows.plan.us, count(rows.blocks), count(rows.delivered.serialIn),
                    count(rows.delivered.midi), count(rows.delivered.bytes), count(rows.delivered.buttons));
    }
}

}  // namespace

TEST_CASE("a script node's cost per block, at 1, 64 and 512-frame blocks", "[.][bench]") {
    const auto start = Clock::now();
    std::printf("\nscript-node cost per block at %.1f kHz, %s build, medians of %d runs\n", kRate / 1000.0, kBuild, kRuns);
    std::printf("%%1-frame: the share of a 1-frame block's real time (%.1f us); %%own: of the row's own block's; allocations "
                "per block, native on the block thread\n",
                kBudgetUs);
    chainTable();
    kernelTable();
    std::printf("total %.2f s\n", usSince(start) / 1e6);
}
````

### Task 9: Delete the sealed kernel

Production documents have run the kernel script node since the flip, so everything only the old kernel path used
goes (design section 5.4). Two commits: first the profiling the DSP runtime did for the kernel stage (spec/08) moves
onto the script host, whose audio runtime runs the kernel node, so `dsp-bench` and `nes-bench` measure again under
a `RETROPLUG_PROFILE` host; then the deletion. Strict parity holds bit for bit through both.

**The profiling move.** Every RPC keeps its name (`dspAllocStats`, `dspResetAllocStats`, `dspRunGc`, `dspTraceReset`,
`dspTrace`, `dspTraceNames`). A profile build's audio allocator keeps the live heap and its peak; an allocation window
(`resetAllocStats`, which can pin auto-GC off) counts calls, bytes and the live-heap change, and per Engine block,
from `beginBlock` to a new `endBlock`, the block count and the worst block's allocations; `runGc` runs and times one
`JS_RunGC`. The trace window and its globals live in the script host, which binds them itself: every script node's
`process` is a `dsp-kernel` span holding `marshal` (the transport) and `js-call`, inside which each input the node
reads is a `marshal` span and the kernel's roles add theirs; `apu-render` starts where the last script node's
`process` ended, as it started after the kernel stage. The profile types are `rp::host`'s, in `ScriptHost.hpp`.

**The deletion.** Native: `DspRuntime` whole, the native kernel node and `rp.engine.kernel/1`,
`Engine::runKernelStage` and its fan-out, `loadKernel` / `setSystems`, `dspActive_`, both `Engine::cartSystemId`
overloads, the `SetSystems` and `LoadKernel` commands with the invoker's two producers, and `SystemTable`'s
`takesHostMidi` / `takesControllerMidi` with the "kernel gets no staged MIDI" rule: the engine now clears the
staging at every block's end, which is what a plan holding the input nodes leaves anyway. The host outputs move into
the engine (`EngineMidiOut`, `controllerOut_`). RPC: `compileScript`, `dspLoadKernel` and `dspSetSystems`, with
`registerDspKernelRpc`; the union is 87 methods. `ScriptCompiler` stays: the tests compile their toy nodes with it.
TS: `src/dspRuntime.ts`, `src/dspKernelBundle.ts`, the session's unused `dsp` client and its SDK declaration, and
the `__DSP_KERNEL_BUNDLE__` define with its last user, `test-native/dsp-runtime.test.ts`. Staged host MIDI becomes
allocation-free: each staging is a flat arena (message frames and offsets, one byte buffer), reserved at
construction for what the input nodes carry in a block, with two no-allocation cases, one through the ring.
`KernelNode.test.cpp` loses its "today" half: each case now holds the node to digests of what it sent (FNV-1a over
every block's frames, flags and bytes, per system and port, the tagged MIDI out, the control-surface out), recorded
from the tree in which the same cases still compared it to the old stage and found them equal; its behavioural checks
stay. The bench keeps its chain table and the kernel node's rows, today's numbers kept in its header. The specs'
links into the deleted files point at the script host; their narrative is Task 10's.

**Files:** 56 files, by step below.
- Delete: `packages/native/src/host/dsp/DspRuntime.cpp`, `packages/native/src/host/dsp/DspRuntime.hpp`, `packages/native/src/host/graph/KernelNode.cpp`, `packages/native/src/host/graph/KernelNode.hpp`, `packages/retroplug/src/dspKernelBundle.ts`, `packages/retroplug/src/dspRuntime.ts`, `packages/retroplug/test-native/dsp-runtime.test.ts`
- Modify: 49 files

````diff
+// ---- profiling (spec/08-profiling.md) ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+#ifdef RETROPLUG_PROFILE
+void ScriptHost::endBlock() {
+    const ScriptAllocations now = audioAllocations();
+    ++windowBlocks_;
+    maxBlockAllocs_ = std::max(maxBlockAllocs_, now.allocs - blockStart_.allocs);
+    maxBlockBytes_ = std::max(maxBlockBytes_, now.bytes - blockStart_.bytes);
+}
+
+DspAllocStats ScriptHost::allocStats() const {
+    const ScriptAllocations now = audioAllocations();
+    DspAllocStats s;
+    s.enabled = true;
+    s.allocCalls = now.allocs - windowStart_.allocs;
+    s.reallocCalls = now.reallocs - windowStart_.reallocs;
+    s.freeCalls = now.frees - windowStart_.frees;
+    s.allocBytes = now.bytes - windowStart_.bytes;
+    s.liveBytesDelta = counters_.liveBytes.load(std::memory_order_relaxed) - windowLiveBytes_;
+    s.peakBytes = counters_.peakBytes.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
+    s.blockCount = windowBlocks_;
+    s.maxBlockAllocCalls = maxBlockAllocs_;
+    s.maxBlockAllocBytes = maxBlockBytes_;
+    return s;
+}
+
+void ScriptHost::resetAllocStats(bool disableAutoGc) {
+    windowStart_ = audioAllocations();
+    windowLiveBytes_ = counters_.liveBytes.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
+    windowBlocks_ = maxBlockAllocs_ = maxBlockBytes_ = 0;
+    // QuickJS checks its threshold only as it makes an object, so SIZE_MAX means a collection never starts by itself.
+    if (disableAutoGc) JS_SetGCThreshold(audioRt_, static_cast<std::size_t>(-1));
+}
+
+DspGcResult ScriptHost::runGc() {
+    JS_UpdateStackTop(audioRt_);
+    const std::int64_t before = counters_.liveBytes.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
+    const auto t0 = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
+    JS_RunGC(audioRt_);
+    DspGcResult r;
+    r.enabled = true;
+    r.ms = std::chrono::duration<double, std::milli>(std::chrono::steady_clock::now() - t0).count();
+    r.freedBytes = before - counters_.liveBytes.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);  // the cycles collected
+    return r;
+}
+
+namespace {
+std::uint64_t steadyNs() {
+    return static_cast<std::uint64_t>(
+        std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::nanoseconds>(std::chrono::steady_clock::now().time_since_epoch()).count());
+}
+}  // namespace
+
+double ScriptHost::traceNow() const { return static_cast<double>(steadyNs() - traceStartNs_) / 1000.0; }
+
+void ScriptHost::spanBegin(std::uint32_t label) {
+    if (traceArmed_) traceStack_.emplace_back(label, traceNow());
+}
+
+void ScriptHost::spanEnd() {
+    if (!traceArmed_ || traceStack_.empty()) return;
+    const auto [label, t0] = traceStack_.back();
+    traceStack_.pop_back();
+    traceSpans_.push_back({label, t0, traceNow()});
+}
+
+void ScriptHost::spanSince(std::uint32_t label, double t0) {
+    if (traceArmed_) traceSpans_.push_back({label, t0, traceNow()});
+}
+
+void ScriptHost::traceName(std::uint32_t label, const std::string& name) {
+    if (traceNames_.size() <= label) traceNames_.resize(label + 1);
+    traceNames_[label] = name;
+}
+
+void ScriptHost::traceReset(bool arm) {
+    traceStack_.clear();
+    traceSpans_.clear();
+    traceStartNs_ = steadyNs();
+    lastProcessEnd_ = 0.0;
+    traceArmed_ = arm;
+}
+#else
+void          ScriptHost::endBlock() {}
+DspAllocStats ScriptHost::allocStats() const { return {}; }  // enabled false
+void          ScriptHost::resetAllocStats(bool) {}
+DspGcResult   ScriptHost::runGc() { return {}; }
+double        ScriptHost::traceNow() const { return 0.0; }
+void          ScriptHost::spanBegin(std::uint32_t) {}
+void          ScriptHost::spanEnd() {}
+void          ScriptHost::spanSince(std::uint32_t, double) {}
+void          ScriptHost::traceName(std::uint32_t, const std::string&) {}
+void          ScriptHost::traceReset(bool) {}
+#endif
+
 }  // namespace rp::host

+// ---- profiling the audio runtime (spec/08-profiling.md) ---------------------------------------------------------
+// Real only in a RETROPLUG_PROFILE build; in any other every field is 0 and `enabled` false. They cross the harness
+// RPCs (dspAllocStats, dspRunGc, dspTrace) as they are, so their field names are what packages/retroplug/src/
+// audioDriver.ts reads. "dsp" is the DSP (audio) thread, whose JS the script host's audio runtime runs.
+
+// The allocation window: what the audio runtime did since the last resetAllocStats(). `liveBytesDelta` is the net
+// change of its live heap (flat ~0: refcount churn; rising: a leak). The block counts are per Engine block, each
+// measured from its beginBlock to its endBlock, so a benchmark reads them once per window.
+struct DspAllocStats {
+    bool          enabled            = false;
+    std::uint64_t allocCalls         = 0;
+    std::uint64_t reallocCalls       = 0;
+    std::uint64_t freeCalls          = 0;
+    std::uint64_t allocBytes         = 0;   // asked for, by allocs and growing reallocs, in the window
+    std::int64_t  liveBytesDelta     = 0;   // usable bytes
+    std::uint64_t peakBytes          = 0;   // the live heap's all-time peak, usable bytes (informational)
+    std::uint64_t blockCount         = 0;
+    std::uint64_t maxBlockAllocCalls = 0;   // the worst single block (the tail)
+    std::uint64_t maxBlockAllocBytes = 0;
+};
+
+// One self-driven collection pass (JS_RunGC): `freedBytes` ~0 proves the runtime accumulates no reference cycles.
+struct DspGcResult {
+    bool         enabled    = false;
+    double       ms         = 0.0;
+    std::int64_t freedBytes = 0;
+};
+
+// One span of the trace window: `t0` and `t1` in microseconds from the window's start (traceReset), `label` an index
+// into traceNames().
+struct DspTraceSpan {
+    std::uint32_t label = 0;
+    double        t0    = 0.0;
+    double        t1    = 0.0;
````

- [ ] **Step 4: Commit the move**

````bash
git add -A -- packages/native/src/host/engine/Engine.cpp packages/native/src/host/engine/Engine.hpp packages/native/src/host/rpc/EngineRpcService.cpp packages/native/src/host/rpc/EngineRpcService.hpp packages/native/src/host/script/ScriptHost.cpp packages/native/src/host/script/ScriptHost.hpp packages/retroplug/src/audioDriver.ts packages/retroplug/src/script/kernelNode.ts packages/retroplug/test-native/dsp-bench.test.ts packages/retroplug/test-native/nes-bench.test.ts
git commit -F - <<'EOF'
refactor(engine): the script host profiles its audio runtime - the allocation window, the GC pass and the trace spans

The profiling the DSP runtime did for the kernel stage (spec/08-profiling.md), moved onto the script host, whose audio
runtime runs the kernel node since the flip; the native kernel path no plan runs is left for its own deletion. Every
RPC keeps its name (dspAllocStats, dspResetAllocStats, dspRunGc, dspTraceReset, dspTrace, dspTraceNames), and
dsp-bench and nes-bench measure again under a RETROPLUG_PROFILE host instead of skipping there.

- Allocation: a profile build's audio allocator keeps the live heap and its peak in usable bytes; an allocation window
  (resetAllocStats, which can pin auto-GC off) counts calls, bytes and the live-heap change, and per Engine block,
  from beginBlock to a new endBlock, the block count and the worst block's allocations. runGc runs and times one
  JS_RunGC there. The bytes are what QuickJS asked for, as the script host already counted them.
- Tracing: the trace window and the spanBegin / spanEnd / traceName / traceArmed globals of the audio context live in
  the script host, which binds them itself (the engine's binder goes). Every script node's process is a dsp-kernel span
  (the kernel node's, in every document TS builds), holding marshal (the block's transport) and js-call, inside which
  each input the node reads is a marshal span and the kernel's roles add theirs. apu-render now starts where the last
  script node's process ended and runs to the plan's end, as it started after the kernel stage; state-publish follows.
- The engine forwards the RPCs to the script host; the profile types (DspAllocStats, DspGcResult, DspTraceSpan, the
  span labels) are rp::host's, in ScriptHost.hpp.
EOF
````

````diff
-## `DspRuntime` + `ScriptCompiler`: the bare DSP kernel runner
-
-Native runs the TypeScript DSP role kernel but understands nothing about roles — it is "a
-dumb, role-agnostic runner … fed only by bytes." The kernel itself
-([`dspKernel.ts`](../packages/retroplug/src/dspKernel.ts)) and its behaviour are
-04's topic; this doc covers the C++ runner.
-
-[`DspRuntime`](../packages/native/src/host/dsp/DspRuntime.hpp#L28) owns a **second, bare
-QuickJS context** (no txiki — one of the two runtimes; see
-[01-architecture.md](01-architecture.md)), held by `Engine::dsp_`. The kernel bundle defines two
-globals when evaluated — `setSystems(json)` (the rarely-changing system structure, parsed once)
-and `processBlock(input)` (run one block) — and calls three bound C sink thunks as it runs, all
-**system-addressed** so one context drives every system
-([`DspRuntime.cpp`](../packages/native/src/host/dsp/DspRuntime.cpp)):
-
-| Thunk | Fills | Fanned to |
-|---|---|---|
-| [`pushSerialIn(system, frame, byte)`](../packages/native/src/host/dsp/DspRuntime.cpp#L17) | `serialIn_` | the addressed core's serial FIFO |
-| [`emitMidiOut(system, frame, [bytes])`](../packages/native/src/host/dsp/DspRuntime.cpp#L32) | `midiOut_` | the host (DAW) after the block |
-| [`pressButton(system, frame, button, down)`](../packages/native/src/host/dsp/DspRuntime.cpp#L60) | `buttonOut_` | the addressed core's joypad |
-
-**A `JSValue` never crosses out** — the runner reads back only these byte-addressed vectors,
-cleared at the top of each `processBlock`. The `DspRuntime` is set as the context opaque, so
-each thunk reaches its collector via `JS_GetContextOpaque`. The **drift-exact PPQ tick clock
-lives entirely in the JS kernel** (`walkTicks`) — native owns no `nextTick` / `eachTick`
-primitive; it only passes `BlockInfo { frames, sampleRate, tempo, ppqStart, transport }` in.
-
-`loadKernel` is `JS_ReadObject` + `JS_EvalFunction` on the bytecode, which runs the top-level
-code that defines the globals; re-loading hot-swaps the kernel. Every entry point re-anchors
-with [`JS_UpdateStackTop(rt_)`](../packages/native/src/host/dsp/DspRuntime.cpp#L102) because
-the driving thread differs (the control thread on the pull path, the audio thread while
-running), and QuickJS's stack-overflow guard is calibrated against the thread that created the
-runtime — without the re-anchor a call from a different stack throws a spurious overflow.
+## `ScriptHost` + `ScriptCompiler`: the script-node runtime
+
+Native runs the TypeScript DSP role kernel but understands nothing about roles. The kernel itself
+([`dspKernel.ts`](../packages/retroplug/src/dspKernel.ts)) and its behaviour are 04's topic; it
+runs as a script node ([`kernelNode.ts`](../packages/retroplug/src/script/kernelNode.ts)), and this
+doc covers the C++ runtime under it (docs/modular-graph-phase-b3a-design.md section 2).
+
+[`ScriptHost`](../packages/native/src/host/script/ScriptHost.hpp) owns **two bare QuickJS
+runtimes** (no txiki; see [01-architecture.md](01-architecture.md)), one per Engine, both loaded at
+construction with the script-node bundle embedded as bytecode
+([`bundle.ts`](../packages/retroplug/src/script/bundle.ts)): a control-side one that only validates
+settings and gives a node's ports, and the audio-side one that holds every instance and runs
+`process`. Each script type is an `rp_node_type` of the package `rp.script`, its instances native
+shims the planner creates and destroys like any node's. A node reads its inputs and writes its
+outputs through one reused `Block` object, straight from and into the plan's queues, so **a `JSValue`
+never crosses out**. The **drift-exact PPQ tick clock lives entirely in the JS kernel**
+(`walkTicks`); native passes only the block's transport in. Every entry into a runtime re-anchors
+with `JS_UpdateStackTop` because the driving thread differs (the control thread on the pull path,
+the audio thread while running), and QuickJS's stack-overflow guard is calibrated against the
+thread that last entered it. A profile build profiles the audio runtime there
+([08-profiling.md](08-profiling.md)).
 
 [`ScriptCompiler`](../packages/native/src/host/dsp/ScriptCompiler.hpp#L17) (`dsp::compileToBytecode`)
-compiles a script to QuickJS bytecode on a **transient, bare context — deliberately not the
-`DspRuntime`'s** — so the DSP side is proven never to re-parse source: bytecode is the only
-thing that crosses into the DSP heap. It backs the `compileScript` RPC. The bytecode is
-version-locked to this exact qjs-ng build, which is fine because the compiler and DSP contexts
-are the same `qjs`.
+compiles a script to QuickJS bytecode on a **transient, bare context**: the engine-graph tests use
+it to build their toy script nodes. The bytecode is version-locked to this exact qjs-ng build, which
+is fine because the compiler and the script host are the same `qjs`.

+## Running as a script node
+
+The kernel runs as the script node `rp.dsp.kernel`
+([kernelNode.ts](../packages/retroplug/src/script/kernelNode.ts), docs/modular-graph-phase-b3a-design.md
+section 4) inside the script host's **bare QuickJS audio context** (no txiki) on the audio thread,
+distinct from the control-plane runtime; see [01-architecture.md](01-architecture.md) for the
+two-runtimes model and [02-native-host.md](02-native-host.md) for the script host.
+
+**The bundle** ([script/bundle.ts](../packages/retroplug/src/script/bundle.ts)) is esbuilt to one
+IIFE, compiled to bytecode at build time and embedded in every native binary, so every Engine has the
+kernel node with no boot call. The node builds its **own** registry (**`dspRoles` only**: no core
+roles, no ROM providers).
+
+**Its settings** are the kernel's structure (`KernelStructure`, plus whether each system has a
+`serialOut`), and a structure change reshapes it: the instance is kept and `setSystems` keeps each
+surviving id's state. **Its ports** are per system, named by id: it reads `midiIn`, `controllerIn`,
+`controllerConnected` and each Game Boy's `serialOut` of last block, builds the kernel's `BlockInput`
+at the block-start ppq, and its `SinkTarget` sends each sink call on the addressed system's
+`serialIn` / `midi` / `bytes` / `buttons` output (wired to that system node's input of the same name),
+or on `midiOut` / `controllerOut` (to the host output nodes).
````
